events.long_description:
Paraparaumu Community Conversation #1
I’d love for you to join me in Paraparaumu on Saturday 15 August at 3pm at the Paraparaumu Memorial Hall for a community conversation about the future of our electorate and our country.

This event is an opportunity for you to hear a bit about who I am, why I’m standing, and what I believe our electorate deserves. But just as importantly, it’s a chance for me to hear directly from you about what matters most to you and your family.

We’ll talk about the issues shaping everyday life across Kapiti, from good local jobs and access to quality healthcare, to affordable homes and taking real action on the cost of living. This isn’t just about the election on November 7; it’s about how we build a just, thriving future for both our people and the planet.

Hope to see you there!

events.long_description:
Prophetiae Sibyllarum [Paraparaumu]
The Tudor Consort celebrates its 40th birthday in 2026 and we have an incredible season planned to celebrate. Collaborations with five different ensembles, a debut in Auckland, three premiere performances, and of course a performance of Thomas Tallis’ 40 part masterpiece Spem in alium. Make sure you visit our website to get all the details and secure your tickets!



We will be taking part in our third Aotearoa Festival of the Arts with SoundCathedral on Sunday March 1, an incredible re-composition of Orlande de Lassus’ Prophetiae Sibyllarum by Michael Norris, written especially for our anniversary and the 25th birthday of Stroma contemporary music ensemble. We celebrate going ‘over the hill’ in style in our May 2 concert XL, featuring two 40 part works by Tallis and Mäntyjärvi. We have two concerts with our friends Orchestra Wellington - Leonard Bernstein’s energetic Chichester Psalms as part of W:Ellington on 30 May, and Victoria Kelly’s brand new opera Ocean on 28 November. A debut in Auckland with NZ Barok sees us performing Lotti and Handel, and we finish the year with Messiah with Australian virtuoso harpsichordist and director Erin Helyard.




This is one of the most exciting seasons in our history, and I hope very much you can join us as we celebrate!

events.id: Come Together 2026--Wellington NZ
events.name: Come Together 2026
events.long_description:
New Zealand’s most successful rock series ever returns in 2026, focusing on an electrifying trio of landmark albums. Come Together is bringing three iconic albums to Wellington. This year, they take on Bruce Springsteen’s Born to Run, Radiohead’s OK Computer and Talking Heads’ Stop Making Sense. Each concert will faithfully recreate an album and follow up with a set of classics and deep cuts that span each artist’s catalogue. 
The group is made up of a rotating roster of Aotearoa’s most acclaimed rock musicians. What began as a bold celebration of legendary rock albums has since exploded into one of New Zealand’s most electrifying live concert experiences. The collective includes Jon Toogood, Tami Neilson, Liam Finn, Delaney Davidson, Reb Fountain, Julia Deans, Dianne Swann, Mel Parsons, Ed Knowles, Arahi, Jazmine Mary, Deva Mahal, and many more. Their endeavours have drawn thousands of fans, cementing Come Together as a must-see event on the music calendar.

events.id: The Dire Straits Experience-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: The Dire Straits Experience
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
From sold-out arena performances across Europe, the celebrated Dire Straits Experience now heads to Wellington. Personnel for the Long Highway World Tour has been assembled by Dire Straits veteran Chris White, who toured with the original band in the 90s. Prodigious singer-guitarist Terence Reis is also on board, adding further clout to the musical genius on stage.
Delving into Mark Knopfler’s platinum catalogue, this world-class ensemble reignites Dire Straits’ greatest hits with skill and showmanship. Hear classics like Money for Nothing, Walk of Life, So Far Away, Brothers in Arms, Sultans of Swing, Tunnel of Love, Telegraph Road, and plenty more. A seven-piece ensemble will take you on a two-hour odyssey with full concert production values.
Formed in London in 1977, Dire Straits was active until 1988 and then again from 1990 to 1995. Across six studio albums and five live albums, they have sold more than 120 million units worldwide.

events.venue: Various venues, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
It’s the ultimate cinematic experience. Your winter just got a whole lot warmer with a selection of over 150 feature films, short films, and documentaries — all courtesy of the New Zealand International Film Festival (NZIFF). 
It’s all lights, camera, and action when the annual NZIFF present 10 action-packed days of film in August. Artistic Director Paolo Bertolin and his team of film curators have scoured the world for independent, quirky, and award-winning movies. For 2026, this includes coming-of-age drama, a Mexican erotic thriller, campy animation, a Japanese exploration of grief, and a Kiwi mockumentary.
Now celebrating 58 years, the festival never fails to deliver a huge smorgasbord of films to choose from. Catch it at multiple venues across Wellington.

events.id: Circa Theatre Season 2026-Circa Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Circa Theatre Season 2026
events.venue: Circa Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Inside Circa Theatre’s waterfront venue, you’ll find two performance spaces. Both offer a smorgasbord of professional theatre throughout the year. Playwrights from international heavy hitters to brilliant Kiwi voices are represented. It also includes programming from comedies and cabarets to contemporary dance and pantomime. 
Before or after your show, visit the on-site café, brasserie and restaurant, Chouchou. It opens out onto a deck, where you can take in views across the harbour. Look up to admire the art installation above. Called ‘Velarium’, it undulates in the wind, mirroring the water in the harbour. 
Circa Theatre began its life in 1976. A breakaway group of actors and theatre practitioners decided that Aotearoa needed a new and innovative approach to theatre. Five decades later, it is still pushing boundaries, making people laugh and cry, and creating theatrical memories. 
If you don’t have your own Circa memory yet, there’s an opportunity to create one nearly every night of the week.

Torque Sounds are back!
Presenting our first Girls Torque here in Aotearoa. Celebrating the wāhine DJs of Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Expect quality selectors playing on the classic Torque Sounds rig that you've heard all over Pōneke and beyond.

The talent is undeniable, the ranks are deep, and the dancefloor belongs to everyone.This is not a nostalgia trip. It's a resurrection: same name, same energy, new city, new era!

M.CAP
Fortuna
Malware
Claire-voyant
Fluffcore

Each of the DJ's on this lineup have their names woven into the fabric of Wellington's club scene, each making waves in their own way;
• M.Cap is the founder of 'Nine Oh Nine' who facilitate girls & Femmes only DJ workshops.
• Fortuna is the founder of 'Fortunes' known for their deep/prog/melodic house & techno events.
• Malware is the Co-founder of Venom Events who focus on Techno events here in Pōneke.
• Claire-voyant is one of the founders of Torque Sounds and the original Girls Torque event back in London.
• Fluffcore is the Co-founder of TGF known for their dark techno events.
Come and kanikani to your hearts content amongst friends Saturday August 15th at Valhalla.

events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre
events.long_description:
Myths & Legends - Wellington
Arctic North meets Pacific South in a programme of heart-stirring Finnish works with conductor Pietari Inkinen and NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen.

Programme:
Sibelius Pohjola’s Daughter
Magnus Lindberg Violin Concerto No. 2 (NZ Premiere)
Sibelius Lemminkäinen Suite

Aotearoa New Zealand’s dramatic landscapes chime in kind with a country half a world away: Finland. In this concert, Arctic North meets Pacific South in a programme of heart-stirring Finnish works that resonate with audiences here.

Pietari Inkinen leads the Aotearoa New Zealand premiere of Finnish composer Magnus Lindberg’s Second Violin Concerto, with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen as soloist. This duo of Finnish talent are the perfect team to evoke the work’s “massive, expansive ... panoramic vista ... of dark clouds over forests and lakes, of repressed passions and baleful desires” (Financial Times).

We pair this contemporary Finnish masterpiece with a past master. Sibelius’ Pohjola’s Daughter and Lemminkäinen Suite were both inspired by the ancient epic the Kalevala. The latter describes the mythological adventures of the wizard Väinämöinen, the hero Lemminkäinen and their entanglement with the primordial forces of nature, death and magic.

Lisa and Wade are one of Aotearoa’s finest duos, with a rich and engaging sound. Together, they bring a chemistry that only comes from years of performing at the highest level. If you’re looking for a beautiful and unforgettable musical experience on a Saturday night, their blend of jazz and blues, contemporary pop and soul, and homegrown vibes is the perfect tonic.

events.name: Porirua Parkrun
events.venue: Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana
events.long_description:
What is Porirua parkrun? It is a free 5km walk or run event - It’s not about coming first or winning. You can go at your own pace and just enjoy being with other people. It is inclusive and the perfect way to start your weekend in the outdoors chatting to people.

The start occurs just upstream of the Bothamley Park carpark. This car park is off Champion street, opposite the intersection with Windley Street. Head to end of carpark where the concrete ends and there is a gate. For location see https://goo.gl/maps/wEohfp9bRu82.

The course is following the old coach road (circa 1870's) established for the early farms in the area. Today this historic track is located within a park, away from cars and now used by walkers, runners and cyclists.

The track is generally 3 metres wide with a gentle gradient and a compacted gravel surface beside the Kenepuru Stream through a picturesque wooded wild valley. (Note there is a pinch point for a short section after the 2km marker where participants need to go single file each direction for approx 30 metres)

The valley runs east-west with mature trees which means this has to be one of the most sheltered places, out of the wind to exercise in Wellington.

What does it cost to join in? Nothing - it's free! but please register before your first run or walk, so you can get your timing results. You only need to register with parkrun once, to participate at any of the parkrun events around the world. Don't forget to bring a copy of your barcode. If you forget it, you won't get a time.

How fast do I have to be? Walking is fine as long as you can finish the 5km. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

One dog per adult is welcome, as long as it is on a short hand held lead.

Children welcome but those 10 years and under need to be kept within arms reach of a supervising adult.

Note there is no toilets in the park, so go before you go.

We're friendly! Every week we grab a post park run/walk coffee/tea at Get Fixed within Kai Tahi at 20 Parumoana Street, to mix exercise with socialising.

There are volunteering opportunities even week. So those doing Duke of Edinburgh or similar challenges can get volunteer credits. Ensure you contact us well in advance at "porirua@parkrun.co.nz"

AWHI Yoga and Wellbeing’s accredited 200hr YTT program is a comprehensive and thorough journey into becoming a 200 hr certified Yoga Teacher. We are the only vinyasa yoga teacher training in the world that blends Te Ao Māori and ancient yoga wisdoms, offering a uniquely 'Aotearoa' experience while retaining universal relevance for teaching and practicing yoga in any part of the world.

Our training is suitable for individuals interested in becoming a yoga teacher, or those looking to take a personal journey towards deepening your own practice and knowledge. Either way, we guarantee a transformative and life-changing experience that will deepen your relationship to yoga, others, Aotearoa and your self.

Our uniquely Aotearoa Teacher Training explores the beautiful marriage between ancient Yoga and Te Ao Māori teachings over five separate modules during our three months together. Our course follows the Māori hauora/wellbeing model of Te Whare Tapa Whā, which takes the same holistic view of health taken by traditional Yoga. As we work through each pillar we start tapping into something way greater than ourselves, enabling us to connect with our purpose in life and how we might share this in service to the world!

A $1,000 deposit reserves your spot.

events.name: Sparkly Tapered Rings In Three
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Make a stunning heirloom-worthy ring over three sessions!

An excellent, fun class if you have already taken one of our Stacking Rings or Textured Earrings classes and fancy adding to your jewellery collection.

You will learn to create a tapered pattern for a ring to fit your finger. You will get to practice in copper or brass first then make your masterpiece in solid golden bronze. You will measure and cut the bronze, then apply a beautifully shiny, sparkly hammered finish using carefully polished hammers. Then you’ll be guided through soldering and forming up your tapered band, before carefully cleaning it up and applying the finishing touches to make this a ring that will be coveted for generations.

All materials supplied, optional upgrade to solid sterling silver - silver sheets in a range of thicknesses are available for purchase in the workshop.

*If you really love your bronze or brass ring and want to elevate it with a thin sterling silver liner, a 4 or 6 week block is ideal to take your piece to the next level.

Included in the class fee are copper for practising on, and sterling silver bar to create your twist ring and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but any person under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.venue: The Dowse Art MuseumLower Hutt, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview
A talk on Wayne Youle and his place in New Zealand art, given by Auckland Art Gallery's Nathan Pōhio.
The Dowse Art Museum invites audiences to a special floor talk with Nathan Pōhio on Sunday 16 August at 11am. Pōhio is Kaitiaki Matua, Toi Māori | Senior Curator, Māori Art at Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki.
In this illuminating discussion, Pōhio will situate Wayne Youle's practice within the broader landscape of New Zealand and Māori art. Pōhio will reflect on the humility, wit, conceptual rigour, themes and community engagement that define Youle’s art making to date, drawing on more than 20 years of watching him thrive as both an artist and a respected member of the Ōtautahi arts community.
The talk coincides with Wayne Youle: Back In Five, a major survey exhibition charting two decades of Youle’s practice.

events.id: Advanced Stone Setting: Stepped Bezel in 3 sessions-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Advanced Stone Setting: Stepped Bezel in 3 sessions
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
This workshop is ideal for intermediate-advanced students who have already learned basic soldering and how to bezel set cabochon stones.

A stepped bezel is a beautiful way to set faceted stones, creating a clean, elevated frame that both protects and highlights the gem. In our three-part Stepped Bezel Setting Class, students will learn the complete process of designing and fabricating stepped bezels using sparkling cubic zirconias in copper.

Designed for jewellers looking to refine their fabrication and setting skills, this hands-on workshop explores how to create clean, professional stepped bezels for faceted stones. Students will learn techniques for measuring, constructing, soldering, and setting with accuracy, while gaining a deeper understanding of stone fit and bezel design.

This is a technique class where you will learn techniques to practice in your own time or in regular block classes.

This class will run over 3 separate 3hr sessions and is working towards creating a simple band ring with a stepped bezel.

Session 1 will cover the technique, demonstrations and the basics of measuring and preparing the setting. Students will design their piece and begin the construction.

Session 2 will pick up on the setting techniques, reminding and refining essential steps in the process. Students can expect to be soldering in this class.

Session 3: Troubleshooting can be covered in this class, as well as learning to clean up the settings. Students may begin a second setting that they can continue in their own time.

We will be working in copper for this class ( silver is available for purchase, but we recommend making your first project in copper first). Students should expect to have at least one completed set project and possibly some other practice pieces begun by the end of the three classes.

What is provided: class fees cover your practice metal (copper) and stones (CZ) and detailed handouts that are useful for you to take away to refer to when practicing and honing your skills.

Experience Stonehenge Aotearoa at its most breathtaking — as the sun dips below the Wairarapa horizon.
Our Sunset Guided Tour blends astronomy, storytelling, and the natural beauty of twilight for an evening you will never forget.

Led by one of our knowledgeable guides, this 90-minute experience explores how ancient cultures used the Sun to track time and mark the turning of the seasons. You’ll discover the scientific and cultural thinking behind the Henge’s unique Southern Hemisphere design before watching the sunset alignment from inside the stone circle.

Weather permitting, you’ll witness how the setting Sun interacts with the structure — a striking moment that links ancient knowledge with the rhythms of the natural world.

Duration and Schedule
• Allow: Approximately 90 minutes
• Start Time: Begins one hour before sunset
• Availability: Offered any day with advance booking

Coalitions crumble, loyalties burn, Winston probably survives another term somehow and the nation faces a meltdown it really didn’t vote for.

Irreverent and rowdy, PSA delivers up-to-the-minute raucous political comedy and features Pōneke’s funniest performers.

Public Service Announcements began as a late night comedy experiment in 2011, created by James Nokise and Anya Tate-Manning. Over the last 5 election cycles we have created 19 original productions at BATs and Circa Theatre, and over 100 artists have worked on PSA across the last 15 years.

PSA balances smart and stupid; inside political gags and fart jokes, a ruthless investigation of leaders and election promises, but most importantly side-splitting, pants-wetting comedy.

This time Carrie Green takes the wheel as Director, and we have an all-star line-up of hilarious Wellington performers, and a team of razor sharp writers and designers.

events.long_description:
WHAC Presents: Honest 10 on Sunday 16 August 2026

Hi all.
Join us at 8:30am on the Sunday of 16th August 2026 for a 5k or 10k run/walk over a flat course taking in Wellington's beautiful waterfront. It's a great chance to test your 5km or 10km fitness and maybe have a go at walking or running PB.
Check out other dates as well as photos and results on the WHAC website https://whac.org.nz/wp/honest-10/

Other dates for 2026:
Sun 20 September
Sun 18 October
Sun 15 November
Sun 20 December

EVERYONE IS WELCOME NO MATTER WHAT YOUR LEVEL OF FITNESS. The is an optional 8:15am early start for those who think they might need more time (eg over 70 mins for 10k). Let us know when you sign up if you might want this option.
[Note: If there are gales force winds, it is likely we will cancel due to safety reasons. Check back on this FB page at 7am on the morning of the race if the wind is howling as well will post any cancellation by that time. If nothing is here, then the event is going ahead :) ]

Organised by WHAC, the Honest 10 provides a fast, fun and friendly environment. The race course has been officially measured and there will be pacers running 40min, 45min, 50min, 55min and 60min to help you run your best.

Cost: Just $10 for 10km, $5 for 5km!!

How to enter:
1. Pre-register by email (recommended) BEFORE 5PM on Saturday 15 August (payments methods for pre-registrations include online bank transfer (an email with your reference will be sent back to you) or pay cash on the day.
Account Name: Wellington Harrier Athletic Club
Account Number: 12-3493-0058553-00
Use "H10 [your race number]" as your reference. Eg "H10 #23"
OR
2. Sign up on the day from 8am (cash only).

Photos are free of charge and posted online (on the WHAC website) alongside results after the race. https://whac.org.nz/wp/honest-10/

Where: At the Whale's Tail next to Freyberg Pool, Oriental Bay

When: Registration from 8am. Race starts at 8:30am Sunday morning. Let us know when you register, if you request an early 8.15am start, eg if you are walking the 10km or are likely to run slower than 70mins.

***Pre-registration details***
Email the following details to BEFORE 5pm Saturday 15 Aug🙂 You will receive a confirmation email back with your race number. If you select 'N' for prepaid, just bring cash to the race with you. If you select 'Y' for prepaid, pay via WHAC's bank account details below.
- Name
- Age
- 5km or 10km
- M, F or D (unfortunately we are currently unable to give age-calculated results for the gender-diverse (D) category, as our source currently only provides age-calculated result data for M and F)
- Phone number
- Prepay Y or N

BANK ACCOUNT DETAILS If you select "Y" for Prepay when you register via email, transfer your $10 entry fee (or $5 for 5k) to
Account Name: Wellington Harrier Athletic Club
Account Number: 12-3493-0058553-00
using "H10 [your race number]" as your reference. Eg "H10 #23"

Looking forward to seeing you on Sunday 16 August

events.long_description: How did Wellington become a culinary paradise? Capital of Kai tells the story through 100 years of Wellington's food creatives, restaurant workers, and café culture. It's a love letter to the hospo whānau who have shaped the city. Walk through galleries of heritage treasures: the Green Parrot's working griddle, Hiakai's light-up signage, Il Casino's couch, Shanghai restaurant's 1980s menu, the Matterhorn café's cowbell. You'll see the arc from 1930s British hotel dining (roast mutton, boiled vegetables, milky tea) through European influences brought home by migrants and travellers, and the diverse cuisines - Chinese, Malaysian, Indian, Syrian, Greek, Māori - that define Wellington now. Hungry for more? Feed your curiosity at Capital of Kai.

events.long_description:
Unwrapped: Whittaker’s since 1896 invites Chocolate Lovers behind the scenes to discover how a local maker became a global name. Set within the wider history of cacao production, the exhibition traces Whittaker’s story—from J.H. Whittaker’s founding vision and the iconic products that followed through to the company’s ongoing commitment to quality, beans-to-bar manufacturing and ‘Good Honest Chocolate’ values.

The exhibition unwraps the story of New Zealand’s Most Trusted Brand and features objects to delight all the senses. Visitors will encounter nostalgic memorabilia and classic advertising, a scent station that reveals chocolate’s layered aromas and artworks made in collaboration with contemporary creatives.

2026 marks 130 years of Whittaker’s. What began as J.H. Whittaker’s small family business in 1896 has grown into a world-class chocolate manufacturer, still proudly family-owned four generations on and based in its original Porirua factory.

events.name: Next Gen Cook Off
events.venue: LTD., Level 1, 60 Dixon Street
events.long_description:
The first four Mondays in August, an up-and-coming chef takes over the Everybody Eats kitchen at LTD and delivers a three-course dinner built from rescued food, cooking it their way and style. Walk in, take a seat, and let the Everybody Eats volunteers whānau take care of the rest. No bookings. Pay what you can. 
Sixth year running, and the model stays simple: good food, good company, and a room full of people making a difference one plate at a time. Every course uses rescued ingredients, because eating is fundamental and everyone deserves access to something . 

3 August — Oscar Little, Hummingbird
Oscar Little started his culinary career five years ago as a commis chef at Shed 5 and The Crabshack, where he learned what it means to commit to a team. He’s since worked his way up to chef de partie at Hummingbird. Along the way he’s volunteered with Everybody Eats, and it’s that spirit of giving back to the community that drives him to compete this year.

10 August — Brayden Puketapu, Koji
At 22, Brayden Puketapu is already developing a cooking voice that’s distinctly his own. Working at Koji, he’s drawn to the creative challenge of transforming overlooked ingredients and putting his own stamp on both classic and contemporary dishes. His heritage is central to that identity, grounding his food in something personal while keeping it fresh and inventive.

17 August — Eugenous Evan, Rosella
Indonesian-born Eugenous Evan came to Wellington five years ago and hasn’t looked back. After stints at Shepherd, Hillside & Daisy’s, and Supra, he’s now chef de partie at Rosella, where he’s been for just over a year. For Eugenous, cooking is an act of care: a way to share something of himself with every person who sits down to eat.

24 August — Aryan Dhankhhar, Mosaic Venues (Mr Go's, Kisa, Ombra, Parla)
Aryan Dhankhhar’s love of food started young, holding weekend cooking competitions with his sister and himself in their family kitchen in Haryana, India, with their mother as judge. Since then he’s built a career spanning hotels, restaurants, and catering, working across techniques from sous vide to traditional barbecue. A highlight: leading the team at Wilson Barbecue during Wellington On a Plate 2024, where they set a world record selling over 6,000 burgers in a single day. Now at Mr Go’s, he brings that same drive and precision to every plate.

Next Gen Cook Off is proudly supported by The Gas Hub.

Business Continuity Planning
This practical Business Continuity Planning workshop helps small and medium-sized businesses prepare for disruption before it happens.

About this Event

Could your business keep operating if something unexpected happened tomorrow?
Disruptions don’t wait until you’re ready. Severe weather, supplier delays, cyber incidents, key staff absence, power outages, cash flow pressure or system failures can all stop normal operations fast.
This practical workshop will help you understand what a Business Continuity Plan is, why it matters, and how to start building one that works for your business.
You’ll learn how to identify your most critical business activities, understand the risks that could interrupt them, and put simple steps in place to keep operating, recover faster and communicate clearly when things go wrong.
What you’ll walk away with
A clear understanding of what a Business Continuity Plan should include
A practical framework to assess, prepare, respond and review
Tools to identify your critical processes, dependencies and recovery priorities
Simple steps to strengthen your business resilience over 30, 60 and 90 days
Confidence to start your plan without waiting for it to be perfect
Who should attend
This workshop is designed for New Zealand small and medium-sized business owners, managers and decision-makers who want to be better prepared for disruption.
Why attend
Because a simple plan started today could make all the difference when disruption arrives tomorrow.

events.name: Introduction to Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Workshop - August 2026
events.venue: Naumi Hotel, 213 Cuba Street, Wellington, New ZealandWellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview




A 2-day introductory, experiential ACT workshop for clinicians.
Over 1000 randomised control trials have clearly demonstrated ACT’s efficacy for a wide range of diagnoses and life problems. ACT helps people make space for their thoughts and feelings while moving towards the life they value. At this experiential workshop you will establish a foundational understanding of Psychological Flexibility, develop skills for using ACT and learn about Relational Frame Theory (RFT).
Over the two days you will learn how to:
meet clients where they are and foster their willingness to change
help clients hold their painful thoughts and emotions gently; identify and actively move towards their values; and develop awareness of the present moment and their capacity to notice it
develop a therapeutic relationship in which support can be provided compassionately and flexibly
formulate life struggles from an ACT perspective
practice ACT exercises and relate the concepts back to your own life and clinical experiences.
This workshop is fully catered with vegetarian food.
Giselle Bahr and Ben Sedley are clinical psychologists and co-founders of ACT Wellington. Since being trained and supervised by many of the world’s leading ACT therapists and researchers, ACT has been the foundation of their practices for many years. Giselle and Ben have both worked at Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services, in Private Practice with adults and adolescents, and trained clinical psychology students at Victoria University of Wellington. Giselle has developed and facilitated groups introducing ACT to parents and adults, and served on the Board of ANZ ACBS. Ben wrote Stuff That Sucks: Accepting what you can’t change and committing to what you can, Holding the Heavy Stuff: making space for critical thoughts and painful emotions, and Stuff That’s Loud: A teen’s guide to unspiralling when OCD gets noisy (with Lisa Coyne). He is also an ACBS Peer Reviewed ACT Trainer.


QUESTIONS AND MORE INFORMATION

Please get in touch if you have any questions about this training. You can email us at:
training@actwellington.co.nz

Can I have a GST Receipt?
If your employer requires a GST receipt from you, please email us and we will send you one.

A refund is available until 30 days before the workshop. This includes all costs except for the eventbrite nonrefundable fee.
A 50% refund is available until 14 days before the workshop.
From 14 days before the workshop, your ticket is non-refundable but fully transferrable. To transfer your ticket to another attendee contact us with the new details.
Full refunds will be made if the event cannot proceed due to Covid19 restrictions, or attendees are unable to travel to the event due to Covid19 restrictions.

events.name: Rivers of Nihil
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Pennsylvanias progressive death metal progenitors Rivers of Nihil make their first voyage to Aotearoa New Zealand.

The quartets musicianship has been honed to a fine point thanks to an unrelenting touring schedule over the past few years, including headline tours of the U.S. and EU/UK, as well as touring with Cattle Decapitation, Carnifex, Lorna Shore, Between the Buried and Me, and touring with titans of progressive death metal Cynic, Beyond Creation, and Dååth.

Life on the road for Rivers is a treat for fans and band members alike. For the most part, its very mellow, with a lot of laughs and a lot of ball-busting. Andy (Guitar, Vocals), and I have been friends for over 15 years, and Jared (Drums) has been in the fold since 2017 says founding member/guitarist Brody Uttley. Founding bassist Adam Biggs became the bands new lead vocalist/bassist in 2023, which upped the ante and led to the release of self-titled album Rivers of Nihil (2025). Traditionally, a self-titled record can signal a return to basics and/or a fresh beginning, and in 10 powerful songs, its clear that both those factors are in play. I feel like these songs are the perfect blend of all our albums, with all the fat cut away, says Uttley.

River of Nihil have riffs, big choruses, the prog, the solos, the sax and now it will have Aotearoa New Zealand

events.long_description:
AR Monthly Concert - Laldy and Owen Hugh
Laldy; Wellington-based fiddle player Rachel James and guitarist Donald James combine forces for one mission: to play folk and “gie i' laldy”, meaning to do something with gusto or great enthusiasm. With Welsh and Scottish roots, they are inspired by Scottish, Irish and Scandinavian music traditions.
Laldy brings to the stage a set which weaves together contemporary and traditional folk tunes and songs with original writing and arrangement. Playing a selection of sweet songs, modal grooves and traditional bangers, Laldy are a lively and danceable offering to the New Zealand folk and festival scene.
Owen Hugh - has been writing songs since he was 16 though it
took him 3 years of trying before writing a decent one. He has just remastered all his albums and they are available on sites such as YouTube, Spotify and Apple music. His music always touches the soul and contains Celtic, Rock Folk and Blues influences. He cut his teeth at folk clubs in NZ and the UK in the 90’s and has played Edinburgh Fringe Festival 4 yrs in a row as well as several festivals in UK. Once described in the American Press as a cross between “Billy Connolly and James Taylor”, be prepared to laugh and cry possibly at the same time. After a period of writer’s block he is now recording and road-testing new material.
Entry: $20/$15 for members. Cash only (no eftpos facilities). Note: The concert will be on the first floor, with access via stairs or the lift. (Yes, the lift is back in action!) You may have to press the button at the side of the door to gain access to the building.

events.venue: Te Herenga Waka Marae, 46 Kelburn Parade, Wellington
events.long_description:
Ngā Mokopuna: A Living Building Story Tour

Join us for an introductory guided tour of Ngā Mokopuna, Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington's pioneering regenerative building project.

This experience explores the vision, values, and aspirations behind a building designed to tread lightly on the environment while creating lasting benefits for people and place. Grounded in principles of kaitiakitanga and inspired by mātauranga Māori, Ngā Mokopuna reflects a commitment to caring for our natural world and future generations.

During the tour, you'll learn about the Living Building Challenge, one of the world's most ambitious sustainability frameworks, and discover how Ngā Mokopuna has been designed to meet its rigorous standards. The project represents a significant step towards becoming one of Aotearoa New Zealand's next recognised Living Buildings.

From outside the building and surrounding precinct, you'll hear the stories behind its design, sustainability features, and cultural foundations. You'll also meet staff and student ambassadors who work and study within Ngā Mokopuna and learn firsthand how the building supports teaching, learning, wellbeing, and community.

The tour also provides an opportunity to view Te Tumu Herenga Waka Marae and hear how the marae and Ngā Mokopuna together express values of sustainability, kaitiakitanga, belonging, and connection.

Whether you're interested in sustainable design, Māori worldviews, education, architecture, or the future of the built environment, this tour offers a unique insight into a project that seeks to demonstrate what regenerative design can achieve.

Come and discover how sustainability and kaitiakitanga are being brought to life at Ngā Mokopuna.

events.name: 9 week Yoga Beginners Course
events.venue: Yoga in Daily Life Centre, 23 Jessie St, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
The Beginners Course teaches the “Sarva Hitta Asanas” from Level 1 - postures that are good for everyone. The Course covers all the foundations you need for an ongoing yoga practice as well as plenty of time for guided relaxation. Loosening your body, joints, and mind, the exercises are designed for complete balance and the awakening of energy in body, mind, and soul. Experience yoga postures, breath techniques, meditation and relaxation, along with knowledge about basic yoga philosophy and a healthy lifestyle. A wonderful course for new beginners and those looking to deepen their practical experience of yoga.

Some of the many benefits of yoga include: improvement in posture and breathing, increased strength and flexibility, a greater ability to cope with stress, and a feeling of peace and calm.

This course called "part 1" will cover the second half of Level 1 from the System of Yoga in Daily Life.

events.long_description:

Explore how understanding your inner drives can lead to greater freedom, clarity and self-mastery.
Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars:
Befriending Desire, Anger and Greed

We often try to suppress or fight our strongest inner impulses, only to find they grow stronger in the background. This workshop explores how to understand, work with, and transform these powerful forces into clarity and strength. Discover how true freedom begins not with repression, but with knowledge and inner skill.

Please note our events now start at 6pm. Please try to be on time.
End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host: Hriman

Hriman is Wellington’s own home grown monk for over two decades, drawing on his background in philosophy, the arts, and contextual studies to his work. He shares his realisations and insights through travel, writing, and dynamic presentations that foster clarity, reflection, and growth.

events.venue: Massey University Theatrette, Block 10 (Old Museum Building), Buckle Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
The Music Managers Forum Aotearoa (MMF) is proud to announce FOUNDATIONS, a refreshed evolution of its long running Back to Basics seminar series. Presented in collaboration with Ka Korokī Ka Maranga | Māori Music Industry Collective, FOUNDATIONS is a free two hour workshop for artists and self managers in the early stages of building a music career.

For this session, we will be joined by Mikee Carpenter (Manager - Georgia Lines) and AJA (Artist)

SECURE YOUR SPOT HERE: https://www.mmf.co.nz/news-pages/2026/7/16/vgjzb0thbu20b6fey3l2uvqk9ihm51

FOUNDATIONS was born out of a moment of reflection for MMF. With the loss of long time Back to Basics presenter Lorraine Barry in 2025, the team felt it was the right time to relook at the programme she had shaped for so many years. Lorraine was a dedicated advocate for emerging artists and managers, and FOUNDATIONS carries her commitment to helping the next generation navigate the industry with confidence.

The workshop covers the building blocks every artist needs from day one, including the NZ music ecosystem and funding pathways, rights and royalties, finding and growing a real fanbase, releasing music with a team around you, understanding the business side of the industry, patience in building a career, and the financial realities of a life in music. Each section is followed by open Q&A, giving attendees the chance to bring their own questions to experienced guests.

“Lorraine Barry was a mentor to me for over eight years and someone I always turned to for advice, as well as being a great friend. It’s an honour to carry on the work she was so passionate about in artist development, on behalf of the MMF.” - Mikee Carpinter

events.id: Thriving As a Nation of Readers: Strengthening Reading Communities-National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Thriving As a Nation of Readers: Strengthening Reading Communities
events.venue: National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington
events.long_description:
As part of NZ Children’s Book Week 2026, Te Awhi Rito Reading Ambassador Kate De Goldi will chair a Panel session on why reading for pleasure matters and why strengthening our school reading communities is so important.

Having the skill to read is much more powerful when it’s paired with the will to read. Reading for pleasure is the foundation for full literacy. It builds vocabulary, knowledge, critical thinking and imaginative power.

It also develops an understanding of self and others and contributes to wellbeing. However, in Aotearoa New Zealand there is a steady decline in the numbers of young people reading for pleasure.

Join us at this free event where the panel will explore the current reading landscape. They will discuss the ways schools, libraries, families and whānau, and other organisations can collaborate to build reading communities that support and inspire life-long reading for pleasure.

The event is for educators, librarians, researchers, and anyone interested in engaging young readers.

events.id: RIVERS OF NIHIL - NZ TOUR-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
events.name: RIVERS OF NIHIL - NZ TOUR
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Pennsylvanias progressive death metal progenitors Rivers of Nihil make their first voyage to Aotearoa New Zealand.
The quartets musicianship has been honed to a fine point thanks to an unrelenting touring schedule over the past few years, including headline tours of the U.S. and EU/UK, as well as touring with Cattle Decapitation, Carnifex, Lorna Shore, Between the Buried and Me, and touring with titans of progressive death metal Cynic, Beyond Creation, and Dååth.
Life on the road for Rivers is a treat for fans and band members alike. For the most part, its very mellow, with a lot of laughs and a lot of ball-busting. Andy (Guitar, Vocals), and I have been friends for over 15 years, and Jared (Drums) has been in the fold since 2017 says founding member/guitarist Brody Uttley. Founding bassist Adam Biggs became the bands new lead vocalist/bassist in 2023, which upped the ante and led to the release of self-titled album Rivers of Nihil (2025). Traditionally, a self-titled record can signal a return to basics and/or a fresh beginning, and in 10 powerful songs, its clear that both those factors are in play. I feel like these songs are the perfect blend of all our albums, with all the fat cut away, says Uttley.
River of Nihil have riffs, big choruses, the prog, the solos, the sax and now it will have Aotearoa New Zealand

events.name: Winter’s Saga
events.venue: Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join us this winter as our community cast brings fireside tales of Norse mythology to life. Blending contemporary dance and physical theatre, Winter’s Saga follows the legendary paths of Loki, Odin and Thor beneath the branches of mighty Yggdrasil. Battles will rage, heroes will rise and fall, and the worlds of gods and mortals will collide in an epic live performance event.
Choreographed by Kate Avery, James Burchell, Joana Joy, Trinity Maydon and Hanna Hairil with support from Sacha Copland
Costume design by Ella Malcolm
Lighting and sound design by Lucas Zaner
Set design by Miho Aragane
Props design by Sherise Ho
Featuring original music by Anna McBride
Produced by Shereen Capper
Winter's Saga is brought to you by Wellington Community Ballet Theatre - a group of community dancers and performers staging dance theatre productions. The company supports emerging choreographers and freelance artists as well as creating opportunities for the community to dance on stage.
The company premiered its first production, "Four Questions" at the New Zealand Fringe Festival in March 2026 to near sold-out audiences. It was nominated for "most promising emerging company" at the Fringe Festival. The audience said: "What a great show! Loved it!"; "It was really lovely to see people truly enjoying dance. I hope to see more like that."; "I really enjoyed it. I heard it's the first performance of the company, which is really impressive, it was super well put together." Winter's Saga will be Wellington Community Ballet Theatre's second production.
Content warning: This production contains flashing lights. It includes depictions of physical violence and death. Parent discretion is advised.

events.id: Pub Choir — Just Think About It-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Pub Choir — Just Think About It
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
You’ll definitely feel better if you come and have a sing with a few thousand strangers. That’s what New Zealand-born vocalist, conductor, and composer Astrid Jorgensen thinks. Astrid is the brainchild behind the touring show Pub Choir — Just Think About It. The premise is simple — come to the Michael Fowler Centre on 19 August and learn one popular song in three-part harmony. What began as a small gathering in a pub has now grown to fill concert halls around the world. No prior training is required — just bring your voice and a sense of humour. 
Astrid established Pub Choir in Brisbane in 2017. Her work associated with the show has gone on to win her several awards. This includes one of the 40 Under 40 Most Influential Asian-Australians by the Asian-Australian Leadership Summit in 2021 and a Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) in 2023.

events.id: Crying Tiger-Tuk Tuk Thai Kitchen, 15 Hartham Place North-WOAP
events.name: Crying Tiger
events.venue: Tuk Tuk Thai Kitchen, 15 Hartham Place North
events.long_description:
Charcoal smoke, sizzling meat, and you're in Nong Khai, a small northeast Thai town where families gather around the grill for Crying Tiger steak. Beef steak marinated 48 hours in coriander root, garlic, black pepper, oyster sauce, palm sugar, whiskey, and mandarin juice, char-grilled until the meat weeps with its own juices.
The chef grew up cooking this dish with family and friends. It arrives with sticky rice and a Northern Thai Isarn dipping sauce of tamarind, lime juice, ground chillies, and fresh coriander. Alongside: a sharp granny smith apple salad dressed with chilli and fish sauce, topped with prawns; and tom zapp, slow-cooked pork soft bones that melt into a soup fragrant with kaffir lime, lemongrass, and ground rice.
This is a three course set menu for $75.  Alcohol can be purchased separately.  Minimum 2 orders per table.

events.id: Entre Calles-Cuba Street Tavern, 172 Cuba Street-WOAP
events.name: Entre Calles
events.venue: Cuba Street Tavern, 172 Cuba Street
events.long_description:
Cuba Street Tavern owner Rich spent eight trips wandering Barcelona's backstreets, finding treasured and memorable venues, not because they were advertised but because someone leaned in and said, "trust me, you need to try this place". Entre Calles recreates that feeling through shared tapas, Spanish-inspired drinks and music. 

Tapas arrive in waves across shared tables while DJs spin Spanish tracks. Nobody's ordering from a menu, plates just come, each one designed for passing and picking at, the kind of eating where the conversation flows as easily as the Spanish-inspired drinks. Expect pinchos that hit hard, dishes that layer and surprise, and the feeling of being somewhere because someone recommended it rather than because you planned. It's tight, vibey, and a little chaotic in the best possible way. 

Your ticket includes eight courses of shared tapas and three paired Spanish-inspired drinks.

events.name: Dinner With Dionysus
events.venue: Noble Rot Wine Bar, 6 Swan Lane
events.long_description:
For this five-course degustation, Head Chef Nicolas Mentzas draws on his Greek heritage to present the flavours and textures of home through a refined, fine-dining lens. Often perceived as relaxed and informal, there is a quiet depth to Greek cuisine. It is shaped by season, coastline, mountain herbs, and generations gathered around the table.
Dinner unfolds as a carefully composed menu that honours tradition while embracing precision in one of the world’s oldest wine cultures. Rather than a shared feast, expect elevated dishes rooted in Greek culinary history, reinterpreted with elegance and detail. Each course is paired with Greek wines, highlighting distinctive indigenous grape varieties and the growing confidence of the country’s modern producers.
Throughout the evening, the Noble Rot sommelier team will introduce each pairing, exploring how Greece’s food and wine traditions complement one another in perfect harmony, at the highest level.
Your ticket includes an amuse bouche on arrival, five courses, an arrival wine, and seven Greek wines paired throughout the evening.

Description
This course provides a pragmatic introduction to key business analysis concepts and the business analyst role. It includes a number of hands-on exercises to apply what you learn. It is targeted at those who are new to Business Analyst roles or considering moving into this profession. The course is also highly suitable to subject matter experts, business representatives, and project roles that involve business analysis activities.
Business analysis is a broad and exciting profession and skill set. Your role is to understand businesses, their needs and their problems and then help assess and validate solutions to fulfil these needs or solve these problems. In the process you will be involved in a wide range of activities including analysis, requirements management, communication, solution assessment and validation, and planning.

events.long_description:
Overview




Join RIVAL Wealth for a small, interactive session exploring the rise of AI and what it could mean for your investments.
Artificial intelligence is changing how businesses operate, how markets move, and where capital is being invested, so what does that actually mean for your investments in practice?
This session steps away from the headlines and focuses on the practical side of investing in a world shaped by AI. Matt Logan, a Portfolio Manager at Fisher Funds, will walk through how AI is influencing portfolios today, and where we are seeing real impacts in markets and investment decisions. With almost 20 years' experience at Fisher Funds, Matt is a senior member of the investment team and brings extensive experience analysing markets, managing risk and identifying investment opportunities.
He will cover:
• How AI is affecting global markets and investment returns
• Where opportunities may sit, and where risks are building
• How your KiwiSaver or investment portfolio may already have exposure
• What a considered, long-term approach looks like in this environment
This is an opportunity to ask questions and understand how this fits into your wider financial plan, and what it may mean for your own situation.
A light lunch and refreshments will be provided.
You are welcome to arrive from 11.30am for a coffee and a chat, with the presentation starting at 12.00pm. If you are joining us for your lunch break, feel free to arrive closer to the start time. We will be in the Te Papa Noho room at the BNZ Partners Centre, Wellington.
We are keeping this session small, so we recommend registering early to secure your place.
Parking is available at Stout Street, Wellington and Queens Warf Waterfront parking, both a short walk to the BNZ Partners Centre.

events.name: Google Gemini Academy: Educator Roadshow (Wellington)
events.venue: Wellington CollegeWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview
Join us for our annual edu roadshow! Join Steve (Google) & Jack (Fusion) to learn AI basics, prompting & responsible use in the classroom.
What to expect
This half-day workshop gives you a practical introduction to Google Gemini and generative AI in education, delivered by Steve from Google and Jack from Fusion Networks.
You'll leave with the skills and confidence to use AI in your classroom and admin work, and you'll sit the Google Certified Gemini Educator exam right there in the session, no pressure, no separate booking.
Who it's for
Teachers, school leaders, and support staff who want practical, hands-on AI skills. No technical background needed.
What you'll learn
Understanding Gemini and generative AI
What generative AI is and how it's different from other tech
How Gemini fits into tools you already use, like Docs, Gmail, and Classroom
Where AI can genuinely save you time (planning, grading, feedback, communication)
Using Gemini in your day-to-day practice
Writing prompts that actually get you useful results
Creating quizzes, lesson outlines, and rubrics with Gemini
Building your own "Gem" for repeat classroom tasks, like bell-ringers or feedback frames
Drafting emails and staff communications faster
Using AI responsibly
Spotting bias, errors, and "hallucinations" in AI output
Talking to students about plagiarism and responsible AI use
Building your own classroom guidelines for AI
Sit your certification exam on the day
At the end of the session, you'll sit the Google Certified Gemini Educator exam in a relaxed, supported environment, straight after covering everything you need to know. No exam anxiety, no need to book or study separately later.
Format
Half-day, hands-on session. Bring a laptop and your Google Workspace login.

Secure your seat for the 2026 New Zealand Book Awards for Children and Young Adults and join the celebration of the best books of the year for young New Zealand readers. Meet this year’s finalists and be there as the winners are revealed at an exuberant awards ceremony at Pipitea Marae on Wednesday 19 August.

Forty-four gifted children’s writers, illustrators and translators are finalists in this year’s awards. Their achievements will be honoured on the night by publishers, politicians, booksellers, librarians, media and supporters of the children’s literature community. The public is warmly invited to purchase tickets too.

Winners in the 2026 New Zealand Book Awards for Children and Young Adults will be announced in six categories: Picture Book (the BookHub Award), Junior Fiction (the Wright Family Foundation Esther Glen Award), Young Adult Fiction (the Wheelers Books Award), Non-Fiction, Illustration (the Russell Clark Award) and Te Reo Māori (the Wright Family Foundation Te Kura Pounamu Awards).

One of the category winners will receive the prestigious Margaret Mahy Book of the Year award. The judges will also present the NZSA Best First Book award to a previously unpublished author or illustrator from a shortlist of five titles.

Following the ceremony, all ticket holders are invited to enjoy food, refreshments, and conversation, served from 8.30pm to 10.00pm in Pipitea’s wharekai.

This is a popular event with a limited number of seats, so book your place today to join this wonderful celebration the very best children’s literature in of Aotearoa.

events.name: Pub Choir - Wellington, Aotearoa - Michael Fowler Centre (Just Think About It Tour)
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre
events.long_description:
Pub Choir - Wellington, Aotearoa - Michael Fowler Centre (Just Think About It Tour)
There are many facts in the known universe. For instance, did you know a giraffe is 30 times more likely to be struck by lightning? I guess because they are so tall?

Another fact is that Pub Choir is the world’s biggest, best, funniest, hottest music lesson. This fact has been verified by independent* sources (*we paid a guy on fiverr to say it).

An actually true fact is that Pub Choir is an opt-in experience. You don’t HAVE to buy a ticket and you are allowed to rot at home like you always do. But you PROBABLY should come and have a sing with a few thousand strangers. You would DEFINITELY feel better if you did. And hasn’t your sister-in-law been asking for years to go with you? It couldn’t be that bad could it?!? Everybody keeps bloody going on about it, maybe it’s worth a look. Anyway, just think about it.

What I'm saying is that Pub Choir will be touring across the world this year and Astrid is brewing some truly great arrangements, which I can claim with some authority, because I am her. We'll start in July in Australia, then head to NZ, Europe, the UK, and Asia. More info to come! In the meantime, the tour is called ‘Just Think About It’. And if you could, that'd be great.

You’ll learn one song in 3 part harmony at the show. That’s it, that’s the whole promise! Just think about it! Please come and have a sing! No worries if not!

This show is 18+ Please be aware that this event will be filmed & photographed. By purchasing a ticket and attending this event, you are giving your consent to be filmed & photographed during this event.

Tickets on sale here 2nd April 10am Local: https://www.ticketmaster.co.nz/event/24006471EC0A482C

Doors 6pm
Show 7pm

events.long_description:
Step into a little corner of France without leaving Wellington.
French Cheese Escape invites you on a curated tasting journey through France’s most iconic French cheese and their regions. During this relaxed experience, you’ll enjoy a guided “fromage flight” featuring four carefully selected French cheeses - from creamy and delicate to bold and beautifully aged.

Come with friends, a date, or solo, and immerse yourself in the tastes of France at your own pace.

events.name: Dessert First
events.venue: Le Ciel Bakery, 6/100 Tory Street
events.long_description:
For Chef Shuchi dessert has always been the most emotional part of a meal. It's where people slow down, and where conversation softens. For this event you're encouraged to skip right to dessert for this five course dessert tasting menu each tied to a memory. Some from Shuchi's life, some shared in our collective memories, all rooted in the small, often overlooked moments that shape how we experience sweetness.

Raspberry panna cotta tastes like school lunches and summer berries. Rich brownie with hazelnut mousse is the sweet thing you crave after a long day. The lemon cake that became Le Ciel's bestseller without anyone realising. Apple crumble soufflé carries memories of Shuchi's grandmother. Passionfruit posset brings the taste of home from Tanzania. Each course is plated with technique and restraint, refined, but never losing its warmth or intent. You'll spend an evening in the warm, slow space where dessert deserves to be.

Your ticket includes five plated courses plus one palate cleanser.

Overview
Join us for our annual edu roadshow! Join Steve (Google) & Jack (Fusion) to learn AI basics, prompting & responsible use in the classroom.

This half-day workshop gives you a practical introduction to Google Gemini and generative AI in education, delivered by Steve from Google and Jack from Fusion Networks.
You'll leave with the skills and confidence to use AI in your classroom and admin work, and you'll sit the Google Certified Gemini Educator exam right there in the session, no pressure, no separate booking.

Teachers, school leaders, and support staff who want practical, hands-on AI skills. No technical background needed.

Understanding Gemini and generative AI
What generative AI is and how it's different from other tech
How Gemini fits into tools you already use, like Docs, Gmail, and Classroom
Where AI can genuinely save you time (planning, grading, feedback, communication)
Using Gemini in your day-to-day practice
Writing prompts that actually get you useful results
Creating quizzes, lesson outlines, and rubrics with Gemini
Building your own "Gem" for repeat classroom tasks, like bell-ringers or feedback frames
Drafting emails and staff communications faster
Using AI responsibly
Spotting bias, errors, and "hallucinations" in AI output
Talking to students about plagiarism and responsible AI use
Building your own classroom guidelines for AI
Sit your certification exam on the day

Half-day, hands-on session. Bring a laptop and your Google Workspace login.

Masterton Street Eats & Beats

Formerly known as Thursday Night Food Trucks, Masterton Street Eats & Beats is Masterton's favourite weekly food truck and community event, bringing together great food, live music, and a relaxed family-friendly atmosphere every Thursday evening.

With a rotating lineup of food trucks and street food vendors, no two weeks are ever quite the same. From gourmet burgers and international cuisine to sweet treats, coffee, and local favourites, there's something to satisfy every craving. Add live music, plenty of seating, and a welcoming community vibe, and you've got the perfect way to kick off your weekend early.

Whether you're catching up with friends, bringing the family out for dinner, or simply looking for an easy meal after work, Masterton Street Eats & Beats offers a fun and affordable night out for all ages.

Event Details
Every Thursday
4:30pm – 7:00pm (rain or shine)
Outside the Masterton Club, Chapel Street (SH2), Masterton
Free Entry

What to Expect
• rotating food and beverage vendors throughout the season
• Live music and entertainment
• Family-friendly atmosphere
• outdoor seating available or bring a picnic blanket
• New vendors regularly joining the lineup
• EFTPOS and cash accepted by most vendors

Food truck and street food vendors are always welcome to enquire about joining the event.

Come hungry, bring your friends, and enjoy one of the Wairarapa's favourite weekly community gatherings.

More than most brewing, the craft of spontaneous fermentation is an international passion - so this Beervana weekend, we’re bringing some of the best in the world here to Wellington for your tasting pleasure.

No tickets, roll up and drink as you please.

Thursday 20 August | 4pm – 9pm
Friday 21 August | 2pm – 9pm
Saturday 22 August | 2pm – 9pm

Overview
Hear from graduates across our Screen Arts, Design, Commercial Music and Fine Arts programmes who are a few years into their careers.
What can you do with a creative degree?
College of Creative Arts | Toi Rauwhārangi graduates go on to build incredibly varied and inspiring careers across the creative industries and beyond. While creative study is sometimes questioned for its “employability”, the reality is that Aotearoa New Zealand’s arts and creative sector contributes $17.5 billion to GDP and makes up 4.2% of the total economy.
So where do our Screen Arts, Commercial Music, Design and Fine Arts graduates really end up?
Join us for a candid panel with recent graduates from Massey University’s College of Creative Arts | Toi Rauwhārangi and hear the real story of life after study: how they found work, what that transition looked like, and how they’re using what they learned in the real world. From building creative businesses and freelance careers to working in agencies, education, the public sector, and creative roles, our graduates are forging all kinds of futures.
You’ll hear from people working as:
artists and makers
designers and screen creatives
musicians and creative entrepreneurs
freelancers, contractors and sole traders
business owners and educators
creatives working both inside and outside the traditional creative industries
They’ll share the opportunities, connections and experiences that shaped their journey during study and beyond — including the realities of getting started in today’s economy.

Ecstatic Dance: Golden Hour

Step onto the dance floor, leave your shoes at the door and let the music guide you. A space for freedom, expression, connection, and joy as we move together into the golden hour.

events.long_description:
Overview

What if creating a better future starts with rethinking the way we live today?

FREE EVENT: Join us for an evening of conversation, connection, kai, and practical ideas for building more sustainable and resilient communities.

Who is this for? Anyone interested in creating a more sustainable and resilient future, whether you're already taking action or simply wondering where to start.

We'll bring together leaders, changemakers, and community voices to explore:

🌿 What can we actually do at home?
🌏 How can we build stronger, more resilient communities?
💡 What new ideas and innovations are making sustainable choices easier?
🤝 How can we learn from each other and turn ideas into action?




6:00–7:00 PM: Talanoa, panel & audience Q&A

7:00–8:00 PM: Kai, connection & networking




Talanoa for Tomorrow is taking place across four Wellington sessions, with a different panel of speakers at each event.




We are excited to announce for this session we have:

Rose Dohig is a Community Farm Manager at Kaicycle, where she has spent the last three years connecting people to the whenua and to each other. She believes that community building is one of the most effective tools for tackling the impacts of climate change and loves bringing this vision to life through her mahi. Kaicycle is an urban farm and composting initiative in Newtown that has been operating since 2015. The initiative connects people of all ages with the whenua, shares knowledge and skills on regenerative Hua Parakore growing practices, collects and composts food scraps from local businesses and households using e-bikes, and donates both grown kai and compost to local community programmes. Their education programme connects tamariki and rangatahi to food systems, climate action, kai, and the whenua.




Joshua Peauafi is a Pacific leader, social impact advocate, and co-founder of Potplant Studio. Passionate about relational leadership, diversity, equity, and inclusion, Joshua uses nature and plants as a vehicle to spark meaningful conversations around wellbeing, mental health, and community connection across Aotearoa New Zealand.


Can't make this date?

Check out our other sessions and find a date that works for you:

two/fiftyseven, Wellington

two/fiftyseven, Wellington




With different speakers and perspectives at each session, there will be something new to discover:




Let’s talanoa about fresh ideas to reduce waste, rethink how we live, and create a better tomorrow together.




Spaces are limited




Hosted by POTPLANT STUDIO, in partnership with Wellington City Council.

events.id: Our Kids Online Parent Evening 2026-Kapiti College School Hall, Margaret Rd, Raumati Beach, Raumati-Event Finder
events.name: Our Kids Online Parent Evening 2026
events.venue: Kapiti College School Hall, Margaret Rd, Raumati Beach, Raumati
events.long_description:
We want our school to be a safe place.

Because of the rapidly changing times, our tamariki are growing up in, and the mounting challenges and harms they are facing online we need to start talking about and tackling this as a community.
As such, Kapiti College has organised Filmmaker, Author and Speaker Rob Cope, producer of the documentary "Our Kids Online" to come and give what promises to be a humorous and eye-opening evening talk to our parent community.

His talk will cover:
Cyberbullying - How bullies can reach our kids 24/7
Social media - How social media is affecting the mental health in 3 out of 5 children. FOMO, depression, anxiety.
Gaming and the developing brain – An oversupply of dopamine leading to dopamine deficiency, synaptic pruning, and the underdevelopment of social skills and empathy
Naked Selfies - The pressure to send nudes from intermediate up through high school
Online predators - The methods they use, how to spot them.
Online porn vs healthy sexuality - How consuming online pornography as a child or teen can create a sexual template where violence, aggression, and dominance are seen as normal and consent can become very blurry
Solutions

Filters - Which filters are best and how to install them
Smartphones - How to lock down a smartphone to make it a safe phone
Boundaries - How to put good boundaries in place around device use
3 golden rules - The 3 golden rules that will keep your kids safe
Talking to your kids - How to have difficult conversations with your kids
Challenging our own phone and device usage - Reconnecting as a family.
"We need to tackle this as a community so that all of our kids are safe. When I protected my kids online, I also protected yours, so please, please protect your kids online so that you are also protecting mine" Rob Cope

events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, 111 Wakefield Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
THE WORLD’S GREATEST DIRE STRAITS SHOW RETURNS TO NEW ZEALAND FOR THREE SHOWS ONLY

The Dire Straits Experience brings the legendary sound of one of rock’s most iconic bands back to Wellington, Christchurch and Auckland this August.

The celebrated and critically acclaimed The Dire Straits Experience is set to return to New Zealand in August for three exclusive shows as part of their highly anticipated Long Highway 2026 World Tour.

Performing the unforgettable music of Dire Straits with stunning authenticity, world-class musicianship and full concert production, the internationally acclaimed seven-piece ensemble will play Wellington’s Michael Fowler Centre on Thursday 20 August, Christchurch Town Hall on Friday 21 August, and Auckland’s Kiri Te Kanawa Theatre on Saturday 22 August.

Assembled by original Dire Straits saxophonist Chris White — a key member of the Brothers In Arms and On Every Street tours — alongside acclaimed singer and guitarist Terence Reis, The Dire Straits Experience delivers a breath-taking journey through Mark Knopfler’s platinum-selling catalogue, bringing one of the greatest songbooks in rock history back to life on stage.

Audiences can expect a two-hour live concert spectacular packed with era-defining anthems including Money for Nothing, Sultans of Swing, Walk of Life, Romeo and Juliet, Brothers in Arms, Private Investigations, Tunnel of Love, Telegraph Road and more.

Handpicked from the highest levels of the international touring circuit, the ensemble features musicians whose collective careers include performances with Paul McCartney, Joe Cocker, Ray Charles, Robbie Williams, ABC, Tears For Fears, Roachford — and Mark Knopfler himself. Together, they recreate the musical power, precision and spirit that made Dire Straits a global phenomenon.

More than 40 years since Sultans of Swing first introduced the world to Mark Knopfler’s unmistakable guitar and songwriting genius, Dire Straits’ music remains a defining force in rock history. With over 120 million albums sold worldwide, the band’s songs continue to resonate across generations.

Dire Straits also holds a unique and enduring bond with New Zealand and Australian audiences. Their monumental 1986 Brothers In Arms tour sold more than 900,000 tickets across Australasia, setting concert attendance records that stood for more than three decades and cementing the band’s place in the musical DNA of the region.

“We absolutely loved our 2024 New Zealand Tour and can’t wait to be returning with The Dire Straits Experience to play for all of our friends in New Zealand. See you in August!” said Chris White.

While Dire Straits officially disbanded in 1995, their music has never faded. The Dire Straits Experience is more than a tribute — it is a powerful celebration of a musical legacy that continues to captivate audiences worldwide.

For Kiwi fans, this is a rare opportunity to relive the songs, the sound, and the spirit of one of rock’s greatest bands — live in concert once again.

*Plus booking fees

events.long_description:
Greg Rust: Life in the Fast Lane – Stories from Behind the Microphone
What happens when you're standing trackside as the world's fastest drivers hurtle past at 300 kilometres an hour?

Or when you're interviewing champions moments after victory, heartbreak or controversy?

Most of us only see the finished broadcast.

The highlights.

The interviews.

The polished moments on screen.

But behind every major sporting event are extraordinary stories, fascinating personalities and split-second moments that rarely make it into the final broadcast.

Join renowned motorsport broadcaster and storyteller Greg "Rusty" Rust for a lively and entertaining Learning Lunch packed with behind-the-scenes stories from a remarkable career spent at the heart of international sport and media.

From Formula One and MotoGP to Bathurst, the Winter Olympics and the Commonwealth Games, Greg has spent decades meeting extraordinary people and witnessing history unfold from the best seat in the house.

But this isn't just a conversation about motorsport.

It's about curiosity, human performance, great storytelling and what we learn when we spend time with people pursuing excellence at the highest level.

Expect humour, fascinating stories, unexpected insights and plenty of memorable moments from life behind the microphone.

Meet Greg 🎤

Greg "Rusty" Rust is one of Australia and New Zealand's best-known motorsport broadcasters, presenters and commentators. Over a career spanning almost 30 years, he has covered Formula One, MotoGP, Supercars, World Rally, the Winter Olympics, Commonwealth Games and major sporting events around the world. Based in Hawke's Bay, Greg is also the host of the award-winning Rusty's Garage podcast.

What We'll Explore
• Behind-the-scenes stories from major sporting events
• What really happens when the cameras are rolling
• Conversations with drivers, riders and champions
• The art of storytelling, interviewing and staying curious
• Lessons from a lifetime spent around remarkable people

events.name: Tofiga — Fresh Since Ages Ago
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Comedian Tofiga Fepulea’i is best known as a member of the stand-up comedy duo Laughing Samoans. Many of the hilarious characters created are still thought of fondly by Kiwis. Now Togifa is recreating those characters, plus some new ones, and travelling to The Opera House in Wellington. 
Fresh Since Ages Ago is a collection of skits that bring back Tofiga’s family characters, such as Aunty Tala, Uncle Sam, and Kung Fu master Tavita. A fresh update will be added when Tofiga collaborates with social media sensation and content creator Laban Miller. Together, they will present music, new characters, and new laughs. It’ll take ‘fresh’ to a whole new level of funny. 
Tofiga Fepulea’i’s first stand-up comedy show was performed at the New Zealand Fringe Festival in Wellington in 2003, so it’s fitting that he returns to the capital. events.long_description:
In many parts of Europe, the late afternoon snack is a daily ritual. In Wellington, it is finally getting its moment. For one Friday night, Amuse Snack Bar leans fully into the tradition, turning its pintxos offering into a lively, snack party celebrating kiwi tapas.

Expect a rotating spread of 10 to 15 pintxos built on Amuse’s sourdough baguette, topped with combinations like bacon and egg tortilla, pork belly with persimmon relish, seared tuna with kawakawa aioli, and classic gildas. Snacks are served quickly from the yellow window, ready to eat, with sticks tallied at the end.

Drinks stay close to the theme, with New Zealand vermouths, Spanish reds, and house cocktails designed for grazing. Drop in, eat well, and stay as long as you like.

Wellington! 🌙 Vanessa Tottle and Tragedies are taking over Moon Bar on Thursday, August 20th. Expect a massive night of darkwave, trip-hop, and incredible live electronic music.

Known for their intimate and personal live shows, Ordinary marks the band's first official release ahead of their debut album currently in the works.

events.name: Business Continuity Planning
events.venue: Wellington Chamber Of CommerceWellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview



This practical Business Continuity Planning workshop helps small and medium-sized businesses prepare for disruption before it happens.
Could your business keep operating if something unexpected happened tomorrow?
Disruptions don’t wait until you’re ready. Severe weather, supplier delays, cyber incidents, key staff absence, power outages, cash flow pressure or system failures can all stop normal operations fast.
This practical workshop will help you understand what a Business Continuity Plan is, why it matters, and how to start building one that works for your business.
You’ll learn how to identify your most critical business activities, understand the risks that could interrupt them, and put simple steps in place to keep operating, recover faster and communicate clearly when things go wrong.
What you’ll walk away with
A clear understanding of what a Business Continuity Plan should include
A practical framework to assess, prepare, respond and review
Tools to identify your critical processes, dependencies and recovery priorities
Simple steps to strengthen your business resilience over 30, 60 and 90 days
Confidence to start your plan without waiting for it to be perfect
Who should attend
This workshop is designed for New Zealand small and medium-sized business owners, managers and decision-makers who want to be better prepared for disruption.
Why attend
Because a simple plan started today could make all the difference when disruption arrives tomorrow.

events.id: Lost Wax in Three - Hard Wax - Friday Nights!-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
events.name: Lost Wax in Three - Hard Wax - Friday Nights!
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Over three sessions, create stunning jewellery using the age-old lost wax technique. This is an excellent opportunity to treat yourself to some creative fun on a Friday night!

In weeks one and two, you will learn how to work with jeweller's hard wax to create beautiful textures in metal that can be used to create amazing rings or objects. Your waxes will be sent away for casting in the metal of your choice.

Then there will be a week's break before the third session, to allow time for everyone's waxes to be cast. The third session covers how to trim, clean and finish your casts, turning them into original jewellery ready to wear!

More advanced students can use these sessions to complete projects in a class setting.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Not included are the casting and metal costs which vary from student to student depending on what sized ring they want to make and the type of metal you choose. Small castings can cost around $6.65 - $12 and might cost between $7 to $30 in metals depending on if you use red bronze, white bronze or silver.

This class is great for teens and kids over 12 or so. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.
