events.id: Stained Glass - 4 Weeks Friday Block-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Stained Glass - 4 Weeks Friday Block
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Learn to create gorgeous leadlight designs with our experienced jewellers!

This course starts om Fri 21 August and runs for 4 weeks until Fri 11 September, 5.30pm-8.30pm.

Your 4-week block will give you time to learn the basics and then create one or more stained glass projects.

This class is ideal for creating sun-catchers or small decorative projects for beginners, or working on slightly more complex pieces for those with some experience.

Beginners will start by planning their design, then learning to cut the glass, and prepare it before foiling and soldering each piece, creating a simple elegant clear glass starter project.

Beautiful coloured glass, copper foil and leadlight solder are then available to purchase as required for your other projects.

This is a warm and friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and more advanced students. All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.

All materials (glass, foil, and solder) are extra and can be purchased at the studio at a very reasonable cost.

events.id: Cooking Classes-Sheila's Indian Kitchen, Ashton Fitchett Dr, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Cooking Classes
events.venue: Sheila's Indian Kitchen, Ashton Fitchett Dr, Wellington
events.long_description:
Authentic Indian cooking classes in Wellington with panaromic views over Wellington Harbour.

In each class, you will learn 4-5 recipes like: potato stuff roti, roasted eggplant curry, wholemeal, roti, naan; shahi paneer; dhal, samosa; palak paneer; gourmet chickpeas; vegetable korma; gulab jamun; kheer; mango lassi; masala chai, and many more...

The classes start at 6 pm or 10:30 am on weekends and weekdays with a 2-hour session followed by a dinner or lunch afterwards. The ingredients, copies of recipes, organic karma drink will be provided with a full course meal in a banquet setting. Custom made classes available for gluten free, dairy free and any other food intolerance and dietary requirements.The ingredients, recipes, complimentary organic karma drinks will be provided with a full course meal.

There are 2 to 8 people in each class in purpose built cooking studio. Also a private cooking classes available.

The menu for the class can be:

1) Spicy potato stuffed paratha and roti, rajasthani tomato relish, aalu matter or spicy peas- potato curry, roasted cumin yogurt raita and fresh mint- coriander chutney.

2) Shahi Paneer (cottage cheese cubes with spices and rich tomato-cashew gravy), garlic coriander naan, cumin jeera basmati rice and sweet fragrant rice pudding with cardamom. Also I will teach how to make fresh paneer.

3) Roasted eggplant curry, plain whole wheat chapatti or roti, jeera aaloo or potato curry, Tuar dahl (split yellow lentil) and Basmati rice with homemade pickle.

4) Palak paneer (creamy spinach curry with cubes of paneer), jeera rice (basmati rice with fragrant spices, panjabi chhole or spicy chickpeas curry and mango lassi. Also fresh paneer making.

5) Khadi (chickpeas fritters in yogurt and chickpeas flour soupy gravy), Aloo-Gobhi (cauliflower and potato curry),  savoury wraps with herbs and spices, fresh pickle and basmati rice.

The total cost is $130 per person, this includes ingredient cost. (As an alternative we also sell cooking class gift vouchers.The food options are unlimited and the class provides fresh and best ingredients)
Please contact for booking: indiancooking@xtra.co.nz

So just bring your taste buds! and Enjoy!!

events.long_description:
Chronis Night Challenge 2026
Chronis Night Challenge 2026!

Join us for our second annual night meeting at Kaitoke – Friday 21st and Saturday 22nd August! Bikes and karts racing all weekend, so there'll be plenty of action both nights!

This event is also the second and final round of the North vs South 2026 Challenge – time to defend (or take back) the trophy!

Friday 21st August – Practice & Qualifying
On track approx 4:30pm – 9:30pm
Gates open, sign-on and bike check times: TBC as soon as possible

Saturday 22nd August – Race Day
On track approx 1:30pm – 10:30pm
5 rounds, run in club day format
Gates open, sign-on and bike check times: TBC as soon as possible
Prizegiving immediately after racing finishes

Costs
• KSW member: $110
• Non-KSW member: $120
• Transponder hire is free for the weekend – if you have your own kart transponder, bring it along but check with us first to confirm it'll work with our system!

Entries
Bike entries are limited to 42 total, with a firm cap of 21 per grade based on qualifying times.
Sign up link: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf9BvDyieCadvYiQSwsA05Oaro27dBZHpeSMdgTuVCwa3wlmw/viewform
Entries close 20 August – get in early to confirm your spot!

PLEASE read the Supplementary Regulations (linked in the entry form) before you rock up – they cover everything you need to know for this event!

Grids
Three wide, staggered rows, with 2m between the rear of the bike in front and the front of the bike behind.

Pits
Pit site allocation TBC closer to the time.

Officials for the weekend
Clerk of Course: Alysha Sands
Steward of Meeting: Dane Foster
Friday and Saturday night support crew (so far!): Georgia Lynn, Quentin, John Busby and Matt Clarke

We NEED an army of volunteers for both Friday and Saturday night! There will be lights on the track, sure, but we can't underestimate the safety risk of running at night! We need eyes... everywhere... we can't do this without extra hands. Calling all parents, friends and acquaintances – if you can spare some time either night, please reach out to Alysha!

✨ Light it up! ✨
It's a NIGHT race! So we're going to join our karting counterparts and allow some decorative lighting on your bikes!! Get creative, just make sure you follow the rules in the SuppRegs!

Machine examination will include checking your light setup, and the examiner's decision is final – so make it good, but make it compliant!

Wanna camp at the track?
Parking will be available Friday and Saturday in the far carpark on the western side of the track complex. Self-contained motorhomes and caravans only! Cost: TBC

Does racing make you hungry? Or thirsty?
The Club Café will be serving dinner both nights plus snacks and drinks. Alcoholic drinks available after racing only.

Not a member?
If you're not a BRNZ, MNZ or KSW member you can still race! Reach out and we'll give you the info you need.

Don't wanna race but wanna watch?
Spectators are free to come along and enjoy the racing – everyone's welcome! Just keep your wits about you and stay safe around the track.

More info to follow closer to the event – keep an eye on this page!

See you there!

Please note: the track is closed Friday through Sunday for any activity other than the on-track times listed above.

Manawa Ora - The Foundations of Māori Bodywork and Healing.

Now - more than ever - there is a focus on self-care and a revitalisation of our traditional healing practices.

This workshop will be held at The Manawa Ora whare hauora (clinic) in Glenside, Wellington.

events.name: 1tbsp (AUS) tickets
events.venue: Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Presented by: UNDR Ctrl, Low Strung, & The Slack Agency
Across the last few years, 1tbsp, the Meanjin-born, Gadigal-based producer, songwriter, DJ and Dottidot label founder, has quietly assembled one of electronic music's most distinctive universes – a glossy, hyper-coloured landscape where reggaeton drums collide with toy-box synths, club music sparkles with pop sentiment, and every release feels like a portal into somewhere slightly unfamiliar.
Following a huge run of international touring in the first half of the year, including appearances at Coachella, a North American Bubble Tour and a residency at London's Phonox, 1tbsp jumps the ditch with Bubble Tour - a live show that expands his ever-evolving world.
Originally known through his Grammy-nominated alt-indie project Golden Vessel, Maxwell Byrne launched 1tbsp in 2021 as an outlet for stranger ideas. What began with the kanashī EP soon evolved into a fully realised creative universe, culminating in the release of his debut album Mosquito Love and later the acclaimed Megacity1000.
Released in 2024, Megacity1000 arrived like a transmission from a parallel metropolis - equal parts club record and pop experiment. Across the album's eight tracks, Byrne fused candy-coated percussion, shimmering vocal fragments and bright, maximalist production into a sound entirely his own. Support quickly followed from Pitchfork, Mixmag, CLASH, The Line of Best Fit and EARMILK, cementing 1tbsp as one of Australia's most forward-thinking electronic exports.
That same spirit extends beyond his own catalogue through Dottidot, Byrne's label and creative platform, which has become home to a growing network of artists and collaborators. Recent releases from label affiliates Soltera and Cherry Chola continue to expand the architecture of this ecosystem.
Now, for the first time, Bubble Tour arrives in Aotearoa this August. Welcome to the Bubble Tour.

events.long_description:
TOČKA | Fiunary | Veale Moss
TOČKA beckons Every one to feel carnal and Hollowed. Drawing influence from film, industrial-style production, 00s R&B, and pain, it amalgamates to create a Flayed and Tortured, cathartic club æsthetic. By towing a line between pop femininity and crushing grotesquerie, the artist explores the sensuality in fear, the liberation in disgust, the power in the broken.
-
Fiunary. A terrible and brilliant thing is approaching. A few days ago I felt a weight shift inside me. It happened suddenly, without pause. The air, each footstep, the balance of my head - they all feel different now. No, it's coming from behind my eyes - it's my own gaze that shifted. This is the kind of thing that ruptures you from the inside. What kind of thing is it? I want to be ready to grasp it. fiunary is alive, makes music, and will die.
-
Veale Moss - /viːl/ /mɒs/ , Archivist, unnaturally dense, collected airs of temporary significance.

events.id: Tulsa Meets Martinborough-Union Square, 10 Memorial Square-WOAP
events.name: Tulsa Meets Martinborough
events.venue: Union Square, 10 Memorial Square
events.long_description:
From cattle country to oil fields, from dive bars to dinner tables. Tulsa's food tells the story of America's heartland. General Manager Adam Cruz continues his "meets Martinborough" series by bringing the bold, smoky soul of Southern cooking to the Napoleon dining room's intimate fireplace. 
Five courses trace a culinary exploration: start with a Reuben egg roll (sauerkraut, corned beef, Russian dressing), move through fried pork ribs that legend is made of, followed by biscuits swimming in sausage gravy, and then slow-smoked BBQ pulled pork served with cornbread, fried okra, and black-eyed peas — sides that honour the agricultural plains. Strawberry pecan pie closes out the night. Each course pairs with a Martinborough beverage: hand-crafted brews from Martinborough Brewery, award-winning Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from Palliser Estate, a botanical gin from Margrain, and a Noble wine to finish with pie. 
Your ticket includes five courses and four standard drinks (low and non-alcoholic options available).

events.id: Discover Te Muna - Go behind the scenes-Te Muna Valley, 950 White Rock Rd, Martinborough-Event Finder
events.name: Discover Te Muna - Go behind the scenes
events.venue: Te Muna Valley, 950 White Rock Rd, Martinborough
events.long_description:
Born from passionate vignerons who embrace the challenge of extreme weather conditions, Te Muna valley's unique microclimate and soil structure result in exceptional wines with distinctive style.

Join us for full-day immersive experience in the viticulture, winemaking and wines of Te Muna Valley. Walk the vineyards, meet the producers, go behind the scenes and taste exceptional wines right where they are made.

Your journey begins with a pickup from Martinborough Square, leading to an intimate start at Big Sky Wines. From there tour the stunning Blue Earth Estate before indulging in a long relaxed lunch alongside some of the region's winemakers. The adventure continues with an exploration of the beautiful terraced Craggy Range vineyard,, followed by an insider's look at the renowned winery at Escarpment, both of which are not normally open to the public. We will finish the day with some of the other Te Muna producers joining us to share their wines and their stories.

It will be a day of discovery - the place, the people and the wines of the beautiful Te Muna Valley.

Tickets are strictly limited to 20 people.

events.long_description:
Getting the Most from ChatGPT
(NZ Citizens and residents pay $29 with ID, all others pays $120).
AI tools like ChatGPT are everywhere, but how do you get the best out of them? In this hands-on, phone-based workshop, Jon Bell will guide you through practical techniques to make ChatGPT a more useful, reliable partner in your work and life. Whether you’ve tried it a few times or use it regularly, you’ll learn how to write better prompts, refine responses, and avoid common pitfalls without needing any technical background.
We’ll cover real examples, answer your questions as they come up, and spend plenty of time experimenting together so you leave feeling confident and ready to put your new skills to use.
Please bring: A phone with the ChatGPT app installed, and enough battery to last the day.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
Write effective prompts that get clearer, more useful responses
Use ChatGPT for research, brainstorming, and creative work
Recognise the tool’s limitations (and how to work around them)
Apply practical strategies for using AI in your personal or professional projects
Confidently troubleshoot when ChatGPT gives unexpected or unhelpful answers

events.id: Jewellery Making - Faceted Gemstone Settings-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Jewellery Making - Faceted Gemstone Settings
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Evolve and advance your jewellery making with beautiful faceted stone setting methods! Create jewellery embedded with precious glittering gems in copper, brass and silver - beginners welcome! All material costs included in the course fee.

Description
In this challenging and exciting workshop students will learn to set glimmering round-cut faceted gemstones into brass, copper and/or silver. Create a stone set jewellery project from a choice of simple earrings, a pendant, or a ring.

Students who have already done a Lost Wax Cast Rings class may bring their cast rings and try their hand at setting stones in those instead of starting a new project.

Students will learn ‘Flush Setting’, a method of embedding gems into the surface of metal without the need for solder or joins. The process is adaptable to a number of jewellery types and styles. Students with prior Flush Setting and soldering experience may advance to other methods and to try their hand at learning ‘Bead Setting’, or a simple form of ‘Prong Setting’.

Students may choose from lab-created Sapphires, Rubies and other high strength stones such as Cubic Zirconia in a range of colours.

The workshop is especially satisfying for the magpie in all of us, adding extra colour and shine to jewellery making.

While both beginners and returning students are welcome in the class, be aware that the tools and techniques require a level of fine motor skills, keen eye for detail, and strong hand control which take some patience, practice and perseverance to get the best results.

Our magnifying headsets, work clamps, and patient tutor will help you along the way.

Please wear closed-in footwear suitable for a workshop environment. bring a work apron if you have one or wear clothes you don’t mind getting a little grubby. Remember to bring your reading glasses if you have them.

By the end of the course, students will be able to:

Develop jewellery making skills with introductory faceted stone setting methods

Create a simple stone set project - either earrings, a pendant, or a ring.

Use Vernier Calipers to measure and calculate metal dimensions

Use files to shape brass, copper and/or silver components

Use a soldering torch to attach metal components such as jump rings

File, sand and polish brass, copper and/or silver creations into finished jewellery

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Women's Health and Aging Workshop
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Women's Health and Aging Workshop
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
An interactive workshop presented by experienced physiotherapist Sara Dore, focusing on how movement and function can be challenging for women as they age. Particularly for women, there is more to the core than abdominal muscles and strength and we explore these broader aspects.  Most importantly, you will come to understand that movement is medicine and we can make a difference.
You will be able to make a positive difference for yourself! The objective of this workshop is to give you knowledge and understanding about how you can manage the effects on your health and wellbeing as we age as women.  Knowledge is power!
In this one-day workshop you will discover:
- The base of the pelvic floor. Anatomy of the pelvic floor, and the common conditions urinary incontinence, and pelvic organ prolapse will be discussed. Education on basic pelvic floor advice and management as well as appropriate exercises will also be covered.
- The middle deep abdominal muscles. Trunk stability versus core strength as we age and the impact on our other core muscles and pelvic floor will be discussed. The principles of Clinical Pilates versus traditional Pilates will be presented together with the key principles of movement is medicine.
-The importance of the diaphragm and breathing well will also be discussed to enhance optimal movement and function for women.
Please wear comfortable clothes and socks as this is an interactive workshop, and bring a yoga mat or beach towel.
Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.

The Zentangle® method is an easy-to-learn, relaxing and fun method to create amazing images by drawing structured patterns.

Discover your creative side, even if you think you don’t have one. You might surprise yourself!  If you can hold a pen, you can do this.
Creating Zentangle patterns is super relaxing and a creative form of mindfulness. Increase your awareness and focus, get absorbed and feel more confident while making your own unique and original art.
Learn about borders, strings, and shading. Learn your first tangles and discover the world of Crescent Moon, Hollibaugh, Printemps, and Florz. It feels great to have creativity flowing. Anything is possible one stroke at a time. There are no mistakes to make here!
After a step-by-step introduction you will take home your amazing images and have discovered a new way to relax.
All art materials are included in course fee.  Tea and coffee is available but please bring your lunch/snacks.

events.id: Textured Bracelets-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Textured Bracelets
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
This lively, hands-on workshop is designed for complete beginners, but it’s also a great opportunity for more experienced students to enjoy a creative session making their own unique bangle!

Everyone will leave with a beautifully finished bracelet of their own preferred texture.

We’ll begin by experimenting on a sample strip of copper, where you’ll practice creating textures using hammers, punches and stamps. Once you’re confident, you’ll move on to your main project: a 3mm wide flat strip bracelet in either sterling silver or copper, crafted entirely by you from start to finish. Along the way, you’ll learn essential jewellery-making skills including measuring, texturing, soldering, shaping, and finishing.

Students are free to personalise their bangle with textures or stamped designs. This could be a simple hammered finish, decorative patterns, or meaningful words, names, dates, or poetry lines - making your bracelet truly one of a kind.
Beginners will work with the 3mm strip provided, ensuring a rewarding project that’s manageable to complete. Wider metal is much harder to form and solder, so we are learning to walk before we can run ;)

Copper is included in the course fee; if you wish to work in silver, you can purchase it on the day.

Experienced students may choose to challenge themselves by making a wider bracelet from a flat strip or by creating additional bangles in silver wire. (Please note: extra silver for wider bangles is available to purchase at the workshop for experienced students only, and let us know if you wish to go wider so we can make sure we have the strip in stock.)

This workshop is a taster class: perfect for anyone seeking a fun, creative experience with a beautiful result, or for those looking to dip their toes into jewellery making and build foundational skills.

events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Spend your Saturday afternoons immersed in creativity, learning the timeless craft of jewellery-making in our warm, welcoming studio.

It starts on Saturday 22 August and runs for 4 weeks till Saturday 12 September, 2pm-5pm.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

We set these classes in blocks of 4 weeks so students can easily stack their learning and move into projects like a stone set ring.

This block is ideal for teens and young creatives aged 12 and up.
Please note: anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
A Day in the Heart - One Day Silent Yoga and Meditation Retreat
An invitation to press "pause" for a day, and just Be.

To drop from the busy mind into the silence of the Heart.

And to remember the freedom of who you are, when you're not in a role.


This lovingly crafted offering is a day immersion into practice, providing a glimpse of what the experience of silence can offer.

Suitable for complete beginners in meditation and yoga, as well as for advanced practitioners who'd like to unplug and enjoy retreat-time.


The schedule will include:

- Multiple seated meditation sessions with guidance

- Walking meditation

- Mindful Hatha Yoga and Restorative Yoga sessions

- Yoga Nidra

- Cacao to open the Heart

- Time to journal, walk in nature, or just be


Cost for a whole day program + 2 meals: $195


Food:

breakfast and lunch - nutritious vegan meals prepared with love + tea and cacao


Location:

the Lotus Yoga Centre in Paraparaumu


Date: 22nd August 2026 Saturday

Duration: 7.30am - 5.30pm

please arrive at 7.15am to settle in and start on time


To book, please purchase your ticket below or email Radha for more info at


*WHY IS THIS A SILENT RETREAT? A silent retreat means that everyone participating observes mauna, noble silence (apart from the teacher/ the guide). This means no casual chats and conversations, but also no use of phone or any devices during the day. The practice of silence allows the the mind to quieten down significantly, it is a very unique, deeply purifying and enlightening experience. It creates space for a deep insight and a proper reset, even in the short span of one day.


*WHY MEDITATION? Meditation is known for thousands of years as one of the most powerful practices, within and outside of spiritual context. It is good not only for creating a state of calm or relaxation, but also is the best known path to self-knowledge and self-love. When we retreat into silence beyond mind, there is an unmistakable feeling of being back home, in the heart of being, a sense of connection and purpose.


*WHY "A DAY IN THE HEART"? The Heart/ Hridaya in Sanskrit is a synonym of awareness or presence. According to the great yogis and the non-dual philosophy, the Heart is a place to centre in our meditations, but also an organ of knowledge and the seat of our true Self. When the mind is quiet and we centre within, the Heart can awaken - bringing a sense of being back home, back to what truly matters, back to our Self.

As Rumi said, "Close your eyes, fall in love, stay there"

events.long_description:
Dark Sky Trek Wainuiomata
We’ve teamed up with the Wellington Astronomical Society to bring you this exclusive FREE behind-the-scenes event.

Walk deep into untouched native forest, through some of the oldest trees in the Wellington region as darkness falls. You may even hear the calls of kiwi and rūrū (morepork). Explore an area not normally open to the public, including a glowworm-filled tunnel that links to the Orongorongo Valley.

The Wellington Astronomical Society will share insights on Dark Sky awareness and preservation and provide a telescope for viewing the Moon and the Southern Cross. Talk to Remutaka Conservation Trust volunteers about their Kiwi release programme and nest monitoring efforts.

Wainuiomata Regional Park is working towards dark sky reserve accreditation, one of only three in the Southern Hemisphere. Light pollution from the city washes out most stars, but the park offers one of the best stargazing experiences in the region.

What to bring:
• Torches/headlamps (red lenses preferred)
• Sturdy waterproof footwear
• Warm and wet weather clothing

Note: This event includes a steep hill walk in the dark. A moderate level of fitness is required, and it is not suitable for children under 15.

This event is strictly limited to 30 people. Registrations for this event will be on a first in first served basis and opens at 10am on Tuesday 14 July via this link:

events.name: Adam McGrath
events.venue: Hilltop, 17 Upland Road, Kelburn, Wellington
events.long_description:
Gate opens 6.30pm, music starts 7pm

We are SO LUCKY to have Adam McGrath returning to Hilltop – he’s one of the best. Adam has already had a full-on year (and it’s only half way), including touring with the ‘Come Together’ Born To Run – Bruce Springsteen concerts, and then touring with Gary McCormick. Adam is the winner of the 2024 Aotearoa/New Zealand Folk Artist of the Year Award at the Aotearoa/New Zealand music awards. Described by RNZ as a “National Treasure” and the Herald as “NZ’s toughest minded songwriter”, Adam is also widely known as lead singer and songwriter with one of NZ’s most loved roots/country bands The Eastern. Adam’s new album Wrecker Songs was released on May Day 2026 to coincide with the 75th anniversary of the Maritime Union of New Zealand (MUNZ). It hit #1 – Aotearoa Albums Chart and #4 – Official Top 40 Albums (all albums, domestic and international). It also reached #1 on the IMNZ (Independent Music New Zealand) Album Chart. “Wrecker Songs is here, on all the streamers, the cd’s are here the vinyl is late, the spirit is high, the heart is a eye and its wide, the muscle is gristly, the bones brittle, the mind shows grit despite the fog, the fists clenched, the struggle real, the solidarity true.”… Click for the first song on the album -> ‘The Assembly” Adam is a folk singer and yarn spinner stationed, he says, wherever he can get a key! He spends eight months a year on the road between NZ, Australia, Europe and parts beyond. With The Eastern and solo he has shared stages with and opened for Fleetwood Mac, Steve Earle, Old Crow Medicine Show, Paul Kelly, Jimmy Barnes and many, more. His song Hope and Wire was the inspiration behind Gaylene Preston’s TV series of the same name and he is known for his service orientated approach to music in the years since. Described as “maybe part folk singer, part preacher, part boxer, and part rodeo clown he is however all heart”. Raucous, tender, roof and spirit raising, a McGrath show goes straight for the spirit level in all of us, looking deep for the good parts and hoping to reach all the thoughtful bits that matter.

Adam’s first solo album was released December ’23. “It’s called Dear Companions, because of everything I’ve learnt or am learning about the people in the songs and what they help me learn about myself and about the world big and small (especially small). But that kind of conception is just how records start, where they end up is up to whoever gets a copy in their life.”
“One of the best modern roots artists, from any country”
-No Depression magazine

Come along and enjoy this great gig in our special space, up close and personal.

These are private house concerts, not for profit, supporting our dedicated musicians. Visit www.hilltophouseconcerts.co.nz to reserve a seat. Suggested donation $30. Email confirmation will include address and details.

Teas, Coffee and Snacks provided. You're welcome to bring anything you'd like to eat or drink.
Parking available in the Coupon zones of Upland Rd & Glasgow St free after 6pm weekdays, and free all through the weekends. The Wilson Carpark at the top of the Cable Car charges 24/7.

events.long_description:
Card Merchant Wellington - Catan Cities Event 2026
​Card Merchant is incredibly excited to be working with CATAN Studio and Asmodee to bring official CATAN Organized Play to New Zealand.

As part of the 2026 Organized Play program, Card Merchant stores across the country will be hosting 10 CATAN Cities Events. These events represent the next step up in competitive play and serve as regional qualifiers for the New Zealand CATAN National Championship.

Each represented city will host a single Cities Event, with 10 events taking place nationwide. The winner of each Cities Event will earn a seeded place in the Top 16 of the New Zealand Catan National Championship, to be held in Wellington later this year.

Whether you're an experienced Catan player or looking to test your skills in a larger tournament environment, Cities Events provide the opportunity to compete against players from your region and take the next step on the road to Nationals.

Event Details

Store: Card Merchant Wellington

Date: 22nd August 2026

Time: 11:00am

Entry Fee: $20

Event Structure

Players will compete across multiple rounds of base game CATAN to determine overall standings.

Preliminary Round

• Each participant will play three separate games of base set CATAN.

• Opponents will rotate between games.

• At the conclusion of the preliminary rounds, players will be ranked based on their overall performance.

Final Rounds

• Depending on attendance numbers, top-performing players may advance to final tables to determine overall placings.

• If attendance numbers are lower, the event may instead consist solely of multiple Swiss-style rounds, with final standings determined by total points or wins.

This structure is designed to provide a competitive tournament experience while remaining approachable and enjoyable for players of all experience levels.

Prizes

In addition to qualification opportunities, a range of official Catan Organized Play prizes will be awarded on the day.

Prizing includes:

8x Summer Hex Sets

2x Gamegenic Catan Sleeves

2x Exit: Adventures on Catan

2x Catan Starfarers Duel

2x Struggle for Catan

1x Tiger’s Eye Dice and Robber promo

1x Aquamarine Dice and Robber promo

1x Hematite Dice and Robber promo

1x Opalite Dice and Robber promo

1x Catan Inclusion Dice set

1x Catan: Dawn of Humankind + Promo

1x Catan: New Energies

Join us for your chance to earn a direct route for Nationals top 16, meet other CATAN players from your region, and take part in New Zealand's official 2026 CATAN Organized Play program.

events.long_description:
Since 1747, Maille has been synonymous with French gastronomy. The supplier to the court of King Louis XV, it remains one of the most recognised French condiment brands in the world. This August, Maille teams up with Le Bouillon Bel Air for Menu du Jour: a special collaborative bistro series served every Sunday throughout the month.

Step into a classic Parisian-inspired dining experience and enjoy a three-course menu where Maille's signature mustards feature throughout each dish. Begin with a leek terrine dressed in a Dijon and wholegrain Maille mustard vinaigrette, followed by Poulet Gaston Gérard—chicken in a rich Maille mustard and cream sauce. Finish with a dark chocolate mousse accompanied by brown butter crumble, poached pear, and a mustard-sesame-honey tuile. This exclusive three-course menu is available for $85 per person, every Sunday in August.

events.long_description:
At Cicio Cacio Osteria, the Mediterranean comes to the table in an intimate dinner shaped by memory and place. Inspired by the owner's childhood on a Mediterranean island, this dinner traces a path from Italy to Spain, across Greece and into the Middle East, with dishes from each region reflecting the shared spirit of the Mediterranean: the sun, the sea, the music, the nostalgia, the being in the moment. The food is uncomplicated and entirely enjoyable, simple, fare focused on freshness and simplicity, letting the ingredients speak for themselves. Expect the most perfect hummus with grilled pita, the best Spanish tortilla, uncommon seafood like octopus and sardines, couscous, lamb, and goat, pastas, and colourful salads, a true insight into the Mediterranean spirit. 

You'll be seated at a long communal table in front of a real fire for a progressive nine-course menu, each plate paired with a matched wine selected to reflect its origin and character. Throughout the evening, the chef shares stories behind the dishes, offering insight into flavours, traditions, and personal history. You're invited to come into the kitchen and share the secrets of each recipe, cooking alongside the chef. A final musical touch ends an evening dedicated to the beauty, spontaneity, and simplicity of the Mediterranean. 

Your ticket includes nine courses, nine matched wines, storytelling, hands-on cooking, and recipe sharing.

events.long_description:
1TBSP | WELLINGTON | MEOW NUI
1tbsp is returning to Wellington for an exclusive NZ show, all his previous NZ dates selling out - get in quick!

PRESALE: Thursday, 2nd of July, 4:30PM NZT
GA ONSALE - Friday 3rd of July, - 4:30PM NZT
PRESALE LINK - https://arep.co/p/1tbsp-bubble-tour-wellington-1

Following a huge run of international touring in the first half of the year, including appearances at Coachella, a North American Bubble Tour and a residency at London's Phonox, 1tbsp jumps the ditch with Bubble Tour - a live show that expands his ever-evolving world.

Across the last few years, 1tbsp, the Meanjin-born, Gadigal-based producer, songwriter, DJ and Dottidot label founder, has quietly assembled one of electronic music's most distinctive universes – a glossy, hyper-coloured landscape where reggaeton drums collide with toy-box synths, club music sparkles with pop sentiment, and every release feels like a portal into somewhere slightly unfamiliar.

Originally known through his Grammy-nominated alt-indie project Golden Vessel, Maxwell Byrne launched 1tbsp in 2021 as an outlet for stranger ideas. What began with the kanashī EP soon evolved into a fully realised creative universe, culminating in the release of his debut album Mosquito Love and later the acclaimed Megacity1000.

Released in 2024, Megacity1000 arrived like a transmission from a parallel metropolis - equal parts club record and pop experiment. Across the album's eight tracks, Byrne fused candy-coated percussion, shimmering vocal fragments and bright, maximalist production into a sound entirely his own. Support quickly followed from Pitchfork, Mixmag, CLASH, The Line of Best Fit and EARMILK, cementing 1tbsp as one of Australia's most forward-thinking electronic exports.

That same spirit extends beyond his own catalogue through Dottidot, Byrne's label and creative platform, which has become home to a growing network of artists and collaborators. Recent releases from label affiliates Soltera and Cherry Chola continue to expand the architecture of this ecosystem.

Now, for the first time, Bubble Tour arrives in Aotearoa this August, Saturday 22nd at Meow Nui.

Tickets on sale: Friday 3rd of July - 4:30pm (Local time) from Tickettek.

Pitch n Faders Presents SNEEKY
We're back and super excited to share our guest with you for August, the one like SNEEKY!!!

Hailing from Tāmaki Makaurau, Sneeky is now holding it down in Te Matau-a-Māui (Hawke’s Bay) as a DJ known for sets that are as dynamic as they are genre-defying. Blending old-school house, filthy funk, raw tech, deep disco, sexy indie, and shadowy melodic rhythms, she weaves sounds that feel both familiar and unexpected.
Not just a DJ, she’s also one of the Bay’s most prominent dance music promoters and the founder of Sound Selectors. A key figure in the local scene, she runs a range of events that create space for emerging DJs while also bringing some of Aotearoa’s favourite acts to the region.
Sneeky has played some of the country’s most respected festivals (Relish, Taniwha’s Den, AUM, Club Festivus, Nest Fest, Outfield, Collins St Festival, Naked in the Trees, Abracadabra, Arkadien), held her own alongside local and international heavyweights (Sammy Virji, Pitch Black, Sanoi, Sweet Mix Kids, Dick Johnson, Flamingo Pier, P.Digsss, Solar Rosa, and Salmonella Dub to name a few), and built a rep for pushing sound beyond the expected. Every set is different, shaped by the room, the energy, band the moment.

FREE ENTRY

As per usual Hape will be guiding us out of dinner service before handing the reins over to Sneeky

The drinks will be flowin and the beats will be rollin

Come join us and get amongst the dance...

Join us to celebrate Inverlochy's Next Generation Artists at an open seminar & exhibition closing celebration.

The Inverlochy Art School Next Generation Artist's Showcase brings together four Wellington based artists in years 11-13 of high school. This year we are very proud to present artwork by Saskia Day, Maia Fletcher-Walker, Emma Phillips and Yuko Thorpe. Working across painting, sculpture and photography, all artists applied to this exhibition in response to our open call and were selected on the highly individual quality of their work and the dedication that all showed to their art.

To celebrate these artists and another year of this fabulous showcase we have prepared a morning devoted to discussing and admiring art!

What makes artworks aesthetic, powerful and meaningful? Gain an insight into some of the hidden rules that govern a work of art with Geetika Chatterjee.

View the exhibition, meet the artists and hear them speak about their work over coffee, tea and cake!


Koha entry.

events.id: Let’s Talk About It: How Conversation Can Impact Social Change for Māori-The Dowse Art MuseumLower Hutt, Wellington-Event Brite
events.name: Let’s Talk About It: How Conversation Can Impact Social Change for Māori
events.venue: The Dowse Art MuseumLower Hutt, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview

Artist, Professor & former politician Metiria Turei chairs a panel on the potential for change that can happen by talking about hard things.
Artist, Law Professor and former politician Metiria Turei chairs a panel on the potential for change that can happen by talking about hard things. Maria Bargh, Kassie Hartendorp and Jack McDonald will draw on their experience and expertise to discuss why we need to have challenging conversations about the difficulties for Māori in order to make significant change.
Responding to the Dowse exhibition Things We Don’t Talk About, that highlights unspoken or unheard challenges that Māori communities face in Aotearoa. Moments of cultural tension, conflict, and sadness that have occurred over many decades are echoed here alongside present-day stories of resilience, perseverance and hope. This panel will reflect on the possibilities of what can happen when issues are brought into the light and how change has been made through acknowledging uncomfortable truths.

Ngāti Kahungunu ki Wairarapa, Āti Haunui a Pāpārangi. Metiria Turei is an Associate Professor at Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka, teaching tikanga Maori law in Te Kaupeka Tātai Ture, the Faculty of Law. She was a member of the New Zealand Parliament and Co-leader of the Green Party. Turei built a career as a social activist before moving to develop her art practice . Her art work is in performative textiles, photography and sculpture, Indigenous Futurism and rangatiratanga.
Maria Bargh is from Te Arawa and Ngāti Awa. She is a Professor of politics and Māori Studies and researches and teaches in Te Kawa a Māui, Māori Studies, Te Herenga Waka, Victoria University of Wellington. She is co-chair of her hapū Ngāti Kea Ngāti Tuara Reservations Trust for lands at Horohoro and in Rotorua.
Kassie Hartendorp (Ngāti Raukawa, Ngāti Tūwharetoa) is a community organiser for social justice and Te Tiriti justice. She is the Director for ActionStation, which created Together for Te Tiriti and led campaigns against the Treaty Principles Bill and to keep Māori wards.
Jack McDonald is an uri of Taranaki and Te Whakatōhea. A political campaigner and activist, Jack currently works as Te Kaihautū Māori at the Public Service Association Te Pūkenga Here Tikanga Mahi. Previously he worked as Te Pāti Māori's Policy Director and before that he helped lead the Green Party’s Māori political work. A writer and music obsessive, Jack is interested in exploring creative and artistic expressions that raise consciousness and drive social and cultural change.

events.name: In Conversation: The Rt. Hon. Helen Clark & Hon. Philip Woollaston
events.venue: Mapua Community HallMāpua, Tasman Region
events.long_description:
Overview
The people, politics and ideas that shaped New Zealand’s conservation legacy, hosted by West Coast-Tasman Labour candidate, Rory Paterson.
As New Zealand debates proposed changes to our conservation laws, there has never been a better time to hear from two people who played a pivotal role in shaping our conservation history.
Join former Prime Minister and former Conservation Minister, the Rt. Hon. Helen Clark, and former Minister of Conservation and former Nelson mayor, Hon. Philip Woollaston, for a special lunchtime conversation exploring the people, politics and ideas that shaped modern conservation in New Zealand.
Helen and Philip were New Zealand’s second and third Conservation Ministers, respectively.
Drawing on their first-hand experience, they will reflect on the vision, challenges and decisions behind some of New Zealand's most significant conservation legislation and discuss the legacy it continues to leave today.
The conversation will be facilitated by Johny O'Donnell and hosted by West Coast-Tasman Labour candidate, Rory Paterson.
Bring your lunch, bring your curiosity, and enjoy an engaging discussion, with plenty of time for audience questions.
Admission is free. Koha at the door is appreciated.
We’ll also have raffles and a silent auction, so bring some cash if you’d like to support our West Coast-Tasman campaign.
Seating reservations on a first-come, first-served basis.

events.name: Tour Toi Māori
events.venue: The Dowse Art MuseumLower Hutt, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview






Exclusive behind-the-scenes tour of The Dowse's collection store, exploring Toi Māori, taonga care, and Things We Don't Talk About.
Go behind the scenes at The Dowse with this tour of our collection store, featuring a special focus on our Toi Māori collection and explore our exhibition, Things We Don't Talk About.
Join Collections Manager Jo Wehrly and Director Karl Chitham for an exclusive look at how we care for, store, and preserve these important taonga.

Things We Don’t Talk About
Land rights, modes of masculinity, rates of incarceration, and the negative impacts of religion are among the topics that are often difficult to discuss. This exhibition draws attention to the challenges faced by Māori communities in Aotearoa through powerful artworks from The Dowse's collection. It highlights unspoken and unheard moments of cultural tension and sadness from recent decades, while also sharing stories of resilience, perseverance, and hope for the future.

Featuring work by 21 artists including Hiria Anderson-Mita, Zena Elliot, Russ Flatt, Ngahuia Harrison, Abigail Aroha Jensen, Rangi Kipa, Maureen Lander, Peata Larkin, Matthew McIntyre Wilson, Fiona Pardington, Michael Parekōwhai, Reuben Paterson, Diane Prince, Ngaroma Riley, Hariata Ropata-Tangahoe, Kereama Taepa, Wi Taepa, Te Mohoao, Terri Te Tau, Areta Wilkinson and Wayne Youle.

//Image: Kereama Taepa, He Pukaea [detail], 2019. Photo: Jess O’Brien

events.long_description:
Raven Mavens CD launch. Be one of the first to hear and see the Raven Mavens Quartette's new music. They will be playing the songs on their new CD as well as some long time favourites.

Since releasing their last album of original songs in 2020 the band has continued to delight audiences throughout Wellington, the Wairarapa and the Kāpiti Coast with their distinctive blend of blues, roots, folk and swing influences.

The Raven Mavens have become renowned for their catchy, blues-infused original songs, written primarily by band leader Cindy Muggeridge. Drawing on her deep roots in blues piano, as well as Latin rhythms and rock ’n’ roll grooves, Cindy's latest collection tells stories of life, love and loss, alongside wry social and political observations. In both performance and recording, she is joined by the exceptional talents of Kate Marshall on vocals, violin, accordion and flute; Marian Carter on vocals, saxophone, clarinet and recorder; and Anje Glindemann on vocals, drums and percussion.

The band is also excited to feature two original compositions by Kate Marshall on this new recording, with Kate taking the lead on piano, supported by the other Mavens.

A unique all-female ensemble, the Raven Mavens Quartette gives every member the opportunity to shine as both instrumentalist and vocalist. Each member is a gifted musician and singer in her own right, but together they create a musical chemistry that is greater than the sum of its parts. Their rich combination of voices and instruments produces a sound more often associated with a much larger ensemble. Audiences can expect humour, passion, warmth and exuberance, all in service of songs that remain firmly at the heart of the performance.

Join the Raven Mavens Quartette for an afternoon celebrating original music, masterful musicianship and the release of a remarkable new collection of songs. Refreshments available for a gold coin.

events.long_description:
Experience the dynamic energy of Fazıl Say’s Space Jump, vividly portraying a thrilling ascent and descent with vibrant rhythms and textures. Schumann’s Piano Trio No. 2 follows, showcasing lyrical warmth and expressive melodies with underlying jovial optimism. The programme features a new work for NZTrio by Keith Moss, melding inventive textures with contemporary flair, before revelling in Reena Esmail’s Piano Trio, a compelling fusion of Indian raags and Western classical traditions, creating a rich and evocative soundscape that bridges diverse musical cultures.

Described as a “national treasure” (NZ Herald), NZTrio He Taonga Wairere is renowned for its eclectic repertoire, outstanding talent and warm kiwi stage presence. Bringing together three incredibly accomplished artists: Amalia Hall (violin), Matthias Balzat (cello) & Somi Kim (piano), every NZTrio performance powerfully reaffirms the importance and cathartic nature of a live musical experience in today’s digital world.

events.long_description:
Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The block starts Mon 24 August and runs for 8 weeks till Mon 12 October, 5.30pm - 8pm.

This class is a mixed-level class, allowing beginners to work alongside advanced students. It is the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

Beginners start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering. Then we move on to making a practice-ring set with a Cabochon stone (cabochon means it has a flat bottom and a smooth domed top) in a Bezel Setting. As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love.

Level 2 students learn to solder more competently on their own using chainmaking as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. They may create a simple stone setting or ring alongside this challenge project so they have something to hone their skills that they are familiar with, as well as taking on a new skill.

Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques. They should prepare to have one or two simple projects they can work on self-directed in class, alongside a challenge project.

This class fee does NOT include materials for any student.

Beginners should expect to spend at least $60 on materials for their ring making project.
All metals and stones as well as quality findings and chains are available for purchase each week in the studio. Students are encouraged to keep their silver scrap and find ways to use it thriftily in future projects!

A note for young makers: those over 12 years are welcome in this class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
Would you like to be able to cook delicious and nutritious Japanese food at home? Let’s have fun cooking attractive and healthy Japanese food together!. All ingredients included in course fee.

We will prepare simple, traditional Japanese home-style meals consisting of rice, soup, and a main dish (Ichijyu-issai). In each class, we'll make a different-flavoured miso soup along with a popular Japanese dish -- for example, teriyaki chicken or tonkatsu (crumbed pork cutlet).

We'll introduce you to Japanese food that's easy to prepare, tasty, and made with simple fresh ingredients plus we'll show you how easy it is to incorporate tasty and healthy Japanese food into your daily diet.
All ingredients are included in the fee. You just need to bring an apron, a dish cloth, a tea towel, and a container to take your food home in. Don't forget your smartphone if you want to take photos!

By the end of the course, you’ll:

become more familiar with using Japanese ingredients
feel more confident to cook authentic Japanese-style dishes at home
have the know-how to make delicious, well-balanced, and nourishing meals for the whole family.

Note: Our cooking courses are designed to provide a collaborative and immersive learning experience where learners often work in pairs and/or groups. While we wish to create an inclusive environment for all participants, it is important to note that our courses are unable to accommodate specific food allergies or deviate from the preplanned dishes and menus.

events.venue: The Opera House, 113/111 Manners Street
events.long_description:
Calling all burger lovers. Class is in session as world-renowned smash burger expert George Motz brings a masterclass to Visa Wellington On a Plate. George has devoted his life to the humble burger, tracing its origins from 13th-century Mongolia to its current place as an American staple. He has made films, written books, and even taught university courses dedicated to the dish. In 2023, he opened Hamburger America in Manhattan, a tribute to regional burger styles and the stories behind them. Now he is bringing that knowledge to this burger loving city, at the bottom of the world, to share with all of you.

On stage, George will guide the audience through his ‘History of the Burger’. Expect a few surprises, along with the kind of detail only a ‘burger scholar’ can deliver. 

For the main event, George will cook his take on the Oklahoma onion burger live, sharing the methods that have earned him a global following. Every step is projected overhead, so you will not miss a thing. From the sizzling onions to the final stack, it is part cooking demo, part storytelling session, and a celebration of a classic. 

The evening wraps up with a Q & A, giving you the chance to ask George about his travels, techniques, and favourite burger joints. 

Whether you are a dedicated burger fan or just curious about what makes a great one, this is a chance to hear from one of the world’s leading voices on the subject.

Your ticket includes the presentation, live cooking demonstration and Q&A. No food will be served. A cash bar and merch will be available to purchase on the night.

This International Chef Collaboration is proudly supported by the New Zealand Government’s Events Boost Fund.

events.long_description:
Overview

A provocation from inside and outside: addressing New Zealand’s systems challenges

Join us for the next lecture in our current seminar series

Over recent decades, New Zealand policy making in most areas has been focused on the short-term: often political claims for solutions have been over-simplified. This has contributed to citizen’s cynicism and a decline in institutional trust which puts at risk the social cohesion which has been one of New Zealand’s greatest assets. Most evident is the continued failure to really lift productivity and reach a trajectory like other small, advanced economies.

The challenges ahead of us include: a big demographic shift in age and composition and the need for a more complete population strategy, the failure to systematically understand the opportunities in the rapid technology revolution underway in both the digital/AI and life sciences, an inevitable shift in the nature of higher education, a persistent failure of Auckland to demonstrate a comparative agglomeration effect, a failure to maximise international partnerships beyond trade and security, and a continued naive exceptionalism with regard to science and research. At the policy level this is reflected in a relative lack of the use of the tools of long-term thinking including anticipatory foresight and formative evaluation and continued siloed and short-term biases in the budget process.

Our guest speaker - Sir Peter Gluckman, founder of Koi Tū: Centre for Informed Futures and the President of International Science Council - will address each of these provocations.

About this event

This will be a hybrid event. Please use this site to register if you plan to attend it in person.

If you would like to attend it virtually, please use THIS LINK to register.

About the presenter

Sir Peter Gluckman ONZ KNZM FRSNZ FRS is founder of Koi Tu: Centre for Informed Futures (a non-partisan thinktank focused on long-term and complex issues facing New Zealand), president of the International Science Council and member of the Prime Minister’s Science, Innovation and Technology Advisory Council. Former President of the International Network for Government Science Advice and chief science advisor to the Prime Ministers of New Zealand (2009-2018). He chaired both the recent Science System Advisory Group and the University Advisory Group.

He is a biomedical and clinical scientist who has published over 750 scientific papers and was awarded the Rutherford Medal in 2001 and has written extensively on the science policy and science diplomacy interfaces. He is the recipient of the American Association for the Advancement of Science medal for science diplomacy.

About this seminar series

New ideas, robust evidence, and insights from leading thinkers are crucial to strengthening the Treasury’s economic analysis and policy advice. Our new guest lecture theme — Navigating Global Shifts: Resilience, Challenges and Opportunities for New Zealand — invites us to reflect on how Aotearoa New Zealand can navigate an increasingly complex and interconnected global environment.

This series explores the major global forces that shape our economic landscape, including evolving trade relationships, geopolitical developments, and the global movement of people, capital, and ideas. Through these discussions, we aim to deepen our understanding of how New Zealand can build economic resilience, respond effectively to uncertainty, and harness our regional and international partnerships to support economic performance, productivity, and our living standards.

Our speakers explore strategies for mitigating the impacts of global disruptions — from pandemics and climate‑related events to geopolitical tensions and supply‑chain shocks – while also examining potential opportunities presented by rapid technological shifts, digital economy, and global innovations, to name a few. The series considers the role of government in supporting economic transitions, strengthening national resilience, and ensuring that New Zealand remains well‑positioned to meet emerging global opportunities. By bringing together diverse perspectives, this series seeks to inspire new ways of thinking about New Zealand’s economic future and to support informed, forward‑looking policymaking.

Please note that the views, opinions, findings, and conclusions expressed in the Treasury Guest Lecture Series are those of the individual presenters. They do not necessarily reflect the views of the New Zealand Treasury or the New Zealand Government.

For updates and our latest research visit: www.treasury.govt.nz

Keep in touch

If you would like to be the first to hear about our upcoming events in the Treasury Guest Lecture Series, please SUBSCRIBE to stay up to date.

events.long_description:
This class is beginner level only, with each student following the class project.

It starts Tue 25 August and runs for 8 weeks ill Tue 13 October, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Our popular weeknight classes are the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

The stone-setting process teaches you many fundamental techniques in one project!

We start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering.

Then we move on to making a practice ring set with a Cabochon stone (a cabochon has a flat bottom and a smooth, domed top) in a Bezel Setting.

As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love. This way, you will learn the basics as you go on your practice ring, before taking the next step in costly silver.

This class has all materials included in the class fee!

Each student receives a carefully curated materials pack including copper or brass, sterling and fine silver for your ring-making projects, as well as two stones from our supply so you get a good stone for your level of experience.

We have loads of gorgeous stones of a range of colours, and they are all appropriate for beginner settings.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, Afterpay or PayPal on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)

events.long_description:
Overview

From Scarlatti to Schubert: The Evolution of the Piano Sonata. Acclaimed pianist Christian Leotta in a remarkable recital.

The Italian Embassy is delighted to present internationally acclaimed pianist Christian Leotta in a recital exploring the remarkable evolution of the piano sonata through the music of Domenico Scarlatti, Ludwig van Beethoven, and Franz Schubert.

Spanning more than a century of musical innovation, the programme traces the transformation of the sonata from Scarlatti's elegant miniatures to Beethoven's groundbreaking masterpieces and Schubert's poetic lyricism. Featuring Beethoven's celebrated "Waldstein" Sonata and his final Piano Sonata in C minor, Op. 111, this recital offers a compelling journey through some of the greatest works ever written for the piano.

Renowned for his interpretations of the Classical and Romantic repertoire, Christian Leotta rose to international prominence at the age of 22 after performing the complete cycle of Beethoven's 32 Piano Sonatas. Since then, he has appeared in more than 50 countries and performed with leading orchestras in many of the world's most prestigious concert halls.

events.name: We're Weird for Other Reasons | BATS Theatre
events.venue: BATS Theatre,1 Kent Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
We're Weird for Other Reasons | BATS Theatre
We’re Weird for Other Reasons is a world-first theatre show entirely created by members of New Zealand’s ace/aro/aspec community. This is a joyful and insightful exploration of our varied experiences of the asexual and aromantic spectrums, brought to the stage for our community, friends, the curious and kind.

After critically acclaimed and sold out shows at Auckland Pride and Wellington Pride/NZ Fringe, We're Weird for Other Reasons returns! Part documentary, part sketch show, this is a fun, theatrical, empowering and enlightening celebration of identities that are often underrepresented through performance.

Free Workshop: As part of the season we are offering a free workshop for aspec (asexual and/or aromantic) and questioning folks to discuss and explore aspec identities and experiences in an affirming and gentle space. Offered by Dr James Wenley (Te Herenga Waka-Victoria University of Wellington) and the team behind We’re Weird for Other Reasons', this workshop will involve playful prompts and exercises for us to connect and share in community.

Audio Description is available at all performances, with a touch tour offered 30 minutes before each performance. Please email to let us know you’re attending.

NOTE: There is no performance of WWFOR on Wednesday 26 August. Instead there will be a one-night-only reprise of Austin Harrison's award-winning comedy show "F^CKING ACE"!

Book tickets to both shows for just $35 as a double-pass!

“A healthy antidote and an invitation to broaden your awareness, not to mention your humanity....it’s a gift. And it’s also a rattling good show.”
John Smythe, Theatreview

events.id: Wines of Poland-Noble Rot Wine Bar, 6 Swan Lane-WOAP
events.name: Wines of Poland
events.venue: Noble Rot Wine Bar, 6 Swan Lane
events.long_description:
Poland's wine scene barely appears on most people's radar, which is exactly the point.  For this special evening, Noble Rot sommelier Maciej Zimny turns the spotlight toward his homeland’s emerging wine scene and the wider momentum of Eastern Europe.

Four courses of refined Polish culinary tradition will be served, each dish interpreted with precision to complement the wines and let them shine. Maciej shares his personal story throughout, the vineyard sites he knows, the producers finding their voice, the momentum building across a region that's changing in real time. This will be a wine education that feels more like conversation rather than lecture. Guided by Maciej’s passion for Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, alongside varieties long enjoyed across Eastern Europe, guests will be the first in New Zealand to taste bottles imported specifically for this event. Expect cool-climate purity, bright acidity, and distinctive expressions from a region finding its voice with growing confidence. 

Your ticket includes an amuse-bouche on arrival, four courses, six matched Polish wines, and Maciej's personal guidance.

events.id: Love Bites-Beach Babylon, 232 Oriental Parade-WOAP
events.name: Love Bites
events.venue: Beach Babylon, 232 Oriental Parade
events.long_description:
Modern dating is a minefield, so Beach Babylon and local comedians Neil Thornton and Anya Rzhevitskaya have turned it into a laugh-filled dining event not to be missed. 

Love Bites is a three-course comedy dinner centred on the chaos of modern relationships: red flags you clocked and ignored, situationships you still can't explain, and texts that should've stayed in drafts. Across the night, Neil, and Anya will take very different angles on love and dating as the courses land, from early sparks and suspicious charm through to full-blown hindsight. The menu mirrors the arc perfectly: entrées spark connection (think love bombing fondue and I'm hooked prawns), mains explore the situationship (steak with main character energy or fish soft launches), and dessert brings the happily ever after. It's loose, social, and just self-aware enough. 

Your ticket includes three courses and a welcome cocktail. Additional drinks available for purchase.

Delicious traditional Indian dishes (not based on ghee and cream!) are the focus in this four-session course where Manjula will share with you the recipes, flavours and aromas she grew up with.

events.name: Distilled Comedy
events.venue: The Bond Store,3C Magrath Ave, Paraparaumu Beach, Paraparaumu 5032, New Zealand, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
Distilled Comedy
The monthly merriment kicks off on August 26th — and winter's almost over but the laughs will keep coming.

Welcome to the comedy open mic that politely asks structure to wait outside while we set fire to it.

This is the Home of The Jar — our slightly unhinged, deeply democratic system where the audience randomly selects who goes up next. No lineups. No pecking order. No sacred cows. Just brave humans, questionable decisions, and whatever name comes out of the jar. It’s equal parts comedy show, social experiment, and mild psychological thriller.

You might see a first-timer stepping up for their debut. You might see a seasoned comic testing fresh material. You might see someone absolutely smash it. You might see someone realise, in real time, that jokes are harder than they look. That’s the magic.

Come in from the cold winter weather, grab some food, sip a cocktail, and settle in. The room fills fast, the energy builds quicker, and being there from the start means you’re fully invested when the jar starts causing trouble.

If you love comedy in its rawest, most unpredictable form — this is your night.
If you’ve ever thought, “I could probably do that” — the jar would love to meet you.

Cheap laughs. Big vibes. Absolute chaos.

events.long_description:
Air Force Band Masterworks
Renowned for its breathtaking ensemble playing and military precision, the RNZAF Band will perform music by some of the greatest composers of all time, including Mahler and Strauss.

Returning to the Gillies Group Theatre for the first time in nine years, the band will present a compelling collection of works under the accomplished artistic direction of Bandmaster Warrant Officer Ben Robertson. The programme also features music by Grammy-nominated composer and flautist Valerie Coleman, along with New Zealand composer Georgina Palmer and masters of the concert band genre, Frank Ticheli and James Barnes.

Don’t miss this opportunity to hear New Zealand’s premier military band perform awe-inspiring works in the intimate setting of Whirinaki Whare Taonga.

events.id: Field to Feast-Mangaroa Farms, 298 Whitemans Valley Road-WOAP
events.name: Field to Feast
events.venue: Mangaroa Farms, 298 Whitemans Valley Road
events.long_description:
Set on a working regenerative farm just outside Wellington, this long-table dinner brings you as close to the land that produced your meal as possible. The vegetables and pasture-raised meat will come directly from Mangaroa Farms and other local suppliers, shared in a cosy winter-dinner setting designed to spark conversation, curiosity, and connection around food. This is an interactive dinner experience that blends food, conversation, poetry, live music and inner-enquiry into one cohesive experience.
You're welcomed with whakawhanaungatanga, a warm welcome drink and canapés to acquaint your taste buds to the land. You'll gather in the yurt for a multi-course regenerative meal, with stories from the farmers and producers who grew the food. Woven through the evening will be live music from Casual Healing, poetry and reflective questions to open the table. Designed to foster a single, focused conversation, this Jeffersonian style dinner invites conversation across the table. You'll talk with strangers and leave with friends. 

Your ticket includes a snack and drink on arrival, a multi-course farm-sourced dinner complete with fresh baked bread, local sides and dessert with non-alcoholic beverages throughout the evening.

events.id: Certified Lego® Serious Play® Change Facilitator (Wellington)-Regus - Wellington, Willis StreetWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
events.name: Certified Lego® Serious Play® Change Facilitator (Wellington)
events.venue: Regus - Wellington, Willis StreetWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview
A first level qualification in Lego Serious Play with its usual twist of change magic added into the learning experience
Lego® Serious Play® is a world recognized hands on technique for facilitating the exploration of challenges, using unique approaches with inclusive groups as they tackle the ups and downs of personal and professional development opportunities.
This workshop will focus on building your skills as a Lego® Serious Play® (LSP1.0) facilitator.
In day 1 you will be introduced to the benefits of the approach and learn the three core elements of LSP: challenge, build and share for individual, group and connected building. We will also explore the needs for clarity of challenge and using LSP to help define that challenge as well as potential for coaching and facilitating others through change.
In day 2 you will learn how to apply the day 1 learning through practical application of the learning as well as define a workshop and practice facilitating an activity individually and with others. Certification will be awarded to attendees who complete the workshop content and successfully deliver a short, facilitated workshop event at the end of Day 2.
All attendees will go away with an information booklet and guide for undertaking LSP themselves and a Lego Exploration pack.
Read less

events.long_description:
Overview





Learn the skills, approaches and techniques needed to effectively plan and successfully facilitate a workshop.
Description
The purpose of this course is to provide participants with the skills needed to successfully facilitate a workshop. This course provides an approach and techniques for the effective planning and running of workshops.
Greater emphasis is being placed on skilled business and digital professionals who have the ability to communicate strongly, engage with stakeholders, and elicit a clear result from your team. Workshop facilitation skills, and increasingly online facilitation skills, have never been more important.

The skills and techniques taught on this course will be applicable to all types of workshops. Course participants undertake a realistic workshop facilitation exercise, to reinforce the principles and techniques learnt during the course.

The ‘Workshop Facilitation’ course is delivered by seasoned Equinox consultant practitioners who apply the techniques and practices presented in this course on a daily basis.

Outline
Introduction
Working agreement
Keys to success
Preparation
Workshop facilitation exercise
During the workshop
Risks and mitigations
Follow up
Online facilitation
Retrospective

Learning outcomes
Following the completion of this course, students will be able to:
Have greater awareness of themselves as a workshop facilitator
Understand a process for preparing and running a workshop
Understand the rationale, justification, and roles for workshops
Learn the intricacies of workshop planning
Have applied the techniques for effectively running a workshop

Audience
The audience for this course is business and digital professionals who get involved in producing results through facilitation.

Prerequisites
There are no prerequisites for this course.

events.name: Printmaking - Drypoint & Collagraph
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Explore the technique of drypoint printmaking in this four week course. We will play with tone and textures to create hand crafted prints for you to take away. This course is for complete beginners and those with printmaking experience who want to broaden their skill set.

In this workshop you will

- Learn the versatile process whereby one etches(scratches) directly onto a polycarbonate plate using specific etching tools.
- Learn how to ink your plate and use the press
- Create multiple editions and or variations from your plate
- Learn to create atmospheric images with the application of inks
- Build a Collagraph plate with textured card and found items to create prints with rich colour and depth.

Basic materials included.

events.name: Between the Lines: Outsider with New Zealand String Quartet
events.venue: Ngā Pou Ruahine, Level 2, Te Matapihi, 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This event will take place in Bleachers, Ground Floor of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library.

The theme of our August musical book club is outsider.

Between the Lines is a monthly early-evening chamber music series and book club that brings music and literature into conversation. Presented in the beautiful setting of Ngā Pou Ruahine in Te Matapihi, the series invites audiences to listen, think, and talk. No prior knowledge of music or literature is required, just a curious mind.

Taking place monthly from April to October on the final Thursday of each month, Between the Lines has been co-created by New Zealand String Quartet, Orchestra Wellington, and New Zealand School of Music. Each month these organisations will take turns presenting a talented group of musicians to perform music and host discussion on a different literary theme. From devil’s bargains to language games, the obsessive tortured artist to the intimate private lives of writers and composers, this book club will delve deep into themes that span across artforms.

Each session will feature carefully selected music and a reading list highlighting the theme of the month. So, arrive solo or bring your book club to Te Matapihi for a new kind of conversation.


The theme of our August musical book club is outsider.

Music to be performed:
John Dowland | Flow My Tears
Fanny Mendelssohn | String Quartet in Eb Major
Erwin Schulhof | Five pieces for String Quartet
Florence Price | Five Folksongs in Counterpoint

History is littered with artists who stood apart from society, and this month’s musical book club explores some of these outsiders. From Dowland’s melancholic reflection as a religious minority, to Fanny Mendelssohn’s struggle as a woman composing and performing in a male-dominated time, Schulhoff’s political persecution and eventual death in the Wülzburg concentration camp, and Price’s struggle as a Black woman in early 20th-century America.


Explore the rest of the series:

Thursday 30 April, 5:30pm - Orchestra Wellington - The Art of Conversation (first & second sessions to take place on Ngā Paiaka/ Bleachers on Te Papa Whenua/ Ground Floor)
Thursday 28 May, 5:30pm - New Zealand String Quartet - Obsession (first & second sessions to take place on Ngā Paiaka/ Bleachers on Te Papa Whenua/ Ground Floor)
Thursday 25 June, 5:30pm - New Zealand String Quartet - Private Lives
Thursday 30 July, 5:30pm - Orchestra Wellington - The Devil's Bargain
Thursday 27 August, 5:30pm - New Zealand String Quartet - Outsider
Thursday 24 September, 5:30pm - NZSM - Te Kōkī - Theme to be announced
Thursday 29 October, 5:30pm - Orchestra Wellington - Language Games
