events.name: Jewellery-making On Thursdays, 8-week Block, Level 2+
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The course starts on Thursday 27 August and runs for 8 weeks till Thursday 15 October, 5.30pm-8pm.

This class is designed for students who already have some skills and are ready to develop their craftsmanship in a lively, warm, and supportive environment. Guided by our highly skilled tutors, you’ll build confidence, refine your techniques, and gain the satisfaction of making jewellery that reflects your personal style.

If you’re brand new to jewellery making, we recommend beginning with our Tuesday Evening 8-Week Beginners’ Block, which gives a solid foundation in essential techniques before moving on to this class.

At Level 2, the focus is on precision and technique. Students explore the art of chain making, a classic jewellery making project that develops fine soldering skills and accuracy in construction. This project is an excellent way to build confidence with the torch and create a piece of jewellery that is both functional and beautiful. The finished chain can become a pendant, bracelet, or necklace, or you may choose to adapt it into a design of your own.

At Level 3 and above, the emphasis shifts toward creativity and design development. Students at this stage are encouraged to take on more complex projects, experiment with new and challenging techniques, and bring their own design ideas to life. With the guidance of our skilled and supportive tutors, you’ll learn how to push your skills further, problem-solve during the making process, and refine your eye for detail and design.

Evening classes are not just about the technical side of jewellery making - they are also a chance to slow down, enjoy the process, and be part of a creative community. Many students return term after term, finding the rhythm of regular making both mindful and rewarding.

Please note: this class does not include a materials allowance, giving you the flexibility to choose your own metals, stones, or other materials. You only pay for what you use, making it easier to customise your projects and work at your own pace.

Our booking system asks for full payment at the time of registration (via credit card, PayPal, or AfterPay). If you don’t have access to these options or would like to pay in instalments, please email us and we’ll happily arrange an alternative.

This course helps small business owners and entrepreneurs unlock the full potential of social media. Each week we’ll cover practical steps to review your current channels, set up strong profiles, and create a tailored content plan that works for your business. You’ll learn how to choose the right platforms, use hashtags effectively, create engaging posts, select visuals that connect with your audience, and understand the role of AI tools. By the end, you’ll walk away with a clear and actionable plan to grow your social media channels and attract the right customers.
Whether you’re starting out or already running a business, a strong social media presence is no longer optional. The challenge is knowing where to focus your efforts when every platform seems to demand something different.
This course is designed to cut through the noise and give you a roadmap that fits your business. Together, we’ll:
Review the main platforms and choose the right ones for your goals
Tailor your profiles so they look professional and trustworthy
Build a realistic content plan you can actually stick to
Learn how to use hashtags and trends to boost reach
Explore how AI can help (and where it can’t)
Understand what visuals work best and how to avoid common pitfalls
Discuss tips for creating engagement and growing a loyal following
The focus is practical and hands-on. Each week you’ll apply the ideas directly to your own business, so by the end of the course you’ll have a solid social media strategy ready to put into action.

events.id: We are not one people: From Parihaka to a Pākehā myth-National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: We are not one people: From Parihaka to a Pākehā myth
events.venue: National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington
events.long_description:
On the morning of the 5th November 1881, an Irishman called Andrew Gilhooly formed up alongside other members of the Armed Constabulary at the entrance to Parihaka pā; he was there for the invasion, the occupation and — much later — for the farming of land taken from Taranaki iwi.

But those events dropped out of the family stories handed down to Gilhooly’s descendants; neither do they feature in national narratives of fairness, egalitarianism and equal treatment.

In this presentation, Richard Shaw, one of Gilhooly’s descendants, will explore the relationship between historical amnesia amongst (some) descendants of settler families and the stories we tell each other of the nation we live in.

What if creating a better future starts with rethinking the way we live today?

FREE EVENT: Join us for an evening of conversation, connection, kai, and practical ideas for building more sustainable and resilient communities.

Who is this for? Anyone interested in creating a more sustainable and resilient future, whether you're already taking action or simply wondering where to start.

We'll bring together leaders, changemakers, and community voices to explore:

🌿 What can we actually do at home?
🌏 How can we build stronger, more resilient communities?
💡 What new ideas and innovations are making sustainable choices easier?

7:00–8:00 PM: Kai, connection & networking




Talanoa for Tomorrow is taking place across four Wellington sessions, with a different panel of speakers at each event.




We are excited to announce for this session we have:

Andrew Wilks is the Manutaki (Director) of Sustainability at Te Herenga Waka – Victoria University of Wellington, leading efforts to embed sustainability and climate action across the University. He is passionate about helping people and organisations take practical action on climate change, build resilience, and create positive futures for their communities.

Dr. Nate Rigler is the Project Lead for the collaborative Kia Mouriora Te Kaiwharawhara Sanctuary to Sea initiative, led by Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne. With a PhD in Pacific Studies and a deep passion for urban biodiversity, Nate works to connect local communities and businesses with native ecosystem restoration in Te Kaiwharawhara water catchment.

Inangaro Vakaafi - Pacific Climate Warriors

Joshua Peauafi is a Pacific leader, social impact advocate, and co-founder of Potplant Studio. Passionate about relational leadership, diversity, equity, and inclusion, Joshua uses nature and plants as a vehicle to spark meaningful conversations around wellbeing, mental health, and community connection across Aotearoa New Zealand.

All our events are in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip as you create! At the end of the night you will leave with your own fluro painting and a fun memory to go with it.

events.long_description:
The Wayside, Seismic State, and Dead Cherry at Valhalla!
Wellington rockers The Wayside, Seismic State, and Dead Cherry hit the Valhalla stage together for the first time. Individually they are electric, collectively they are not to be missed.
Bring your party attitude and your dancing shoes, this show is not to be missed!
Get your tickets now at Under The Radar, door sales also available.
The Wayside:
The Wayside's unique blues rock sound has a groove that gets the room moving. Recent New Zealand Battle of the Band's National Finalists, their high energy performances are punctuated by sick licks and soaring vocals.
Seismic State:
High-octane alt-rock with a blues-funk soul.
A staple of the New Zealand rock circuit, the Wellington quartet is known for a professional, high-energy live show. Since the release of their debut EP State of Things, which earned international airplay and a Top 58 spot on The Generator FM’s Kiwi 101, the band has consistently anchored bills at iconic venues including San Fran and Valhalla.
Their pedigree includes support slots for AMA award winners Dead Favours on their Riffing & Yelling tour, Seismic State delivers a sophisticated performance built for the big stage.
Dead Cherry:
Dead Cherry are are making waves with their high energy slice of old school rock ‘n roll, keeping it raw and real. Their debut EP Mother was released late last year.

Get ready for a night of fun and connection at WELLINGTON'S hottest speed dating event!
Let’s ditch the apps together and embrace real connections. Say goodbye to the dating apps and hello to your very own Cheeky Love Story!
What’s included: Your first drink is on us—let’s toast to great company!
How It Works:
Before the event:
If you have the App store on your phone make sure to download the Cheeky Events App to set up your profile and upload a photo. The app is not avilable yet on Google Store so if you have a Google phone then save and use this web browser link instead to enter who you like and receive any matches:
https://app.cheekyeventsaustralia.com/

P.S. Don’t worry—it’s not a dating app! We’ve skipped the chat feature because we’re all about real, in-person connections.
During the event:
Check in to grab your name tag and free drink token.
Arrive on time to enjoy 15 minutes of casual pre-mingling.
Ladies stay seated while men rotate every 5 minutes—don’t forget to rate your matches in the app!
Take a quick 15-minute break before the next round.
After the rotations, feel free to stick around for some extra socializing!
After the event: Stay for extra mingling and check the app for your cheeky matches 12 hours later!

events.long_description:
Starring Eugene Wolfin on vocals, the octet will present a fizzing set of big band swing, Broadway hits, and gorgeous ballads. Hear the fine lyricism of the 20th century sung by one of Wellington’s most exciting performers.

Free entry! Koha encouraged.

For the last 8 years vocalist Eugene Wolfin has been a regular of Wellington music scene performing in a wide variety of genres including Jazz, Blues, and Rock ’n’ Roll. He has had a hand in a few local Musical Theatre productions performing lead roles in ‘Chess’ and the modern hit ‘If/Then', and is a regular in front of Jazz Orchestras including the Royal New Zealand Air Force Band and the Rodger Fox Big Band.

Traskforce! is bandleader Alex Trask’s most swinging musical organisation. They play fresh arrangements of original compositions, classic swing, and Broadway ballads. This includes songs from the Basie repertoire, Bob Mintzer, Oliver Nelson, Quincey Jones, and Lionel Bart's Oliver! to name a few. The five horn arrangements allow for the power of a big band and the subtlety of a quartet to shine side by side. The band is made up of Wellington’s top players, including members of the Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra, the RNZAF band, NZSM faculty, and rising stars.

events.long_description:
Warm yourself in the heart of winter with a vibrant Lunar New Year feast. Let the Dragons team bring colour, flavour, and good fortune to a midwinter banquet designed to brighten the season. 

The table seats ten, your neighbours, your friends, strangers who are about to become familiar. Everyone stands to toss the Yu Sheng prosperity salad high into the air, and the chaos and laughter start. Then ten courses unfold: eight savoury dishes, each one imbued with symbolic meaning. Golden chicken for family unity. Whole fortune duck for fidelity. Crispy fish for abundance. Long-life noodles for longevity. It's food, luck, and togetherness served at once and you'll leave feeling blessed not only for the meal, but for this convivial and communal celebration. 

Your ticket includes the full ten-course shared banquet, a lion dance performance, and beverages throughout: welcoming tea, and three beers per guest.

events.long_description:
Overview

Get ready to boost your confidence, and your speaking game, and learn how to leave a lasting impression every time you talk.

Speak with Confidence, Speak with Clarity, Speak with Impact




How we communicate shapes how people experience us, how well our ideas are understood and, ultimately, the influence we are able to have.

In this practical and highly interactive workshop, communication specialist and keynote speaker Monique Bradley helps participants develop the confidence to use their voice, the clarity to know what they want to say, and the skills to communicate in a way that connects with other people and creates impact.

Participants will explore some of the most common challenges around speaking and presenting, including nerves, uncertainty about what to say, how to structure a message, how to keep an audience engaged and how to deliver with greater confidence and presence.

Monique introduces simple, practical techniques for managing nerves, structuring presentations, strengthening vocal delivery and using stories to make ideas more engaging and memorable. The session also explores communication as a form of influence and challenges participants to think intentionally about how they want to be experienced and remembered by others.

The focus throughout is not perfection. It is building competence through practice, developing greater self-belief and learning how to communicate with confidence, clarity and genuine human connection. The workshop closes on Monique’s core principle: confidence is built through competence, and competence is built through repetition.

Participants will leave with:
practical tools for managing nerves and speaking anxiety
a simple way to structure what they want to say
techniques for improving pace, pitch, projection and pronunciation
greater awareness of how stories create connection and influence
practical experience speaking and practising their delivery
a clearer understanding of the impact they want their communication to have
Read less

events.name: Sea Shanty Society EP Release Tour
events.venue: Abandoned Taproom Petone, 38 Fitzherbert St, Petone, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
The scuttlebutt is true...

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor-squall of pure shanty.

Singalong shanties! Nautical games! Best dressed prizes!

Limited tickets.

Live review from Maryanne Cathro:

"Having been handed a booklet of lyrics... we grab seats around the edge ... It’s all very casual, with the added delight of people dressed as sailors in striped tops and white hats, pirate hats and newspaper hats, and even life jackets! It’s like they know what is about to happen!

As the band takes to the stage... a spotlight falls upon storyteller Louis Tait. Microphone in hand, he starts to weave a tale of the sea, to riffs of music from the band.

Back to those booklets of lyrics – this whole show is a singalong, and it is with great enthusiasm that the first shanty begins...the audience sings and stomps and laughs.

It’s hard to describe the impact of stadium concert-level audience euphoria in a small community hall, yet that is what it is. Bopping bodies, bathed in coloured light, so into the music, which is just fantastic in every way. The dance area is more like an ecstatic mosh pit.

What is it about shanties? They came out of shared singing, and so they lend themselves to this, I guess. But what Vorn Dont le Père Etait Marin and Lake Davineer bring to these songs is a thoroughly modern, old-fashioned sense of fun and magic.

I am reserving specific comment for the currently most famous shanty in their repertoire, ‘The Wellerman’... The crowd goes wild! The stomping probably puts the hall onto Geonet. I would not have been surprised if a giant cracken had appeared and body-surfed the crowd."

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

events.name: Escarpment Launch & Long Lunch
events.venue: Boomrock Lodge, 292 Boom Rock Road
events.long_description:
Be one of the first in the country to taste the 2023 vintage single vineyard wines from Martinborough's Pinot Noir superstars, Escarpment. From the gravels and windswept terraces of Martinborough, Escarpment has built a devoted following through word of mouth, shared by locals, championed by sommeliers, and remembered long after the last glass. 

Presented by winemaker Tim Bourne against the wild outlook of Boomrock's coastal position, you'll sample their wines paired with locally sourced wild ingredients including wild boar, Cook Strait snapper, tītī (mutton bird), venison, and Wairarapa cheese. 

The afternoon opens with Rosé on arrival and canapés of wild boar arancini and ceviche, then moves to a three-course long lunch. Expect leek, tītī, and Mānuka honey pasta with kawa kawa butter; tart cherry venison loin with purple kūmara gratin and Kikorangi Blue; and a Wairarapa cheese course with dark chocolate and blackberry jelly. Each course is matched with Escarpment's range, celebrating the magic of Wairarapa. Your ticket also includes return bus transport.

events.long_description:
Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society EP release show - Pito One
We didn't forget about the Hutt...Tickets on sale now: https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/gig/103515/Never-Mind-The-Rowlocks-Heres-The-Wellington-Sea-Shanty-Society-EP.utr

The wave doesn’t conform to the shape of the rock. It smashes it. The sea doesn’t pretend to be hospitable. It summons courage. And a shantyband never licks the captain's boot. They release another EP!

The best shanties invite us to open our hearts along with the bottle. To draw strength from camaraderie and drown our pettinesses. To seek the rough edge of the wave and savour the salt within. And so, the WSSS have issued a call to arms with their new collection: Never Mind the Rowlocks, Here’s the Wellington Sea Shanty Society.

Never fear if you find yourself adrift on a sea of AI slop, lapping at your hull, lulling you to sleep — Lake Davineer, Vorn dont Le Père Était Marin, Young Nic, Tomas el Largo, and Louis Quatorze are back again to fill your sails and slap the codfish slime clean off your cheeks.

Just when everyone is lamenting the empty galleys of the good ship Wellington, and those ol’ scurvy-mongers are promising renewed bounty if you would only tack five degrees to port or starboard come election time, these songs remind us the sea at least will sustain us, and there’s rum and (metaphorical) guns for them that wants to fight.

Lin Seal | Wellington Nautical History Monthly

Standing show (Seating reserved for those who need it: ).

⚓⚓⚓

The scuttlebutt is true...⛵

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor squall of pure shanty.


⚓⚓⚓

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

events.id: Keiko Kuwakino + Joe McLeod-Pipitea Marae, 55 Thorndon Quay-WOAP
events.name: Keiko Kuwakino + Joe McLeod
events.venue: Pipitea Marae, 55 Thorndon Quay
events.long_description:
For one night only, two foraging-chefs from opposite ends of the Pacific will bring you - Kai meets Shoku - an all inclusive drinks matched five course meal, with Te Matatini regional winners Te Kapa Haka o Pukeatua and Japanese Taiko drummers Taikoza providing the entertainment. It's an epic event that could only ever happen in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

Pipitea Marae has always been a place of gathering and welcome. For generations, Te Āti Awa ki Te Whanganui-a-Tara has offered manaakitanga to those who arrive by sea, by land, and now, from across the Pacific.

On 29 August, that tradition continues with a dinner bringing together two chefs whose life's work is rooted in the same conviction: that honouring culture and history is best done via the puku.

The story of this harbour is one of guardians, pathways, and the meeting of worlds. Te Āti Awa have long understood that the sea connects rather than separates. What began as a relationship across the Pacific between Te Āti Awa and Japan finds its expression at the table, where two Indigenous cultures share their stories through food.

Chef Joe McLeod (Ngāi Tūhoe) brings more than 40 years' experience as an international chef, alongside six decades spent researching, recording, and reconnecting Mātauranga Kai Māori, returning traditional food knowledge to marae across Aotearoa. One of the foremost authorities on traditional Māori cuisine, Chef Joe's kaupapa is grounded in the belief that food carries whakapapa, and that restoring a people's relationship to their kai is an act of cultural survival.

Chef Keiko Kuwakino travels from Satoyama Jujo in Niigata, Japan, where her Michelin-starred restaurant reflects a practice rooted in wild mountain vegetables, fermentation, and the rhythms of Japan's snow country. Her cooking begins with the land she forages. For Keiko, cuisine starts with the land itself, her role simply to listen carefully to nature and translate its story through food.

Hosted by Te Āti Awa at Pipitea Marae, Kai Meets Shoku is a partnership between Wellington Culinary Events Trust, Te Rūnanganui o Te Āti Awa, and E Kai Māori, supported by MBIE.

Your ticket includes five courses, matched beverages for all courses, and Māori and Japanese entertainment

events.id: Songs from the Deep-Little Beer Quarter, 6 Edward Street-WOAP
events.name: Songs from the Deep
events.venue: Little Beer Quarter, 6 Edward Street
events.long_description:
LBQ drops anchor for one night, trading its usual warmth for something saltier. Long communal tables, low light, rope and timber, and the Pōneke Shanty Club leading the room through some rousing singalongs.
Sea shanties were never written down. They travelled port to port, voice to voice, and that's exactly how the evening works. By the second set the room is carrying the chorus. Between the music, anonymous dockside confessions are read aloud and become part of the night's folklore.

Food is hearty and built for winter: slow-braised beef cheek and dark ale pie, or roasted kūmara and caramelised onion pie to start. Char-grilled market fish or a smoked mushroom and lentil wellington to follow, and a spiced rum sticky pudding or dark chocolate and sea salt tart to close.

Your ticket includes three courses and three drinks. Choose from curated beer, rum, or non-alcoholic ginger beer.

events.id: Hidden Ferments-Chaat Street, 171 Willis Street-WOAP
events.name: Hidden Ferments
events.venue: Chaat Street, 171 Willis Street
events.long_description:
Indian fermentation has long lived in home kitchens and ancient texts, yet rarely takes centre stage in restaurants, especially on the global stage. This collaborative event invites you into that quieter, largely unseen world as chefs Saavni Krishnan and Sriram Aditya from Melbourne's Saadi restaurant, and chef Vaibhav Vishen, from Wellington's Chaat Street, bring a fine-dining lens to India's deep fermentation traditions, set against Wellington's wild, coastal produce. Across an intimate evening, the menu combines age-old techniques and new terroir: cultured grains, pickles, kanji-style ferments, and lacto-preserved fruits.

For both chefs their cooking is rooted in memory and comfort but expressed with restraint, clarity, and precision. Think fermented rice and lentil batters reimagined as delicate snacks, vegetables transformed through lactic fermentation to echo both Indian aachar and Wellington's coastal flora, and broths built on aged, cultured bases for depth and length. The journey traces a loose path from the grain and pulse-based ferments that underpin everyday Indian eating, through preserved vegetables and fruits, to experimental applications responding to Wellington's climate and producers. 

Your ticket includes a five-course tasting menu with thoughtful beverage pairings designed to echo ferment-forward flavours. Non-alcoholic options feature pickled, infused, and cultured elements without overpowering the palate. This event has shared seating.

events.long_description:
Join us for a hands-on experience and discover the rich traditions of taonga tākaro—traditional Māori games that have been played and passed down through generations.

Led by Ness and Pita from Tū Mātau Ora, this interactive workshop invites participants to learn and play a selection of traditional Māori games, including Pōtaka, Poi Toa – Poi Patu, Poi Tauā, I Te Tīmatanga, and Tū Pūhatu.

More than just games, taonga tākaro carry stories, values, and mātauranga Māori, offering a meaningful way to experience te ao Māori through movement, teamwork, strategy, and play.

Whether you're trying these games for the first time or reconnecting with familiar traditions, this welcoming session is a fun and engaging way to connect with others while celebrating the living traditions of Aotearoa.

Learn traditional Māori games
Experience te ao Māori through play
Connect with community
Family-friendly and beginner-friendly

In collaboration with Tū Mātau Ora.

events.long_description:
Getting the Most from AI: Practical Skills for Everyday Use
(NZ Citizens and residents pay $29 with ID, all others pays $120).
AI tools are everywhere, but knowing which one to use — and how to use it well — makes all the difference. In this hands-on workshop, Jon Bell will guide you through practical techniques to make AI a genuinely useful partner in your work and life. Whether you've tried it a few times or use it regularly, you'll leave with real skills you can apply straight away, with no technical background needed.
We'll start with a quick tour of the main tools — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot — so you understand what makes each one different. (They're less different than you might think!) Then we'll spend most of the day going deep on Claude, which Jon considers the easiest to use, while also being the most powerful.
We'll cover real examples, answer your questions as they come up, and spend plenty of time experimenting together.
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
- Write effective prompts that get clearer, more useful responses
- Use AI for research, brainstorming, writing, and creative work
- Understand the differences between the major tools and when to use each
- Recognise the tools' limitations (and how to work around them)
- Apply practical strategies for using AI in your personal or professional projects
- Confidently troubleshoot when AI gives unexpected or unhelpful answers
Please bring: A phone or laptop with ChatGPT and Claude installed and signed in to both. Enough battery to last the day.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Thriving Through Change: Growing Resilience & Cultivating Courage
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
Cultivating true resilience is an intentional practice of the mind, body, and soul. It is rooted in deep self-knowledge and personal empowerment. In our rapidly changing world, the ultimate question we must ask ourselves is: How can I unlock my unique strengths and capacities to not just survive these demanding times, but truly thrive?
By implementing a "living" practice of mindful strategies, creative expression, and physical awareness, we can empower our thinking, elevate our emotional well-being, and bring a renewed vitality to our life's work.
What to Expect
This workshop offers you a rich tapestry of practical tools, storytelling, and collaborative discussion. Together, we will explore diverse pathways to foster courage, helping you shift from a state of survival to one of thriving—even while navigating the daily pressures of stress, grief, anxiety, or the fear of an uncertain future.
What You Will Take Away:
Mindful Strategies: Daily, actionable practices to anchor your thoughts and reduce overwhelm.
Creative & Physical Outlets: Expressive tools to release tension and process complex emotions.
A Personal Roadmap: A clearer understanding of your innate strengths to help you navigate future transitions with confidence.
Details & What to Bring:
Duration: Full-day workshop
What to bring: A personal journal and your favourite pen or pencil. (However, paper and pen will be provided if you need).
Step out of the survival loop. Join us to reclaim your inner strength and cultivate the courage to thrive.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your session.

Bring along a painting and a suitable frame, either a cheapo from Briscoes or a good second hand frame. We will provide all the tools, process and materials to frame your piece of art.
It’s a practical course where you will learn to prepare the frame, cut with a knife, measure and cut a matt with the matt cutter.

- Assembling the tools you need

- Replacing acid leaching materials with foam board
- Cutting techniques
- Making and attaching labels and swing tags
- How to photograph your art

- your artwork to frame
- a suitable frame for the artwork A4 or smaller
- enthusiasm

events.venue: Thistle Hall - UpstairsTe Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview







Fashion waste is one of the Earth's biggest polluters. Let's come together and reduce waste by swapping clothes.
Attend The Clothes Swap and swap up to 10 items that you don't reach for anymore.
How it works:
- Buy a ticket through EventBrite
2 for 1 - $15 (until sold out)
Early bird - $15 (until 30th June or sold out)
General Admission - $20 (1st July until 29th August)
- Bring up to 10 items of clothing that are in good condition - clothing guideline/what to bring below
- Check in your items in 1 hour before the event starts and receive your tokens to swap with. 1 item = 1 token.
- Check in starts at 10am - 11am. The Swap starts at 11:15am - 12:15pm.
- Browse the clothes at the swap event and choose your fabulous new pieces.
- Check out with your tokens and enjoy your new clothes!
- Leftover clothes will be donated
The Clothes Swap Clothing Guidelines
What to bring?
We all want to find good quality clothes to love so we all need to bring good quality clothes to swap.
Please bring garments that are in good condition, not too worn or pilled and with no stains or damage.
Please read our Brand Guidelines via the link below:
https://theclothesswap.mailchimpsites.com/brand-guidelines
Please read our Quality Guidelines via the link below:
https://theclothesswap.mailchimpsites.com/quality-guidelines

When you check in your clothes we’ll have a quick look just to ensure the garments that are coming in are of good quality and are an accepted brand.

Please note: if an item of clothing is an accepted brand but in poor quality, it will not be accepted.
Clothing with no brand labels will also not be accepted.
How to get to Thistle Hall - Upstairs Hall:
The entry to the upstairs hall is around the corner from the entry to the gallery - there'll be a sign. There are stairs inside the door that go up to the upstairs hall which is where the Swap will be or a lift if you need it.

Sound Healing Experience at Tusk Yoga with Claudio
We’re so excited to bring this deeply restorative sound journey to Tusk Yoga for the very first time — an immersive evening of vibration, stillness, and heart-centred connection with multi-instrumentalist Claudio Escutia.

Let yourself be held by the layered tones of Gongs, Crystal and Tibetan singing bowls, Harmonium Native American flutes, and other traditional instruments, all delivered through high-quality audio so the sound is heard *and* felt throughout your entire body.

In this state of deep rest, your nervous system softens, the thinking mind quiets, and you naturally arrive at the heart-mind. Here, silence rises gently through the vehicle of sound itself. 🌿

No yoga or meditation experience is needed — absolutely everyone is welcome.

**What to bring**
Bring your own yoga mat if you like, though studio mats are available. We’ll provide bolsters, blankets, and eye pillows so you can settle in completely.

🎟️ **Booking is essential** — spaces are limited and these events tend to fill quickly. Don’t miss this special first gathering at Tusk Yoga.

Contribution:

General admission : $45


Learn more buy tickets and listen to Claudio’s music here:

https://www.claudioescutia.com/events/sound-healing-experience-at-tusk-yoga-with-claudio

**About Claudio**
Born into a family of musicians in Mexico City and now based in Wellington, Claudio began playing music as a child and later studied classical guitar. His path led him through jazz, world music, and spiritual sound traditions in Montreal, and extensive travels across Asia and Europe deepened his connection with Indian music and yogic philosophy.

He trained in Tibetan singing bowls in Kathmandu and Varanasi, and his work now embraces instruments including sitar, esraj, bansuri, harmonium, flutes, gongs, and voice. Every session is a weave of technical skill, grounded presence, and deep reverence for the healing power of sound.

🎧 Listen & connect:

Niko Ne Zna returns to Vogelmorn Hall for an unforgettable Saturday night of explosive brass, infectious rhythms, delicious food, and music that's impossible to sit still to.

Drawing inspiration from the rich musical traditions of Serbia, Macedonia, Romania, Greece, and beyond, Niko Ne Zna combines soaring brass, driving percussion, passionate multilingual vocals, and original compositions to create a spectacular live experience. Doors open at 5:30 pm, giving you plenty of time to enjoy delicious food and a drink from the fully stocked bar before the music begins. Whether you've been following Niko Ne Zna for years or are experiencing the band for the first time, prepare for an unforgettable evening of exhilarating live music, celebration, and dancing.

events.name: Sea Shanty Society EP Release Tour
events.venue: Raumati South Memorial Hall, 16 Tennis Court Rd, Raumati
events.long_description:
The scuttlebutt is true...

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor-squall of pure shanty.

Singalong shanties! Nautical games! Best dressed prizes!

Limited tickets.

Live review from Maryanne Cathro:

"Having been handed a booklet of lyrics... we grab seats around the edge ... It’s all very casual, with the added delight of people dressed as sailors in striped tops and white hats, pirate hats and newspaper hats, and even life jackets! It’s like they know what is about to happen!

As the band takes to the stage... a spotlight falls upon storyteller Louis Tait. Microphone in hand, he starts to weave a tale of the sea, to riffs of music from the band.

Back to those booklets of lyrics – this whole show is a singalong, and it is with great enthusiasm that the first shanty begins...the audience sings and stomps and laughs.

It’s hard to describe the impact of stadium concert-level audience euphoria in a small community hall, yet that is what it is. Bopping bodies, bathed in coloured light, so into the music, which is just fantastic in every way. The dance area is more like an ecstatic mosh pit.

What is it about shanties? They came out of shared singing, and so they lend themselves to this, I guess. But what Vorn Dont le Père Etait Marin and Lake Davineer bring to these songs is a thoroughly modern, old-fashioned sense of fun and magic.

I am reserving specific comment for the currently most famous shanty in their repertoire, ‘The Wellerman’... The crowd goes wild! The stomping probably puts the hall onto Geonet. I would not have been surprised if a giant cracken had appeared and body-surfed the crowd."

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

events.id: Harvest Moon: Highways, Heartaches and Harmonies-Wairarapa Events Centre, Holloway St, Carterton-Event Finder
events.name: Harvest Moon: Highways, Heartaches and Harmonies
events.venue: Wairarapa Events Centre, Holloway St, Carterton
events.long_description:
Wellington Americana band Harvest Moon returns to the Wairarapa Events Centre in August, renewing a relationship with one of New Zealand’s most enthusiastic country music audiences.

The six-piece band has performed in the region on three previous occasions and says Wairarapa audiences have always responded with warmth, enthusiasm and a genuine appreciation for live country and Americana music.

“There has always been a strong country music culture in the Wairarapa,” says band member Wayne Mills. “Every time we’ve played here we’ve been made to feel very welcome, and we’re looking forward to returning.”

Harvest Moon combines guitars, pedal steel, accordion, banjo, dobro and piano with rich vocal harmonies to create an authentic Americana sound inspired by artists including Johnny Cash, Vince Gill, Brad Paisley, Rodney Crowell and The Mavericks.

Fresh from a sell-out show in New Plymouth’s 4th Wall Theatre, and successful recent performances in Whanganui and Feilding, Harvest Moon continues to attract audiences who appreciate outstanding musicianship, memorable songs and an evening of relaxed entertainment.

“Our shows are about more than just the music,” says Mills. “They’re about sharing great songs, having a few laughs and giving people a couple of hours where they can simply enjoy themselves. We know that’s something Wairarapa audiences have always appreciated.”

It’s 1967, and Judy Garland is back, ready to re-write the narrative and reclaim her legacy after the heartbreak of her previous Australian tour. events.name: Working With Colour workshop
events.venue: Morag Stokes Art Studio, 14 Morepork Drive,39 Awanui Dr, Waikanae 5036, New Zealand, Waikanae
events.long_description:
Working With Colour workshop
This workshop is about mixing colour to produce satisfying and exciting colour combinations in your paintings. We will work with top quality GOLDEN acrylics, and you will learn about how to achieve overall colour harmony in your work. We will also cover working with complimentary colours, ‘loud and quiet’ colours and our personal colour cravings. The workshop will be more about practice than theory, although special attention will be given to colour value (its place on a grey scale) and chroma (brightness). You will also learn about the pigment realities that are often neglected in theory-based colour teaching, in other words, pigment selection for the cleanest and brightest possible mixes. The morning will concentrate on developing your own personal palette and by the afternoon you will be using this palette in an abstract painting inspired by the exciting dance-like colour works of Chinese artist Mimi Chen Ting. We will also take inspiration from the colour works of well-known NZ master colourist Sandy Adsett. Class numbers are limited to 6 and the day is suitable for beginners to art as well as experienced painters. Cost: $180

This year is a major milestone in the history of Wellington Repertory Theatre as it will be 100 years since the establishment of the society and the inaugural production of George Bernard Shaw’s Pygmalion.

To acknowledge this auspicious occasion, we have a commemorative day planned for Saturday August 29th which we would like to invite you to. The venue will be The Gryphon Theatre, 22 Ghuznee Street, Wellington.

The itinerary for the day is as follows:


12 noon – 4 pm: Exhibition of photos and memorabilia. (free entry)
4.00 pm – 4.30 pm: Theatre closed.
4.30 pm – 5 pm: Doors reopens for ticket holders as the official celebration begins.
5 pm – 5.30 pm: Welcome speech, Commemoration, Cutting of the cake
5.30 – 6.30 pm: Canapes and drinks.
6.30 – 7.30 pm: “Through the Decades” (stage performance)
7.30 – 8.30 pm: Informal socialising.
8.30 pm: Official end of the events.


Anyone may visit the Gryphon before 4 pm, but if you want to attend the festivities, you will need to buy a ticket.

A Centenary Celebration ticket costs $35, and gives you access to:
- The Exhibition
- The Cake Cutting and commemoration
- Light Supper
- A free drink (plus cash bar)
- The Performance

Tickets are limited, so book your spot today!

Ticket price includes all food, mahjong tuition and guided play, tea on arrival, and a take-home mahjong guide. Alcohol available to purchase.

events.name: Edible Idioms
events.venue: Lustre Kitchen and Dining, 7-13 Seaview Road
events.long_description:
Language and food belong together, add history and the story deepens into something altogether different. Lustre's taking the words we use every day and turning them into dishes. Cool as a cucumber becomes a palate cleanser, a piece of cake arrives as something entirely new, and every course speaks to the way culture lives in how we talk about food.

Seven courses of interpretation, each one teasing out a different idiom from around the world. There's a German one about sausage and indifference, an Indian one about something fishy in the pulses, moments where the kitchen challenges and entertains in equal measure. One surprise dish waits mid-evening, your job is to guess which idiom it is. The menu shifts with the seasons and the whims of Lustre's local farms, but the game never changes: food as language, language as history.

Your ticket covers the seven-course Lustrous banquet menu and an idiom-inspired arrival drink. Alcohol is available to purchase.

events.id: Kumutoto Kai me te Kōrero-Graze Wine Bar, 95 Upland Road-WOAP
events.name: Kumutoto Kai me te Kōrero
events.venue: Graze Wine Bar, 95 Upland Road
events.long_description:
Kumutoto Awa was one of the living streams of Pōneke long before the city buried it underground in 1866. This four-hour guided hīkoi traces its path from the Kelburn hills to the waterfront, connecting it through kai, kōrero, and the people who are working to restore the place of the awa in the city's future – The Kumutoto Restoration Project. You'll start with a light lunch and cocktail at Graze in Kelburn which will be a collaboration between Chef Max Gordy and the Kumutoto Community Orchard founder and avid forager Milan Magan. You will also meet your hosts Martin and Micheline who will regale you with stories about Wellington's lost streams. From there, the group walks to the only remaining stretch of the Kumutoto stream still visible above ground, where soup waits alongside more kōrero about the whakapapa of the awa. The route then follows the buried path of Kumutoto down the Terrace to Bert's Bar for a final cocktail created with a foraged ingredients from Kumutoto before finishing at the mouth of the awa on the waterfront. All food and drinks across the event are included in your ticket, with ingredients foraged from the Kumutoto Community Orchard and ngahere. Wear comfortable shoes and dress for the weather. The route covers approximately two kilometres and includes steps.
The ticket price includes an optional foraging workshop with Milan Magan. You'll spend an hour in the orchard and ngahere learning about what you'll be eating and drinking the following day. Saturday 1 & 29 August 9-10am.

Blair Morgan & Luca Joass
The Undercurrent presents Blair Morgan & Luca Joass!

Ōtautahi singer-songwriter Blair Morgan brings his original songs to Wellington for a special afternoon performance. Blair's recently released album Sunday River blends folk, Americana and indie influences, telling stories of people, places and journeys. His songs travel from the streets of Lisbon to the west coast of Te Waipounamu, exploring themes of resilience, friendship and home through warm acoustic performances, and engaging storytelling. Performing solo, Blair presents the songs as they were first written- just voice, guitar, harmonica and the stories behind them.

Joining Blair is Wellington singer-songwriter Luca Joass. Known for his heartfelt songwriting and engaging live performances, Luca released his debut single “Young & Free” last year, accompanied by a beautifully crafted music video. As co-founder of Neato Productions, he has also directed several music videos for Blair's Sunday River album.

The return of an annual favourite. Each year, the Winemaker’s Long Lunch brings friends of Noble Rot together around a shared table, and rather than focussing on one region, this time they're welcoming legendary names from across all corners of the New Zealand wine community.
Settle in for an afternoon shaped by conversation, generous hospitality, and wines poured by the people who made them. Winemakers will join you at the table, sharing bottles from their own cellars and the stories behind them. Such as the significant vintages, the vines they grow, and the decisions that define their style. The atmosphere is relaxed and intimate, with time to taste, and ask questions over a glass (or three).
A relaxed three-course long lunch will be served sharing style, thoughtfully designed to complement a line-up of outstanding New Zealand wines poured throughout the afternoon in this fitting celebration of wine and friendship.
Your ticket includes three courses and wines poured throughout the afternoon by the winemakers themselves. This is an afternoon of genuine hospitality.

events.long_description:
Niko Ne Zna Live at Vogelmorn Hall (Wellington)
Niko Ne Zna returns to Vogelmorn Hall for an unforgettable Saturday night of explosive brass, infectious rhythms, delicious food, and music that's impossible to sit still to.

Drawing inspiration from the rich musical traditions of Serbia, Macedonia, Romania, Greece, and beyond, Niko Ne Zna combines soaring brass, driving percussion, passionate multilingual vocals, and original compositions to create a spectacular live experience. Featuring two trumpets, soprano saxophone, tenor and bass trombones, sousaphone, traditional Balkan bass drum (tapan), snare drum, and powerhouse vocalist Nikkie Rich, the band delivers an exhilarating performance that will have you dancing from the first note to the last.

With more than fifteen years of captivating audiences throughout New Zealand and Australia, appearances at WOMAD New Zealand, and original music featured in What We Do in the Shadows, Niko Ne Zna has earned a reputation as one of New Zealand's premier world music acts.

Doors open at 5:30 pm, giving you plenty of time to enjoy delicious food and a drink from the fully stocked bar before the music begins. Whether you've been following Niko Ne Zna for years or are experiencing the band for the first time, prepare for an unforgettable evening of exhilarating live music, celebration, and dancing.

“Straight to the dancefloor.” — Elsewhere

“Driving rhythms, an intoxicating effect.” — Taranaki Daily News

www.nikonezna.com

Saturday 29 August
Vogelmorn Hall, Wellington

OPTIMUS GRYME @ YARD BAR BLENHEIM | 29//08/2026
😼 Totally Chonkers Collective are heading back to Blenheim for a heavyweight night of underground bass music, bringing one of Aotearoa’s most established Dubstep and Drum & Bass artists, Optimus Gryme, to The Yard Bar on 29 August. 🔥

Driven by a lifelong passion for music, Charlie B—better known as Optimus Gryme—has spent more than two decades helping shape New Zealand’s bass music landscape. His journey began in the 1990s with hip hop, progressing from schoolyard performances to playing in front of thousands alongside artists such as Che Fu and King Kapisi.

In 2009, Optimus Gryme made history by releasing New Zealand’s first Dubstep 12-inch record. He went on to release a solo album and create official remixes for some of the country’s biggest names, including Shapeshifter, Shihad, Six60, Tiki Taane and Dub FX.

Across his career, he has performed more than a thousand shows and appeared at major festivals including Homegrown, Rhythm & Vines and Northern Bass. Following a two-year hiatus, he returned in 2020 with his Drum & Bass EP, Welcome to the Streets, continuing a musical journey that shows no sign of slowing down.

Now, Optimus Gryme is bringing that experience to The Yard Bar for a headline set packed with Dubstep, Drum & Bass, heavyweight low-end pressure and unmistakable sound system energy.

Supporting the night is a stacked line-up of Nelson and Marlborough selectors:

🔊 OPTIMUS GRYME
😼 ELUSIV B2B NIL TRACE
🔥 K-ROLLA
⚡ PHILZY

Expect everything from deep 140 and rolling Drum & Bass to heavyweight stompers, underground selections and late-night dancefloor weapons.

Event details

📅 29 August
⏰ 9pm–2am

🎟 Early Bird – $20
🎟 Tier 1 – $25
🎟 Tier 2 – $30
🚪 Limited door sales – $40

Capacity is limited and ticket prices increase as each tier sells out, so lock yours in early.

Round up the crew and prepare for a proper night of underground bass music, delivered by Optimus Gryme and the Totally Chonkers Collective. 😼🔊

events.id: Dolfin-Lin Duo (Cello/Piano)-St Andrews on the Terrace, 30 The Terrace, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Dolfin-Lin Duo (Cello/Piano)
events.venue: St Andrews on the Terrace, 30 The Terrace, Wellington
events.long_description:
A chance meeting in Italy in 2021 sparked a partnership between Hungarian cellist Balázs Dolfin and Chinese-New Zealand pianist Tony Chen Lin. Trained in Hungary and Germany, they bring dynamic energy and deep rapport, drawing on global influences while still calling Budapest their enduring musical home. Tony has played solo piano for Sunday Concerts.

Their recital opens with Anton Webern’s evocative Sonata for Cello and Piano, followed by J.S. Bach’s Sonata for Viola da Gamba and Harpsichord, a lively, expressive dialogue. Zoltán Kodály’s Sonata, Op. 4 follows, inspired by Hungarian folk music, answered by Gao Ping’s Sonata No. 2 “Departure”, a Chinese counterpart. Belá Bartók’s Rhapsody No. 1 transforms peasant music into vivid concert form. Nathanael Dejong’s Abandoned Voices reflects on disconnection in the digital age. The concert closes with Johannes Brahms’s Sonata in E minor, a work steeped in contrapuntal textures and homage to Bach, bridging Hungary and the deep roots of the cello-piano repertoire.

Anton Webern, Sonata for Cello and Piano
J S Bach, Sonata for Viola da Gamba and Harpsichord in D major BWV1028
Zoltán Kodály, Sonata Op 4
Gao Ping, Sonata No 2 Departure (2001)
Béla Bartók Rhapsody No 1
Nathanael Dejong, Abandoned Voices
Johannes Brahms, Sonata in E minor Op 38

This concert is presented in association with Chamber Music NZ

events.id: Kāpiti Chorale presents: American Art Songs-St Paul's Church, 1 Langdale Ave, Paraparaumu-Event Finder
events.name: Kāpiti Chorale presents: American Art Songs
events.venue: St Paul's Church, 1 Langdale Ave, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
“Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.”
These familiar lines from Robert Frost's poem The Road Not Taken form part of Frostiana, Randall Thompson's celebrated setting of Frost's poetry and the centrepiece of Kāpiti Chorale's Session Two programme.
As 2026 marks the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States, the choir will explore a selection of American high choral music spanning more than two centuries, from Billings in the eighteenth century to works by 20th and 21st century master composers Thompson, Barber, Bernstein, Copland, Hagenberg, Higdon, Lauridsen, Stroope, Weill, and Whitacre.
The programme brings together music inspired by poetry, folk frontier traditions, sacred texts, and the natural world. Audiences will hear familiar favourites such as Simple Gifts alongside works including Sure On This Shining Night, Dirait-On, The Seal Lullaby, Lux Aurumque, and A Quiet Moment.
Moving between accompanied and a cappella works, the programme offers a wide range of musical styles and moods while showcasing some of the most loved art music in the American choral repertoire.
Kāpiti Chorale will be joined by accompanist Phillip O'Malley and tenor soloist Jamie Young.

events.name: New Zealand Mountain Film Festival
events.venue: Wairarapa Events Centre, Holloway St, Carterton
events.long_description:
The NZ Mountain Film Festival National Tour takes award winning films to audiences around NZ from August 1 onwards. A selection of the films are available for screenings in your town. The National Tour features a Pure NZ Programme featuring a full Kiwi adventure film line up.

PURE NZ NIGHT: – Total time 126 minutes

Jerry on the Jerry (10 mins) Huw Miles, NZ. World Premiere. A team of packrafters make a second attempt at a first descent of the Jerry River deep in Fiordland.

Race Be Run (15 mins) Richard Carey & Prabhjit Sabharwal, Canada/NZ. Dressed as Superman, a man runs solo along Canada’s highways to raise funds for cancer charities, transforming the grief of losing both parents into a quiet, inspiring mission of hope.

Project Redline (30 mins) Matheson Brown, NZ. A blue-collar nobody from New Zealand goes up against a mountaineering elite in an attempt to strip him of what is widely believed to be an illegitimate world record. FESTIVAL SPIRIT AWARD

Alone on Makalu (22 mins) Nick Kowalski, NZ. Matthew Scholes attempts to summit the world’s fifth-highest mountain without supplementary oxygen.

The Pole of Inaccessibility (25 mins) Danny Warley & Ned Brannigan, NZ. A paraglider embarks on a multi-day bivouac flight across New Zealand’s Southern Alps, navigating glaciers and vast wilderness to reach the country’s most remote point, the Pole of Inaccessibility. He then faces the challenge of getting back out. SPIRIT OF ADVENTURE AWARD

100 Days in Fiordland (24 mins) Dan Sutherland, NZ. Three kayakers spend 100 winter days deep in Fiordland National Park, sea kayaking, hunting, fishing and searching for unexplored whitewater in one of New Zealand’s most demanding wilderness expeditions. BEST NEW ZEALAND MADE FILM

events.name: Kāpiti Chorale presents: American Art Songs
events.venue: St Paul’s Church, Kapiti Road,Paraparaumu, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Kāpiti Chorale presents: American Art Songs
“Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.”

These familiar lines from Robert Frost's poem The Road Not Taken form part of Frostiana, Randall Thompson's celebrated setting of Frost's poetry and the centrepiece of Kāpiti Chorale's Session Two programme.

As 2026 marks the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States, the choir will explore a selection of American high choral music spanning more than two centuries, from Billings in the eighteenth century to works by 20th and 21st century master composers Thompson, Barber, Bernstein, Copland, Hagenberg, Higdon, Lauridsen, Stroope, Weill, and Whitacre.

The programme brings together music inspired by poetry, folk frontier traditions, sacred texts, and the natural world. Audiences will hear familiar favourites such as Simple Gifts alongside works including Sure On This Shining Night, Dirait-On, The Seal Lullaby, Lux Aurumque, and A Quiet Moment.

Moving between accompanied and a cappella works, the programme offers a wide range of musical styles and moods while showcasing some of the most loved art music in the American choral repertoire.

Kāpiti Chorale will be joined by accompanist Phillip O'Malley and tenor soloist Jamie Young.

events.long_description:
Tom and Cole of Strait Speared have been supplying Wellington's best venues with spear-caught butterfish for four years using methods that have minimal impact on the ocean. Knowing your fisherman matters, and tonight they're coming to the table to talk you through why. 

A nine-course degustation using all the parts of the butterfish: fillets, collars, roe. Each preparation different, each one revealing something new about the fish and the selectivity it takes to harvest responsibly. You'll chat with the fishermen about their work, with the chef about different butterfish preparations, and with the people beside you as course after course unfolds. This is what transparent seafood looks like when the person who caught it is sitting across from you. 

Your ticket includes nine courses and one welcome drink on arrival. Additional alcohol can be purchased.

events.id: 2026 Francis Gurry Lecture on Intellectual Property - WELLINGTON-AJ ParkWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
events.name: 2026 Francis Gurry Lecture on Intellectual Property - WELLINGTON
events.venue: AJ ParkWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview
"The Future of IP Dispute Resolution" by Sir Colin Birss, Chancellor of the High Court of England and Wales
5.30pm | Pre-event refreshments
6.00pm | Public lecture

The Future of IP Dispute Resolution
The legal landscape is changing before our eyes. The advent of AI and digital assets, the internationalisation of dispute resolution, and the changing expectations of users, all pose challenges, and intellectual property has always raised issues of its own.
This lecture will examine the state of intellectual property litigation today in the wider context, consider where it needs to be in future, and look at how we need to adapt to meet the challenges.
The topics include the major legal problems in IP which will need to be addressed; the legal and practical impact of artificial intelligence; the importance of digital assets and tokenisation; and the emergence of alternative modes of resolving dispute resolution.
Colin Birss is the Chancellor (Head of the Chancery Division) of the High Court of England and Wales. Called to the English Bar in 1990, he practised intellectual property law. In 2010 he became judge at the Patents County Court (now IPEC), in 2013 he went to the High Court, and in 2021 to the Court of Appeal. He was Deputy Head of Civil Justice 2021-25, and appointed Chancellor in 2025. He sits in the Court of Appeal and in the High Court.

If you are a University of Melbourne alumni, information about your participation may be shared with the Advancement team, as explained in our privacy notice.

Join us for the launch of Otto Wine Club – a new monthly wine tasting series celebrating some of New Zealand's best wineries.

Each month we'll welcome a different winery to Otto, where you'll have the chance to meet the winemaker, hear the stories behind the wines, and taste a curated selection from their range.

Our first event features Schubert Wines, one of Martinborough's most respected boutique wineries. Drop in anytime between 5:00pm and 7:00pm to enjoy your guided tasting.
Your ticket includes:
- A tasting flight of five Schubert wines
- The opportunity to meet the winemaker and learn about the vineyard and winemaking process
- A relaxed after-work atmosphere with plenty of time to ask questions and discover your new favourite drop

Whether you're a seasoned wine enthusiast or simply keen to explore something new, this is a fun, informal way to discover great New Zealand wine.

Spaces are limited, so book early to avoid missing out.

About Schubert Wines: https://www.schubert.co.nz/wines/
After graduating from the German Viticulture and Oenology University Geisenheim Kai Schubert and Marion Deimling travelled the world in search of the perfect terroir and conditions for viticulture, especially their favourite variety – Pinot Noir. Their quest took them to the wine regions of France, Germany, Oregon, California, South America and Australia and ended in Martinborough in the beautiful Wairarapa Valley.

Here they found the perfect climate and conditions for producing low yields and excellent quality grapes. Since 1998 Schubert Wines have been growing and producing wines with intense and complex character that are now nationally and internationally award winning.

events.name: Book Group: The Grass is Singing by Doris Lessing
events.venue: The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
We return to Africa for our September book: Doris Lessing's first novel The Grass is Singing, which takes place in Southern Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe) in the 1940s. The novel opens with a newspaper clipping about the death of Mary Turner, a white woman, killed by her black servant, Moses. The bulk of the novel is the story of Mary's life and the divided society she lived in.

Lessing was born in Persia, to British parents, and moved to Southern Rhodesia when she was six. Many of her books are set in Africa. In 1949 she left the continent and arrived in London with her son Peter (leaving behind her two older children) and the manuscript for this novel under her arm. The Grass is Singing was published the following year. Lessing was awarded the Nobel Prize in literature in 2007.

This is a shorter book, fitting neatly between The Last of the Mohicans and W. Somerset Maugham's Of Human Bondage, which are both longer works. (Of Human Bondage was originally published in two volumes.) But The Grass is Singing packs a punch. Indeed, one Goodreads review begins: "Doris Lessing's first novel has the precision of a fine short story and the depth of a longer novel."

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

RSVP
Bookings essential. Get your free ticket by clicking 'Register' above. Limited places.

If you've signed up, but things change and you're not going to be able to make it along, please email classiclitwgtn@gmail.com as we may be able to make more spaces available for others.

VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library bar's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond (behind the big wooden sliding door).

ABOUT US
Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

events.name: How To Write A Romance Novel: A Workshop
events.venue: Project 100Nelson, Nelson Region
events.long_description:
Overview






A workshop that will take you through the A to Z of writing a character driven romance novel from bestselling author George Penney.
Do you have dreams of typing “The End” on a romance novel you’ve written but don’t know where to start?
Have you always dreamed of being a writer but find the actual process of becoming one intimidating?
Or maybe you’re a forever-writer just looking for pointers for how to shape your ideas into a structure that’ll sell to readers.
This three hour workshop will take you from initial character creation, through romance story structure and then to practical tips on getting your romance novel finished.
You’ll be taken through different romance genres, how to come up with three-dimensional, interesting characters, how to built tension and conflict, tips on writing good sex scenes and how to write that truly satisfying Happy Ever After ending.
This is a practical workshop designed to leave attendees motivated, excited and equipped with the tools to go on and finish that book!

*Please note: This is an AI free writing workshop. We believe that writing should be a messy, wonderful, exasperating, rewarding process that explores the depth of human creativity rather than a test on how well someone can type a prompt into a LLM. If you'd like to argue this point, please send us a non-AI hardbound treatise of no less than one hundred thousand words, hand-written in iambic pentameter.

For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

events.long_description:
Behind the Scenes: Napier Port & Mainfreight Learning Adventure
Have you ever driven past Napier Port or watched trucks moving through Hawke's Bay and wondered what really happens behind the scenes?

Every day, thousands of tonnes of cargo, products and supplies move through systems most of us rarely get to see.

Yet these operations quietly keep our region connected to New Zealand and the rest of the world.

This is a rare opportunity to step behind the gates and discover two of Hawke's Bay's most fascinating and important operations.

Join us for a special Learning Adventure that takes you inside Napier Port and Mainfreight Hastings, guided by people who know these organisations better than almost anyone.

Our day begins with an exclusive guided tour of Napier Port, one of New Zealand's busiest maritime hubs. You'll hear stories of the port's history, watch the operation in action, and gain a new appreciation for the scale and complexity of what happens there every day.

After the port tour, we'll gather for a relaxed waterfront lunch at Madame Social in Ahuriri — a chance to enjoy great food, good conversation and wonderful company.

In the afternoon, we'll head to Mainfreight's Hastings depot for a behind-the-scenes look at one of the country's most innovative logistics operations. From live freight tracking and electric forklifts to sustainable building design and workplace culture, you'll discover what makes this Hawke's Bay business such a success.

Along the way, you'll meet interesting people, hear remarkable stories and see parts of the region that most people never get access to.

Meet Our Guides 🎤

Tony des Landes spent more than 50 years working at Napier Port and is one of Hawke's Bay's leading maritime historians. His knowledge of the port, its history and its role in shaping the region is unmatched.

John Mackay is Hastings Branch Manager at Mainfreight and brings deep insight into the day-to-day operations, innovation and culture that have helped make Mainfreight one of New Zealand's most respected companies.

What We'll Explore
• A rare behind-the-scenes tour of Napier Port
• The history and evolution of Hawke's Bay's maritime industry
• How goods move through New Zealand's supply chains
• Innovation, sustainability and culture at Mainfreight
• The people, stories and systems that keep our region connected

Overview


Wellington Chamber of Commerce and Pax8 are proud to host the Prime Minister, Christopher Luxon.
Join Business Central and the Wellington Chamber of Commerce for an exclusive breakfast event featuring Prime Minister Rt Hon Christopher Luxon in conversation with Hayley Horan, Chief Executive of Business Central.
Set within the iconic Banquet Hall at Parliament, this special event offers members and the wider business community a rare opportunity to hear directly from New Zealand's leader in a professionally moderated fireside chat.
Unlike a traditional keynote speech, this event has been designed as a genuine conversation. The discussion will be informed by the experiences, perspectives, and questions submitted by Business Central and Wellington Chamber members, helping to ensure the topics explored reflect the realities, opportunities, and challenges facing our business community today.
Designed to be engaging, insightful, and business-focused, the discussion will explore the opportunities and challenges shaping New Zealand's future. From economic growth, productivity, trade, infrastructure, workforce development and artificial intelligence, through to geopolitics and New Zealand's long-term competitiveness, the conversation will focus on the issues that matter most to businesses across our region.
Following the fireside chat, attendees will have the opportunity to participate in a live audience Q&A, providing further engagement with the Prime Minister and valuable insight into the Government's priorities and vision for New Zealand.

Shared breakfast at a round table with fellow business leaders
Exclusive access to a one-hour conversation with the Prime Minister
Opportunity to submit questions that may shape the discussion
Live audience Q&A
Networking with business, government, and community leaders before and after the event
Agenda:

8.05 am - Q&A with audience
8.30 am - Closing formalities

Why Attend?
Whether you're a business owner, executive, manager, entrepreneur, policy professional, or emerging leader, this event offers a rare opportunity to gain direct insight into the issues shaping New Zealand's future while connecting with some of the region's most engaged and influential business people.
Bring your questions. Share your perspective. Help shape the conversation.

events.long_description:
Overview












The physics of the ocean in the age of multiple stressors.




Welcome to the biannual New Zealand Physical Oceanography Workshop (POW).
As climate change fundamentally reshapes our marine environments, understanding the fluid dynamics, heat distribution, and structural dynamics of our oceans has never been more critical. This year, our community gathers under a vital, unifying theme: The physics of the ocean in the age of multiple stressors.

We invite abstracts and presentations exploring the fundamental physical processes driving—and reacting to—global environmental change:
Coastal Oceanography of New Zealand
High-Latitude and Polar Dynamics
Next-Generation Ocean Modelling & Data Integration
Cross-Disciplinary Climate Solutions
How to do oceanography in the age of gestures broadly

Call for Abstracts & Registration Details
Oral Presentations: Standard 15-minute slots (including Q&A).
Lightning Talks: Project snapshots—ideal for introducing preliminary findings, novel scripts, or new field deployments.
How to Submit: Please email your presentation title, authors' list, a brief abstract (max 250 words), and your presentation preference directly to the organising committee at oceanography.newzealand@gmail.com.
Abstract Submission Deadline: 20 August 2026
Registration Deadline: 20 August 2026
Hybrid Registration Deadline: 1 September 2026
Registration is $100 for general attendees and free for students. We also have a free hybrid attendance option with the ability to present. Early-career researchers are highly encouraged to present.

We are planning a fun dinner on Wednesday, and we aim to finish early on Thursday.
We're looking forward to seeing you in September!

Presented by: Live Nation
Genre-bending future soul visionaries Hiatus Kaiyote return to celebrate their 15th anniversary with an electrifying night of funk, jazz, hip-hop, rock and progressive R&B as only they know how.
Led by singer-guitarist Naomi “Nai Palm” Saalfield, the Melbourne funkateers –featuring bassist Paul Bender, keyboardist Simon Mavin and drummer Perrin Moss –exploded internationally with their 2012 debut Tawk Tomahawk, which drew praise from the likes of Prince, Erykah Badu and Questlove. They landed their first of three Grammy nominations for their Q-Tip collaboration Nakamarra, received their second for their polyrhythmic record Choose Your Weapon (2015), and had their music sampled by no less than Kendrick Lamar, Beyoncé and Drake (with whom Nai Palm also collaborated on 2018’s monster hit Scorpion).
The band’s kaleidoscopic 2021 album Mood Valiant sent them into the national top five and earned them another Grammy nod, while their latest, 2024’s Love Heart Cheat Code, landed them an ARIA nomination for Best Group. Wizards of the shapeshifting live show, Hiatus Kaiyote have built a formidable reputation for their spectacular stage performances – a high-wire mix of musical mastery and thrilling, edge-of-your-seat chaos.

events.venue: Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBDWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview



Gain a core understanding of requirements elicitation, the importance of planning, and coverage of many valuable elicitation techniques.
Description
This one-day course provides a core understanding of elicitation, the importance of planning, and coverage of many valuable elicitation techniques. Emphasis is also placed on the need to verify requirements with the business to confirm that an accurate understanding has been elicited. During the afternoon session course participants undertake a realistic elicitation exercise, to reinforce the principles and techniques learnt during the course.
Greater emphasis is being placed on skilled business analysts who have the ability to communicate strongly, engage with stakeholders, and elicit a clear understanding of business requirements. Requirements elicitation skills have never been more important for business analysts and IT professionals.

The Requirements Elicitation course is delivered by seasoned Equinox consultant practitioners who apply the techniques and practices presented in this course on a daily basis.

Outline
Introduction to Requirements Elicitation
Goals of elicitation
Elicitation in the analysis process
Requirements elicitation methodology
Plan
The need for planning
Common elicitation problems
Requirements elicitation techniques
Requirements election patterns
Selection criteria
The requirements elicitation plan
Do
Preparing for the elicitation session
Performing elicitation
Managing the elicitation session
Presenting the elicitation results
Check
Communicate the requirements set
Check elicitation results
Check elicitation process
Act – corrective action
Requirements elicitation exercise

Learning outcomes
Following the completion of this course, students will be able to:
Identify where requirements elicitation fits within the broader requirements process
Understand and adopt an elicitation methodology
Select appropriate elicitation techniques for the situation
Plan and manage a requirements elicitation session
Understand the need for verification of elicitation results

Audience
The primary audience for this course is business analysts and systems analysts of all levels of experience. The course will also be of value to any project team members who are involved in elicitation or requirements activities.

Prerequisites
It is recommended that participants have some experience with requirements in project environment before attending.

events.id: Can Electricity Markets Deliver the Clean Energy Transition?-Russell McVeaghWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
events.name: Can Electricity Markets Deliver the Clean Energy Transition?
events.venue: Russell McVeaghWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview
A global perspective on investment, reliability, and the risks of getting it wrong.
Three recent shocks to electricity markets - cheap renewables, declining storage costs, and the return of demand growth - have led some to conclude that electricity markets as we know them have run their course. Drawing on thirty years of restructured markets abroad, this presentation will argue that these developments actually strengthen the case for markets — and will explore what reliability means, and how it should be provided, in a greener electricity system.
Professor James Bushnell – Biography
Professor James Bushnell is a distinguished scholar whose research and policy contributions have helped shape modern understanding of electricity markets, energy regulation, and climate policy, making him one of the most influential voices in energy economics. He is an internationally recognised expert in energy economics, electricity markets, environmental policy, and industrial organisation.The event is being facilitated by ERGANZ and will be hosted at the Wellington offices of Russell McVeagh
Date and Time: Thursday 3 September, 4pm - 6pm @Russell McVeagh, 157 Lambton Quay, please join us for a drink and nibbles from 4pm, presentation to start at 4:30pm with a Q&A to follow.
Please email admin@erganz.org.nz with any dietary requirements.
RSVP: Registrations can be secured by clicking on "Reserve a Spot".
