events.id: State-Market Tensions & Geopolitical Rivalry in the Semiconductor Industry-HMLT002 Hugh Mackenzie BuildingWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
events.name: State-Market Tensions & Geopolitical Rivalry in the Semiconductor Industry
events.venue: HMLT002 Hugh Mackenzie BuildingWellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview
Why are semiconductors central to global power? This keynote explores state-market tensions, supply chains, and geopolitical rivalry.
Using the global semiconductor industry as a case study, this lecture explores ‘decoupling’ amidst the complex web of state-market relations.
Most studies of decoupling focus on the United States and China. In contrast, I focus on the relationship between the United States and the full range of key semiconductor producers (Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, and China). I ask when, and how, states intervene in semiconductor markets and propose that while the main actors in the semiconductor supply chain are not hegemonic powers, their high production capacities mean that their power is ‘pivotal’.
I argue that while technology production chains reflect the conflicting interests of states, because production chains also embody key shared interests, states cannot completely ‘decouple’ from one another. Meanwhile, key stakeholders are not always states, but also private companies and skilled workers. These actors have their own interests as well, meaning that production chains become further intertwined, rendering true decoupling impossible. Their resistance to decoupling means that this ‘stickiness’ will be a feature of any state-led attempt to forge supply chain independence.

In New Zealand there is an increasing number of older persons who retain their natural dentition until later in life. Accordingly edentulous patients will not only be older, they will also be also more challenging to treat. Implant-supported overdentures (IODs) may significantly improve the functional performance in most domains, particularly the bite force and chewing efficiency. They also significantly improve the patients’ OHRQoL. Their design should take into consideration the physiological signs of ageing, but also the morbidity and social context. The lecture presents step by step the manufacturing of age-adequate IODs with conventional and digital workflows. Digital techniques may also be employed to meet the requirements of very old patients with reduced neuroplasticity, as they allow to import successful features from an existing denture. IOD management may become a challenge at the onset of dependency when denture handling relies on the knowledge and skill of caring staff. At this stage, hygiene is even more crucial to prevent aspiration pneumonia. The “back-off” strategy aims at accompanying the functional decline. In summary, IODs significantly enhance oral function and denture satisfaction and therefore be considered a valuable mosaic in the dental treatment for older adults.

Learning objectives
1. Design an age-adequate removable prosthesis
2. Develop concepts for patients with reduced neuroplasticity
3. Know strategies to accompany future functional decline in very old and multimorbid patients

events.long_description:
Overview
A welcoming men’s circle for honest conversation, breathwork and meaningful connection in a space of trust and support.
Men's Circle & Breathwork 
Starts at 6pm
In a world where men are often expected to have everything figured out, this gathering offers a space to be genuine, not perfect.
This is a free event, with an optional plant-based dinner available for $15. While there’s no obligation to stay for dinner, sharing a meal together offers a meaningful way to strengthen connections.
Andre and Sri Jiva co-host this circle with a shared passion for creating authentic, supportive spaces where men can connect deeply, offering this gathering simply because they believe in its importance.
The Men’s Circle provides a safe and nurturing environment where men can share openly, express their feelings and encourage personal growth. Through honest sharing and collective support, participants build resilience, deepen self-awareness, and strengthen their sense of identity and purpose.
 Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
Breathwork is a powerful practice to help ground the nervous system and connect to a deep presence. 
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
 Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.
Join us after this free event for an optional plant-based dinner and dessert for only $20 (or $10 for students).
Meet Andre, your host:
Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human, how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.
Meet Sri Jiva, your host:
Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

Overview

Refresh body and mind with a gentle spring breathwork journey to release winter heaviness and reconnect with your natural aliveness.

Somatic Breathwork: Spring Renewal




Event starts at 6pm

September is a threshold month, a natural invitation to spring clean.

Not just the space around you, but the space inside you too.

Spring Cleansing is a somatic breathwork session designed to help you gently shift some of the heaviness that can build up over the colder months. Think sluggishness, brain fog, tension, low energy, or simply that feeling of being a little stuck in your body.

Through a consent-led, trauma-aware breathwork journey, we’ll create space to:

move stagnant energy and emotions
warm and reconnect with the body
release some of the heaviness that winter can leave behind
return to your breath, presence, and natural sense of aliveness

A chance to pause, breathe, and make room for something new.

You’ll leave feeling lighter, clearer, and more connected to your body, like opening the windows and letting fresh air move through.

This session is for you if:
you’ve felt heavy, puffy, sluggish, or “damp” after winter
your chest/breath has felt tight, shallow, or restricted
you’ve been waking up tired, unmotivated, or mentally foggy
you’ve been indoors more, moving less, and can feel it in your body
you want a reset that’s embodied, not performative
you want a welcoming, choice-based space to explore breathwork
What to expect
Arrival (consent + information) chair, side-lying, and low-intensity options available
Nervous system primer: clearing and activation safely
Breath demonstration + choice of intensity tracks (including a gentle nasal-only option)
A guided somatic breathwork arc. clearing, warming, and releasing what’s been holding on
Optional movement to support circulation (micro-shakes, shaking, or gentle unwinding)
Integration rest + grounding
Closing reflection (brief journaling prompt or quiet pause)
Benefits you may notice

You might experience:

a lighter body and clearer head
more warmth and circulation through chest/shoulders/hips
improved mood and motivation
emotional release without overwhelm
deeper, easier breathing
a renewed sense of momentum that feels steady (not forced)
Please bring:
Yoga mat
Warm layers (we’ll warm up, but your body may cool during rest)
Water bottle
Small towel
Optional eye mask or light scarf
Journal and pen
If you run cold, bring a blanket
Pre-class prep
Eat a light meal 2 hours before class.
Hydrate well throughout the day.
Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours.
Limit caffeine 4 hours prior.
Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
If you have health conditions, please check with your provider.
Feel free to email Lynn at hi@lynofuro.co.nz if there’s anything you’d like to share before the session.
Contraindications and safety

Somatic breathwork may not be suitable for pregnancy; serious cardiovascular conditions; uncontrolled blood pressure; glaucoma or retinal detachment; epilepsy or seizure history; recent surgery or concussion; or severe psychiatric conditions/active psychosis. A conservative, nasal-only track is always available. This is not a substitute for medical care.

Aftercare

After the session, remember to:

Drink plenty of water
Eat nourishing food
Engage in simple movement or a short walk
Journal your insights
Get an early bedtime

Emotional waves may continue for 24 to 48 hours, reach out if you need support.

You’ll also receive a guided audio breathwork aftercare to support you in the 24–48 hours after the session (gentle regulation, grounding, and integration).

Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!
September 1:1 Somatic Coaching — 2 spots available

If this session lights something up in you and you’re ready for deeper support, I’m opening 2 private 1:1 coaching spots in September.

This is for you if you want nervous-system-led guidance to:

regulate stress and restore steady capacity
soften chronic tension patterns in the body
build embodied boundaries and self-trust
move through stuckness with breath, somatic tools, and grounded coaching

To enquire, email hi@lynofuro.co.nz with the subject line: September 1:1.

Meet Your Host: Lynn

Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner based in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Her work combines somatic breathwork, Reiki, and life coaching to support nervous system regulation, emotional wellbeing, and grounded personal transformation in a practical, trauma-aware way.

New Zealand’s most successful rock series ever, COME TOGETHER, returns in 2026 with an electrifying trio of landmark albums: Bruce Springsteen’s Born to Run, Radiohead’s OK Computer and Talking Heads’ Stop Making Sense.

Each album will be performed live, in full, by a rotating supergroup of Aotearoa’s most acclaimed rock artists and musicians — followed by a second set of classics and deep cuts that span each artist’s extraordinary catalogue.

From the wall of sound production of Born to Run, to the haunting dystopian brilliance of OK Computer, to the joyful and immersive perfection of Stop Making Sense, the 2026 series celebrates three albums that have cemented their place in music history. Performed in some of the country’s most beautiful venues, Come Together once again promises epic musicianship, emotional punch and the kind of once-in-a-lifetime collaborations that have made the series a cultural phenomenon.

Widely regarded as one of the greatest live albums and concert films of all time, Stop Making Sense captured Talking Heads at the absolute height of their powers. A bona fide classic, it remains a benchmark for concert performance and sonic brilliance.

Recreated in all its Talking Heads glory, every track from the concert film will be performed — from Psycho Killer to Burning Down the House, Once in a Lifetime, and everything in between. Expect big grooves, art-school cool… and yes, some mighty suits.

Performed by: James Milne, Anthonie Tonnon, Dianne Swann, Julia Deans and the Come Together band — with more to be announced.

When comedian Chris Parker was young, he liked attention. He’s always endeavoured to make people look at him. In his latest show, he continues the theme of a lifetime. Take a Good Hard Look at Me displays the Kiwi comic’s sharp wit and clever timing. Chris says of his hour-long show — “There’s no secrets about to be dished, no valuable lesson to take away. INSPIRE Festival is for all tamariki aged 8-13 (up to year 8) who are interested in STEAMS learning.
Public ticket sales open on 7 August. Early access is currently available by invitation only.

INSPIRE Festival is 4-5 Sept 2026!
$60 per child per day for a full day of STEAMS learning!
INSPIRE Festival 2026 offers two days of student selected challenging discussions and hands-on workshops all focused around STEAMS (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Maths, and Society). This year the festival is being hosted at Nayland College!
• Friday: 1- or 2-hour workshops
• Saturday: 2-4 hour, in-depth workshops. Perfect for students to get really stuck in to topics.
INSPIRE offers thought-provoking discussions and hands on experiments for AGES 8-13 (up to Year 8). Students choose up to 4 sessions to attend, all based on the STEAMS model of education and delivered by New Zealand's top professionals, scientists, businessmen, and mentored college students.
INSPIRE will develop the connection between classroom theory and some very exciting and ground-breaking real careers which make a difference in our world. The inaugural INSPIRE was in 2012 and massive demand has led to it being hosted annually with over 650 students attending and has continued to grow. All attendees will be our future leaders and creative thinkers and they have told us they want more; more challenge, more connections and more opportunities to grow and learn.

events.name: Natural Textured Rings - Taster Class
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Craft a beautiful, personalised ring - a perfect treat for yourself or a thoughtful gift for someone special! This three-hour taster class is designed for absolute beginners, though all skill levels are welcome to join the fun.

You will be guided step-by-step through the core techniques of silversmithing. You'll start by practicing basic texturing, cutting, and shaping with traditional jewellery tools using copper or brass. Once you’re comfortable, you'll move on to crafting your final piece in sterling silver.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:
Measure your finger and cut the metal strip to the perfect length.
Create unique surface textures using a rolling mill, hammers, punches, and even natural elements like feathers or leaves. You can stamp names, dates, whatever you like.
Work safely with a jeweler's torch for heating and soldering the metal.
Finish your ring with sanding and polishing techniques.
By the end of the class, your beautiful, custom-made sterling silver ring will be ready to wear.

This is an ideal activity for individuals, groups of friends, or visitors to Ōtaki looking for a creative experience.

What's Included:
All practice materials (copper or brass).
A strip of sterling silver for your final ring.
All necessary consumables (sandpaper, solder, chemicals).
Use of all tools and equipment.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kanagawa Japan’s #1 rock vocalist DEATHRO returns to Aotearoa in September 2026, presented by Wrought Material and Chain Punk Baddie. Beloved by the Tokyo punk underground, DEATHRO combines new wave, post-punk, and J-Rock into high-energy BEATROCK in the 1980’s Japanese tradition.

DEATHRO showcases his high energy beatrock performances in an extensive journey across both Te Ika-a-Māui and Te Waipounamu this September, including a stop at Great Sounds Great Festival in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Don't miss it!

events.long_description:
John Adams The Chairman Dances
Copland Clarinet Concerto
Gabriela Ortiz Antrópolis (NZ Premiere)
Bernstein Symphonic Dances from West Side Story

Gemma New’s signature “strength, clarity and grace” (WTTW News) invigorates this 20th century American classic, Bernstein’s Symphonic Dances from West Side Story. In depicting a New York gangland Romeo and Juliet, Bernstein’s score captures an irrepressible American swagger. Rhythm & Dance also infuses John Adams’ The Chairman Dances, an outtake of Adams’ opera Nixon in China, which imagines the young Chairman Mao dancing the foxtrot with his mistress.

Aaron Copland’s Clarinet Concerto melds Latin American popular music with jazz in this work commissioned by “The King of Swing” Benny Goodman. And we proudly present the Kiwi premiere of Gabriela Ortiz’s Antrópolis. Grammy Award-winning Ortiz is one of Mexico’s hottest contemporary composers, and this work refers to el antro, Mexican slang for a nightclub.

events.name: Yoga Nidra
events.venue: Awhi Yoga and Wellbeing Centre, 15 Johnston St., Wellington
events.long_description:
Unwind from the stresses of the week and start your weekend in a state of relaxation. Yoga Nidra, often referred to as "yogic sleep," is a deeply restorative practice that promotes physical relaxation, mental clarity, and emotional balance. It's the perfect way to rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul: your hinengaro, tinana and wairua.

Yoga nidra is a powerful technique that directly works to heal your mind by removing samskaras - untying knots and mental impressions. This practice of learning to relax consciously is well regarded as an antidote for stress, anxiety, poor sleep amongst other health benefits.

Everyone is welcome to experience the profound benefits of Yoga Nidra, and no prior experience is required. For some people, however, Yoga Nidra’s prolonged stillness or internal focus can bring up strong emotions, memories, and/or sensations. You are encouraged to listen and respond in a way that feels safe for you — adjusting your position, keeping your eyes open, grounding yourself, or stepping out of the room at any time.

Yoga Nidra may not be suitable for everyone. If you are experiencing acute mental health challenges, unprocessed trauma, or conditions that make stillness or internal focus difficult, we recommend seeking guidance from a qualified healthcare provider or speaking with the teacher before participating.

events.id: A Voyage to the Moon by Offenbach: A NZSM Opera Production-Adam Concert Room, NZSM Kelburn Campus, Victoria University, Gate 7, Kelburn Parade, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: A Voyage to the Moon by Offenbach: A NZSM Opera Production
events.venue: Adam Concert Room, NZSM Kelburn Campus, Victoria University, Gate 7, Kelburn Parade, Wellington
events.long_description:
Classical Performance students from the New Zealand School of Music – Te Kōkī present four performances of Jacques Offenbach's delightful comic opera A Voyage to the Moon, directed by Sara Brodie with musical direction by Kathryn Mosley.

Inspired by this year's space exploration milestones, including NASA's Artemis II mission, this production celebrates Offenbach's imaginative 1875 opera, which was a sensation in Paris, running for an impressive 185 consecutive performances during its first run.

Loosely based on Jules Verne's novel From the Earth to the Moon, A Voyage to the Moon takes audiences on a adventure filled with fantastical lunar landscapes, eccentric characters, and Offenbach's trademark comedic twists. The story follows King V'lan, his adventurous son Prince Caprice, and their companions—including Microscope and Rhombus—as they journey to the Moon, where they encounter Cosmos, Princess Fantasia, Flamma, and other curious inhabitants of the lunar world.

Directed by Sara Brodie, who also led last year's fantastic production of L'enfant et les sortilèges, the opera features vocal numbers performed in French with English surtitles. The spoken dialogue is presented in English, bringing the comedy vividly to life for contemporary audiences.

This production showcases the talents of students across the Classical Performance programme, with NZSM voice students performing all roles and in ensembles, and the NZSM piano students taking part as rehearsal pianists (répétiteurs) and playing for the performances. Musical direction is provided by Head of Collaborative Piano Kathryn Mosley, and the production is coordinated by Head of Classical Voice Jenny Wollerman.

Join us for an imaginative, entertaining, and truly 'out there' operatic adventure!

events.long_description:
Expect soaring harmonies, a dynamic live show, and feel-good vibes when Mel Parsons performs live in Wellington this September. With a style that ranges from indie folk to alt-country, the Kiwi artist has established a reputation for moving songwriting. 
The tour repertoire is based around songs from her latest album, Castle Hill. Named after the remote mountain town in the Southern Alps where it was recorded, Castle Hill was recorded live with Mel’s longtime band members, Aaron Stewart on bass and Jed Parsons on drums. It also includes Ben King (guitarist from Goldenhorse and Grand Rapids). They will support her on stage too. Singles from the record that you’ll hear include alt radio chart toppers, Post High Slide, Brick By Brick, Be Here Now, and Grain by Grain. 
Since her first album in 2009, Mel has established herself in New Zealand’s musical landscape. Awards include Best Folk Artist (2020 New Zealand Music Awards) and Best Country Music Song (2016 New Zealand Music Awards).

events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre,111 Wakefield St, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Rhythm & Dance - Wellington
Stamp the beat and feel the heat in this concert of pan-American dance, jazz and pizzazz!

Programme
John Adams The Chairman Dances
Copland Clarinet Concerto
Gabriela Ortiz Antrópolis (NZ Premiere)
Bernstein Symphonic Dances from West Side Story

Gemma New’s signature “strength, clarity and grace” (WTTW News) invigorates this 20th century American classic, Bernstein’s Symphonic Dances from West Side Story. In depicting a New York gangland Romeo and Juliet, Bernstein’s score captures an irrepressible American swagger. Rhythm & Dance also infuses John Adams’ The Chairman Dances, an outtake of Adams’ opera Nixon in China, which imagines the young Chairman Mao dancing the foxtrot with his mistress.

Aaron Copland’s Clarinet Concerto melds Latin American popular music with jazz in this work commissioned by “The King of Swing” Benny Goodman. And we proudly present the Kiwi premiere of Gabriela Ortiz’s Antrópolis. Grammy Award-winning Ortiz is one of Mexico’s hottest contemporary composers, and this work refers to el antro, Mexican slang for a nightclub.

In association with New Zealand Herald.

events.long_description:
A Voyage to the Moon by Offenbach: A NZSM Opera Production
Classical Performance students from the New Zealand School of Music – Te Kōkī present four performances of Jacques Offenbach's delightful comic opera A Voyage to the Moon, directed by Sara Brodie with musical direction by Kathryn Mosley.

Performance dates:
Friday 4 September, 7:30pm
Saturday 5 September, 3:00pm & 7:30pm
Sunday 6 September, 3:00pm

Duration: 70 minutes
Venue: The Adam Concert Room
Tickets: On sale now via Eventfinda with student and concession discounts available!

Inspired by this year's space exploration milestones, including NASA's Artemis II mission, this production celebrates Offenbach's imaginative 1875 opera, which was a sensation in Paris, running for an impressive 185 consecutive performances during its first run.

Loosely based on Jules Verne's novel From the Earth to the Moon, A Voyage to the Moon takes audiences on a adventure filled with fantastical lunar landscapes, eccentric characters, and Offenbach's trademark comedic twists. The story follows King V'lan, his adventurous son Prince Caprice, and their companions—including Microscope and Rhombus—as they journey to the Moon, where they encounter Cosmos, Princess Fantasia, Flamma, and other curious inhabitants of the lunar world.

Directed by Sara Brodie, who also led last year's fantastic production of L'enfant et les sortilèges, the opera features vocal numbers performed in French with English surtitles. The spoken dialogue is presented in English, bringing the comedy vividly to life for contemporary audiences.

This production showcases the talents of students across the Classical Performance programme, with NZSM voice students performing all roles and in ensembles, and the NZSM piano students taking part as rehearsal pianists (répétiteurs) and playing for the performances. Musical direction is provided by Head of Collaborative Piano Kathryn Mosley, and the production is coordinated by Head of Classical Voice Jenny Wollerman.

Join us for an imaginative, entertaining, and truly 'out there' operatic adventure!

events.long_description:
Celebrate the season in style aboard the Spring Fling Express.

This heritage rail journey whisks you from Kapiti through the lower North Island’s most breathtaking landscapes.
Tailor your day with two delightful options: jump off at the iconic Taniwha Daffodils to wander through vibrant golden fields, or continue to Waipukurau. In town, explore the bustling Spring Market or opt for short "shuttle" train trips to discover our charming neighbouring townships. Combining nostalgic rail travel with the very best of country hospitality, this is the ultimate springtime escape.

Hop aboard the Spring Fling Flyer for a delightful short-haul heritage rail experience during the festival's launch weekend!
Operating as charming shuttle excursions from Waipukurau, these trips offer a nostalgic journey to both Ōtāne and Takapau, connecting communities and celebrations along the line.

While at the station, don’t miss 'Tracks through Waipukurau', a platform exhibition celebrating 150 years of journeys, stories, and connection.
It is a fun, flexible, and scenic way to immerse yourself in the Spring Fling festivities while experiencing the golden age of rail.

TICKET INCLUDES: Nostalgic heritage 1-day train travel from Paekakariki to Waipukurau and return.

KEY EVENT INFO: All ages welcome
Service operates in wet weather
Due to the age/design of heritage carriages, this experience is not suitable for passengers with limited mobility; please contact the Steam Incorporated bookings team to discuss options if you have any questions.
Meal options available and caters for a range of dietaries (including gluten free/vegetarian/vegan).
______________________________

Your Spring, Your Way

Running throughout September- and October, this year's Spring Fling is a curated showcase of our district's finest heritage, hospitality, and heart. Whether you're seeking a long, indulgent lunch in a historic garden or a heart pumping coastal trak, there is a Spring Fling experience crafted specifically for you.

Central Hawke's Bay is a hidden gem waiting to be discovered, come and experience the warmth of our hospitality and the magic of our landscapes.

events.name: Bob Ross Landscape Painting Workshop
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
NZ’s first Certified Bob Ross Instructor, Malcolm Sime, will prove to you that if you can hold a pen and write, you can hold a brush and paint. Come along and create a landscape oil painting from scratch to take away at the end of the day!

Description
If you don’t already know who Bob Ross is then Google him, and you will be amazed at how he creates fantastic paintings using simple tools. You can too!

Wear old clothes, come with nothing except your lunch, and go home with an oil painting completed 100% by yourself.

All materials are included in course fee – a 16x20 inch professional canvas, Bob Ross oil paints, brushes, and all equipment, as seen on NZ TV and YouTube.

This is a unique technique of wet-into-wet oil painting, which is ideal for those who have never painted before, as well as more experienced artists.

Please note: Suitable for all adults - please make sure you have a method to transport your wet oil painting home at the end of day. Each workshop focuses on doing a specific set landscape painting - the whole class group does the same painting.

(Please note there is no wheelchair access to this venue).

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Whether you’re already retired, or planning ahead, this practical workshop will help you to reflect, re-envision and re-vitalise your life and develop a plan for your future, on your own terms. (NZ citizens and residents free with ID, all others pay $109).

In your middle years, working, retired or somewhere in between? What’s next? Life is about much more than work or leisure, but most of us have given little thought to what “retirement” might mean.

It’s difficult to speculate what may happen in the future, but we can be proactive and take control.
This course offers insights into how to make the most of our time once we’re less focused on career and/or child-rearing. It covers many of the issues people face when considering a move from current employment to a different lifestyle that includes more time to do the things we’ve always promised ourselves we’d do – “when we retire”.

After the workshop, you’ll be able to identify a number of common issues and potential ways to manage them when considering and planning your “rejuvenation”, rather than a retirement. We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.

By the end of the day, you’ll have:
- Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you
- Completed a personal life audit exercise and considered your strengths
- Explored possibilities in the major aspects of your life and identified potential challenges and strategies for overcoming them
- Developed a blueprint to maximise the best years of your life and developed a “future-proofing” downsizing plan
- Considered options to include a sense of purpose and explored and implemented choices that provide you with that sense of purpose
Bring a pen and paper.

1 day, Sat 9:30 AM – 4:00 PM
Wellington High School
Presented by Angela Robertson

events.long_description:
Art Therapy for Well-Being: A Canvas for Self-Discovery
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
Sometimes, our minds get stuck in habitual thought loops—endlessly cycling through the same worries, fears, and anxieties without ever finding a breakthrough. When words fall short, art therapy offers a different language. By shifting from thinking to creating, we bypass the noise of everyday stress and tap into an intuitive visual language that can surprise us with fresh insights, new perspectives, and profound meaning.
This workshop is a gentle, immersive introduction to a pathway of self-restoration, self-compassion, and self-worth—the vital foundations for true self-healing.
What you will experience:
A Shift in Perspective: Break free from repetitive thinking by engaging the creative, intuitive side of your brain.
Tools for Daily Coping: Learn how the simple act of making art can become a sanctuary for processing stress and finding grounding.
A Pathway to Wholeness: Explore how visual expression can reveal hidden strengths and foster a deeper sense of self-care.
Important Note: You do absolutely not need to be an artist or have any artistic experience to attend. This day is about the process of expression, not the final product. While this workshop is not a substitute for clinical individual or group therapy, it is a powerful, supportive introduction to the healing power of the arts.
What to Bring:
A journal and a pen or pencil. All other creative materials will be provided.  Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks and  photo ID.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Bike Maintenance for Beginners
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Bicycle Maintenance for Beginners
Have you recently started riding a bicycle and want to make sure you can take care of it properly? Or have you been riding for ages, but have always been scared to fix anything yourself?
Are you unsure of how to pump your tyres, or how much oil your chain needs? Find yourself fumbling for words when trying to describe that clunking sound to the guy in the bike shop?
This one day course lays bare the nuts and bolts of bicycle mechanics for absolute beginners, as well as those with a little experience. Through practical experience working with your own bicycle, you will find out what needs to be done to keep it running smoothly. We’ll cover what to look out for when things start to wear out, and how to check for problems, so you can be confident your bicycle is safe to ride. You will also learn how to fix some of the most common mechanical problems, and learn about the correct terminology and tools to use.
Those who feel intimidated in bike shops are especially welcome in this course. No question is a stupid question!
Bringing a bike to work on is essential, preferably one that you are riding regularly, because the best way to learn is by building familiarity with your own ride. E-bikes are welcome, although the extra weight can mean they are more challenging to work on. Regardless of whether your bike is in pristine condition, or desperately in need of TLC, it is welcome on the course – bikes showing a bit more wear can be useful for the learning of the whole group.
Bring your pushbike along on the day.  If you have the following, please bring them as well:  A multi-tool and pump; chain oil and rag; lightweight close-fitting gardening or rubber gloves.
Note: A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
(Please note this course is not exhaustive and is not a professional training course).
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Name most parts of a bicycle correctly
- Perform a quick safety check on any bicycle
- Fix a flat tyre
- Adjust your bike to fit your body
- Oil and clean your chain
- Identify and fix some common brake problems
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Retirement Reinvented
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
In your middle years, working, retired or somewhere in between? What’s next? Life is about much more than work or leisure, but most of us have given little thought to what “retirement” might mean.
It’s difficult to speculate what may happen in the future – but we can be proactive and take control.
This course offers insights into how to make the most of our time once we’re less focused on career and/or childrearing. It covers many of the issues people face when considering a move from current employment to a different lifestyle that includes more time to do the things we’ve always promised ourselves we’d do – “when we retire”.
After the workshop, you’ll be able to identify a number of common issues and potential ways to manage them when considering and planning your “rejuvenation”, rather than a retirement. We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
By the end of the day, you’ll have:
Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you
Completed a personal life audit exercise and considered your values and your strengths
Considered options to include a sense of purpose and explore choices that can provide you with that sense of purpose
Explored possibilities in the major aspects of your life and identified potential challenges and strategies for overcoming them
Begun to develop your blueprint to maximise the best years of your life and have considered a “future proofing” downsizing plan.
Bring pen and paper.

events.id: Coptic Book Binding Workshop-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Coptic Book Binding Workshop
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Coptic binding is one of the earliest forms of creating a book, with raw simplicity you can produce a book of any size with the unique feature of opening out flat. No special tools or materials are needed and yet a wide spectrum of creative results can be created, from a notebook, sketch book and album to a highly crafted artwork. The books themselves can be made from found items, recycled material or quality art papers and card.

In this workshop you will be guided in assembling your chosen materials for your book, create decorative covers and learn Coptic binding - an elegant and simple binding that is unlimited in versatility. You will produce one bound book and one bound album. Once you have Coptic binding in your skill set you can produce your choice of books in any shape or form, for any purpose.

All basic materials supplied.

Half an hour for lunch. Bring a drink bottle and a packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy House or explore the cafes in Te Aro. Coffee & tea provided at lunch.

You must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course or attend with a paying adult.

events.name: Finding Tiny Moments of Joy in Everyday Life
events.venue: Project 100Nelson, Nelson Region
events.long_description:
Overview





Do you need more joy and calmness in your life? Then this workshop about how to find small joys in the world might be for you!
In an increasingly frenetic world with social media and news cycles encouraging us to see things as increasingly doom and gloom, this workshop will help you recalibrate by using micro journaling to rediscover the small joys in your everyday life.
Because while we can’t change the big things, sometimes a small shift to a more positive outlook can help us go about our day-to-day lives less stressed and more resilient.
With fun, practical steps George Penney, author of the US, UK and Australian bestselling book of people watching vignettes, Tiny Moments of Joy: Spotted on Market Day in Aotearoa New Zealand, will guide you through looking at the world around you with fresh eyes, finding moments of peace, calm and even happiness.


For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

Tickets here
Eyegum has worked hard to curate a programme that is sure to offer something for everyone, from first time gig-goers to seasoned live music obsessives. The eclectic lineup includes national treasures like Bic Runga and Savage, heavy-hitting legends Beastwars, Kody Nielson’s enigmatic project Silicon, indie math rockers So So Modern, powerhouse party starter Mokotron, local hip hop sensation MĀ, and everything in between.
Tonic Collective are back with an impeccably curated lineup for their travelling stage, which includes Pitch Black celebrating 30 years as Aotearoa electronica pioneers and award winning sonic explorer Amamelia.
It's not all music, three of our best poets Chris Tse, Dani Yourukova, and Jackson McCarthy will also perform.

Eyegum Music Collective presents GREAT SOUNDS GREAT, a multi-venue music and arts festival taking over Pōneke's Te Aro precinct for one night only on Saturday 5 September 2026. Showcasing 40 of Aotearoa's best artists across 10 neighbouring venues, this is one big party you shouldn't miss.
Eyegum has worked hard to curate a programme that is sure to offer something for everyone, from first time gig-goers to seasoned live music obsessives. The eclectic lineup includes national treasures like Bic Runga and Savage, heavy-hitting legends Beastwars, Kody Nielson’s enigmatic project Silicon, indie math rockers So So Modern, powerhouse party starter Mokotron, local hip hop sensation MĀ, and everything in between.
Tonic Collective are back with an impeccably curated lineup for their travelling stage, which includes Pitch Black celebrating 30 years as Aotearoa electronica pioneers and award winning sonic explorer Amamelia.
It's not all music, three of our best poets Chris Tse, Dani Yourukova, and Jackson McCarthy will also perform.
Excitingly for 2026, we are adding a new venue, the incomparable Meow Nui, helping make this year's event bigger and better than ever. We are also throwing a warm-up party, The Night Before, across three venues in Newtown village on Friday 4 September. This will showcase 12 incredible up-and-coming artists and is the perfect way to prepare for the main event.
Ticket holders will receive a wristband that will give them access to each of the participating venues throughout the event. Information on how to pick up wristbands will be provided to ticket holders closer to the time.
Presented with support from Abandoned Brewery, RadioActive.FM, and Wellington City Council.
Venues: Meow Nui, San Fran, Meow, Valhalla, Rogue & Vagabond, Bedlam & Squalor, Hotel Bristol, St Peter's on Willis, Flying Nun Records, Tonic Travelling Stage.

events.long_description:
The Spring Fling Express
🌼🚂 The Spring Fling Express – A Heritage Rail Journey to Central Hawke’s Bay’s Biggest Spring Celebration! 🚂🌼

Saturday 5th September 2026

Celebrate the arrival of spring aboard Steam Incorporated’s Spring Fling Express, a special return rail journey from the Kāpiti Coast and Manawatū to Waipukurau for the opening weekend of Central Hawke’s Bay’s much-loved Spring Fling festivities. Travel behind heritage diesel locomotive Da 1410 through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge and some of the North Island’s most picturesque countryside aboard our beautifully restored heritage train.

Once in Waipukurau, choose how you'd like to spend your day:

🌼 Taniwha Daffodils Experience
Enjoy coach transfers to the famous Taniwha Daffodils, where thousands of blooms create a spectacular spring display. Wander the gardens, soak up the atmosphere, enjoy a packed lunch, and even pick your own daffodils to take home.

☕ Explore Waipukurau at Your Own Pace
Spend the day discovering local cafés, shops, gardens and attractions before re-joining the train for the journey home. Perfect for those wanting a relaxed day out in the heart of Central Hawke’s Bay.

🚉 Boarding from:
Paekākāriki, Paraparaumu, Waikanae, Ōtaki, Levin and Palmerston North.

🎟 Fares from just $119 Adult / $99 Child
🌼 Taniwha Daffodils packages available!

Whether you're chasing spring colour, exploring a charming country town, or simply enjoying a day aboard one of New Zealand’s most unique heritage rail experiences, the Spring Fling Express promises a memorable day out for the whole family. Seats are limited and advance booking is essential. 🌸🚂

Mantra, Pranayama & Meditation Course
You practice asana but do you practice YOGA?

This intensive workshop explores the foundational theory, embodied practice, and teaching methodology of pranayama, meditation, and mantra — three profound and transformative limbs of yoga.

Over two full days (plus pre-recorded content to complete in your own time), you'll cover breathing physiology and the subtle body, foundational meditation techniques across multiple lineages, the ethics of mantra, and safe trauma-aware instruction. The workshop includes extensive practice teaching time with peer feedback — so you leave not just informed, but ready to teach.

What you'll learn:
*Breathing physiology and the subtle body
*Foundational meditation techniques across multiple lineages
*The theory and ethics of mantra
*Trauma-aware instruction for breath and meditation practices
*Practice teaching with structured peer feedback

Format:
* Two full-day in-person intensives (9:00 am – 5:00 pm) on Saturday 5th September & Saturday 26th September 2026
*Pre-recorded content to complete between sessions at your own pace
*One optional online wānanga to follow up after the course concludes (date/time TBD)

Who can enrol:
There are no restrictions on who can enrol for this course. Anyone with an interest in learning more about yoga beyond asana is welcome - Haere mai!

200-CYTs can receive 25 Continuing Education credits with Yoga Alliance *or* earn 25 hours towards AYS's 300hr YTT pathway!

Facilitator:
Tom Brotherstone (E-RYT 500) - AWHI co-owner with over a decade of teaching experience in Yin and Vinyasa yoga. Tom trained in Rishikesh, India and his focus is on building community through practice — providing supportive platforms for growth and self-discovery. His easeful, approachable style puts students immediately at ease, and his classes weave yoga philosophy throughout, grounding movement in meaning.

events.name: Mel Parsons - Castle Hill Album Release Tour
events.venue: The Opera House, 111 - 113 Manners Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
Singer-songwriting luminary, Mel Parsons, has announced a seven-date national theatre tour with her band in August and September 2026, celebrating her much-anticipated new album, CASTLE HILL, to released on August 7.

Plus1 proudly presents Mel Parsons live around Aotearoa in some of our country's most beautiful theatres.

Thursday August 27 - Theatre Royal, Nelson
Friday August 28 - Isaac Theatre Royal, Christchurch
Saturday August 29 - Glenroy Auditorium, Dunedin
Thursday September 3 - Clarence St Theatre, Hamilton
Friday September 4 - Q Theatre, Rangatira - Auckland
Saturday September 5 - Opera House, Wellington
Sunday September 6 - Globe Theatre, Palmerston North

Full tour info at plus1.co.nz and MelParsons.com

Taking its name from the remote mountain town in the Southern Alps where it was recorded, CASTLE HILL was produced by Josh Logan and recorded live with Mel’s longtime band members Aaron Stewart (bass) and Jed Parsons (drums); joined by Ben King (Goldenhorse, Grand Rapids) on guitars. Parsons says of these sessions: “it was a full immersion recording experience over a stolen summer holiday”

Following the release of SABOTAGE in 2024, multi-award winning Parsons toured the country with Crowded House, performed in Canada and Australia, and has continued her stellar run including a finalist nod for Best Folk Artist at the 2026 AMA’s.

Singles already released from the record include the alternative radio chart toppers Post High Slide, Brick By Brick, Be Here Now, Don't Leave The Light On, and Caravan, as well as new single Grain By Grain. Castle Hill album release tour is funded through NZ On Air and supported by the NZ Music Commission.

Expect soaring harmonies, a dynamic live show, and a feel-good vibe throughout as Mel Parsons performs live this August and September. Come and celebrate one of Aotearoa’s finest live artists!

events.name: Trip: Raumati South Peatlands
events.venue: Poplar Ave, Raumati South, Paraparaumu 5032,Paraparaumu, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Trip: Raumati South Peatlands
This property was originally held by the Crown as an alternative route for the Kāpiti Expressway. Now planned for housing, large areas are protected SNAs including an area of mostly intact mānukā/kanuka fen which is unusual on the Kāpiti Coast.

Species of note include Scrambling Coral-Fern (Gleichenia microphylla) and Fork-leaved Sundew (Drosera binata). Time can also be spent determining the presence of Kunzea robusta and/or Kunzea amathicola.

Meet: 9:30 am at entrance of Te Rā school. Park at the QEP entrance and cross the road, please don’t park at the school. If travelling by train a pick-up can be organised from Paeākāriki Station, or walk 3.6 km/50min from Paraparaumu Station.

Leader: Andy McKay (Tel 04 296 4653, Mobile 027 555 5653, )

events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Widely regarded as one of the foremost songwriters of her generation, Suzanne Vega emerged as a leading figure of the folk revival of the early 1980s. Four decades later, she is still writing and singing great songs. In her Wellington show, Suzanne will perform a career-spanning set. See her on stage at St James Theatre performing favourites like Tom’s Diner, Luka, Marlene On The Wall, and plenty more. There’ll also be new songs from her 2025 album, ‘Flying with Angels’. Joining her on stage will be longtime guitarist, Gerry Leonard, and cellist Stephanie Winters. 
Since the release of her self-titled, critically acclaimed 1985 debut album, Suzanne Vega has played to sold-out concerts across the world. She is a masterful storyteller who, according to one The New York Times critique, “observes the world with a clinically poetic eye.” Her song lyrics often focus on city life, ordinary people, and real-world subjects. They are notably succinct, understated, and immediately recognisable.

events.long_description:
The Tui Express
Climb aboard The Tui Express for a spectacular, first-class rail experience. This is our fan-favourite excursion and an unforgettable scenic journey aboard our premium carriages, making it the perfect, easy day out for anyone looking to enjoy a fantastic Sunday on the rails with friends and family. It also falls on Father's Day weekend, offering a wonderful opportunity to treat Dad.

The undisputed crown jewel of this journey is our passage through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge. With the old highway permanently closed, the rail line offers an exclusive, front-row seat to this rugged natural wonder. Watch the dramatic river below and feel the history as we steam through the gorge's tunnels. There is no better place to experience this than from our open-air viewing platform, the ultimate vantage point for taking photos, hearing the thunderous echo of the steam locomotive, and catching the crisp air of the Manawatū Gorge.
Throughout the trip, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. You can sit back, relax, and purchase a range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, hot espresso coffees, and sweet treats right from the rails as the scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight to Mangatainoka Station. Upon arrival, step off the platform and stretch your legs with a flat, leisurely 15-minute walk to the world-famous Tui Brewery, or hop directly onto one of our dedicated transfer buses waiting for you. Once at the brewery, relax and enjoy the iconic historic grounds. Your ticket includes a delicious, hearty BBQ buffet lunch and a complimentary Tui beverage (or non-alcoholic alternative) to wash it down. If you prefer to opt out of the meal, you can do so during booking for a discounted fare.

Your ticket covers your return journey from Plimmerton in beautifully maintained premium carriages alongside exclusive rail-only views of the Manawatū Gorge, rugged cliffs, and historic tunnels. You will have unrestricted access to the open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography, plus full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling refreshments, espresso coffees, and snacks. At the destination, you get a freshly prepared BBQ buffet lunch inside the iconic Tui Brewery grounds, one complimentary Tui beer, cider, or non-alcoholic beverage, and free transfer buses between Mangatainoka Station and the brewery.

Approximate Itinerary
Morning Travel – Northbound to Mangatainoka
Plimmerton depart – 7:50am
Paraparaumu depart – 8:25am
Ōtaki depart – 9:15am
Levin depart – 9:50am
Palmerston North depart – 11:00am
Mangatainoka arrive – 12:15pm

Evening Travel – Return Journey
Mangatainoka depart – 2:15pm
Palmerston North depart – 4:20pm
Levin depart – 5:15pm
Ōtaki depart – 5:40pm
Paraparaumu depart – 6:25pm
Plimmerton arrive – 6:50pm

Space in these premium carriages is strictly limited and this fan-favourite trip fills up incredibly fast, so secure your tickets today for an incredible Sunday on the rails!

events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Join us for this fabulous introduction to working with colourful molten glass at the Winter Special Price!

This class is a great way for absolute beginners to get a taste of working with glass to produce beautiful beads that can be used in a myriad of ways, including making a unique gift for your loved one (or yourself!).

As one of the earliest forms of human adornment, beads have long functioned as a way to express individuality, and what better way to do that than to learn to make your own unique beads?

Students are shown correct lampworking techniques to produce several decorative beads in just 3 hours! How many beads you make is up to you; some students make up to 10 while others make fewer using trickier techniques.

Kids over 12 (or so) are welcome to take the class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.name: Silver Clay Taster
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join us to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Precious Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.

Beginners start with simple pendants/earrings. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!

Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Precious Metal Clay is the ultimate recyclable material!

Included in the course fee is 5 grams of fine silver clay, enough to make a pendant or earrings, or a collection of charms - it's up to you.

Extra findings such as earring hooks and chains will be available to purchase (you can also make your earring hooks if you are feeling adventurous).

This class is great for kids also but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany any person under the age of 16.

events.venue: Toi Aro Arts Centre, 3-6 Market Lane, Wellington
events.long_description:
Spend a cosy evening in our warm, welcoming studio and create something truly special with your own hands.

In this relaxed 3 hour class, you’ll learn how to transform simple square wire into an elegant twisted ring. We’ll guide you through softening and twisting metal to create beautiful, flowing forms, then show you how to shape your ring to fit perfectly.

You’ll get hands-on with the jeweller’s torch to solder your piece, before refining and polishing it to a stunning, professional finish. It’s a satisfying process from start to finish - and you’ll head home with a ring you made yourself.

Copper is included in the class fee, and if you’d like to elevate your piece, sterling silver is available to purchase in the studio.

Perfect for complete beginners, a fun evening out with friends, or a memorable creative experience while visiting the city. It’s also a great next step if you’ve taken one of our Stacking Rings or Textured Earrings classes and want to keep building your jewellery collection.

Suitable for ages 12 and up. Please note that anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Widely regarded as one of the foremost songwriters of her generation, Suzanne Vega emerged as a leading figure of the folk revival of the early 1980s. Accompanying herself on acoustic guitar, Vega sang what has been called contemporary folk or neo-folk songs of her own creation in Greenwich Village clubs. Since the release of her self-titled, critically acclaimed 1985 debut album, she has given sold-out concerts in many of the world’s best-known venues. Known for performances that convey deep emotion, Vega’s distinctive, “clear, unwavering voice” (Rolling Stone) has been described as “a cool, dry sandpaper-brushed near-whisper” by The Washington Post, with NPR Music noting that she “has been making vital, inventive music” throughout the course of her decades-long career. Bearing the stamp of a masterful storyteller who “observes the world with a clinically poetic eye” (The New York Times), Vega’s songs have tended to focus on city life, ordinary people and real-world subjects. Notably succinct and understated, her work is immediately recognizable—as utterly distinct and thoughtful as it was when her voice was first heard on the radio over 40 years ago.

events.long_description:
Dying Matters Week Wellington Region
Dying Matters Week connects people across Aotearoa to start conversations in a safe space, learn from local experts and seek support to plan for later life and end-of-life and to navigate grief and loss.

Dying Matters Week will occur throughout the Wellington Region with different events occuring over the week. Dying Matters to us all because, it will happen to us all. How it happens and how we deal with it can make the biggest difference to both us and the people who love and care for us. This week is designed to expand the conversation and provide information and resources to enable all of us to be empowered around death and not to be frightened of it. Individual events will be featured on this page with details about how to access each event.

In a supportive, hands-on studio environment, you’ll learn the essential skills needed to confidently design and create your own fused glass pieces. events.long_description:
Cooking: Gourmet Sausage Making
Come along and learn how to fill sausage casings with a tasty mincemeat and get tips and tricks on how to make your own customized sausage mixes at home with the use of various herbs and spices. Everyone will get some sausages to take home and enjoy.
All ingredients included in course fee but please bring your apron, a dish cloth and a couple of tea towels to the session. 
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-  Recognise how to handle a knife safely
-  Understand food safety and hygiene around sausage-making and avoiding cross contamination
-  Recognise the difference between two kinds of sausage casings and why you use each of them

events.long_description:
Comedy, cabaret, poetry, family-friendly acts, and world premieres are all on the radar for this theatrical event. The annual TAHI NZ Festival of Solo Performance provides a stage for more than 25 actors, celebrating emerging artists to experienced professionals. Storylines vary from rugby to the manosphere to an improvised nature documentary. Laughing and crying are both considered acceptable responses.

Tahi in Te Reo Māori translates to ‘one’, but another translation for this word is ’unity’. Dr. Sally Richards, director of TAHI, chose the name because of this duality. Solo theatre requires both personal courage and creative collaboration. As Sally says, “I see the stage manager, broom in hand, sweep before and after a performance. It reminds me that the solo performer is a misnomer — that solo performance relies on successful collaboration with others.”

Discover the brilliance of solo theatre at TAHI this September.

events.long_description:
Overview

Create a team that communicates better, takes ownership, and solves problems together.

Every team experiences tension.

A conversation goes sideways. Someone starts blaming. Another person steps in to fix everything. Before long, the real issue has been lost and the same pattern begins again.

This free leadership session will help you recognise those patterns and respond differently.

Leadership: Escape the Drama Triangle is a practical 90-minute workshop for business owners and team leaders who want their people to communicate clearly, take greater ownership, and solve problems together.

During the session, we will explore how workplace conversations can fall into the roles of Victim, Rescuer and Villain, and how leaders can help shift those conversations from blame, excuses and denial towards responsibility, accountability and ownership. This reflects the workbook’s movement from the “Victim Cycle” to the “Victor Cycle” and its focus on improving the quality of words, conversations, relationships, collaboration and achievement.

You will learn how to:

Recognise the Drama Triangle in everyday team conversations
Identify when people are operating below the line
Avoid rescuing, blaming or taking over
Reframe conversations so people can take responsibility
Create clearer, more productive team discussions
Help your team move from problems towards practical next steps

This is not about removing every disagreement from your workplace.

It is about giving you a simple way to recognise unhelpful patterns early and guide the conversation towards a better outcome.

You will leave with practical language and ideas you can begin using with your team straight away.

Who is this for?

This session is suitable for:

Business owners
Managers and team leaders
People responsible for workplace culture
Leaders dealing with repeated communication issues
Anyone who finds themselves stepping in to solve everyone else’s problems

Event details

Date: 9 September 
Time: 12:00 pm–1:30 pm 
Venue: Paraparaumu Beach Golf Club 
Cost: Free

Places are limited, so early registration is recommended.

events.long_description:
Overview

Share ceremonial cacao, heartfelt conversation and a nourishing dinner in an evening of authentic connection and presence.

Cacao & Connection Circle
Starts at 6pm

This evening is an invitation to slow down, be present, and experience genuine human connection. Together we'll share ceremonial cacao, meaningful conversation, and a welcoming space where there's no need to perform, impress, or have all the right words. Just come as you are.

What to Expect

We'll begin with a gentle grounding practice to help everyone arrive. This is an opportunity to pause, settle into the present moment, and reconnect with yourself before connecting with others.

From there, we'll gather in a circle to share ceremonial cacao. 

We'll then move into a heart-sharing circle. A thoughtful question will be offered as a prompt, and you're warmly invited, but never expected to share your experience. There is no advice-giving or fixing here. Instead, we practise honest expression, deep listening, and creating space for one another to simply be witnessed.

What Heart-Sharing Can Offer

 Authentic Connection

Experience the kind of connection that comes from being seen, heard, and accepted exactly as you are.

Meaningful Conversation

Step beyond everyday small talk into conversations that invite honesty, curiosity, and presence.

Greater Self-Awareness

Sharing and listening often brings unexpected clarity about your own thoughts, emotions, and life experiences.

Gentle Personal Growth

Speaking from the heart and listening without judgement can quietly shift perspectives and deepen understanding.

A Sense of Belonging

Being part of a supportive circle can ease feelings of isolation and remind us that we all share common human experiences.

 

After the circle, we'll enjoy a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert together, both included in your ticket. It's a relaxed time to continue conversations, connect naturally, and simply enjoy each other's company.

Meet Andre, your host:

Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human, how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.

events.long_description:
Overview

Journey inward through Māori sound, pūrākau and crystal bowls, creating a peaceful evening of deep listening, rest and restoration.

Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey




Starts at 6pm

Experience a peaceful Māori sound journey blending taonga pūoro, story, and crystal bowls for deep relaxation and inner calm

“Āio” speaks to peace and inner calm. In this immersive evening, pūrākau, taonga pūoro and waiata are woven together with the healing vibrations of crystal singing bowls, creating a space for deep listening, rest and restoration.

The organic tones of traditional Māori instruments including kōauau, pūtōrino, porotiti and pūtātara blend with the resonance of crystal bowls, chimes and ukulele, inviting you to slow down, soften and reconnect with your wairua and body. Through story, sound and vibration, this is a gentle journey inward.

What to bring:

Yoga mats, blankets and cushions will be provided, but you are welcome to bring extra for comfort!




After the sound journey, share in a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, included in your ticket, a warm way to close the evening together.

Meet your hosts & musicians: Smita, Peter, and Alexandra:

Smita (Ngāi Te Rangi) was born and raised in Aotearoa. From a young age she was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.

Peter is Pākehā, with grandparents from England and Ireland, and has been on a four-year journey learning the art of taonga pūoro — the traditional Māori musical instruments of Aotearoa. Guided by the wisdom and generosity of expert makers and players, he has learned both to craft and to play these unique instruments. For Peter, taonga pūoro offer a way to connect deeply with sound, story, and the natural world, and he is excited to share their voices as part of this sound bath experience.

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from artists such as Deva Premal, The Flying Mystics, Stevin McNamara, and the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

events.long_description:
Pub Sing - where the audience turns into the choir at the pub, with a live rock band,

No sheet music, no experience needed, and absolutely no solos.

Katy reveals three songs on the night (usually a crowd-pleaser, a ballad, and a banger), and even if you don’t know them, you’ll pick them up fast with colour-coded lyrics on screen.

You learn different harmony options, sing along with the band, and blend into a room of up to 80 voices, so no one’s listening to you; they’re singing with you.

There’s banter, laughs, a bit of silliness, and a whole lot of feel-good energy. It’s not karaoke (shudder), it’s everyone singing together just for the fun of it, and it’s the perfect end-of-week lift you needed.

*All ticket sales goes directly to the band*

events.name: Big Low Dream - Wellington
events.venue: Hannah Playhouse,12 Cambridge Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Big Low Dream - Wellington
BIG LOW DREAM is a new contemporary dance work about what we reach for, together, in the dark. Choreographer Jessie McCall looks to dream logic - unruly, queer, ethically imaginative, as a way to hold onto meaning in a time of overlapping crises. Paradises slip their frames. Unexpected pleasures co-inhabit with the unthinkable. Spectacle flirts with collapse.

Ominous and funny, intimate and sweeping, BIG LOW DREAM is a rehearsal of possible futures — tender, desperate, and rising.

Choose Your Price Night - preview show Thurs 10 Sept 7pm

Creative Team
Choreography: Jessie McCall
Production Design: Meg Rollandi
Sound Design: Thomas Lambert
Lighting Design: Tony Black

Cast
Airu Matsuda, Caleb Heke, Sasha Matsumoto, Millie Maden

Praise for Jesie McCall:

"Through the combined impact of dance and design, McCall enables multiple truths to coexist, just as they do in our reality… This is a production in the hands of an artist who knows precisely what they’re doing. It’s focused and formidable; well-made and compelling." - Tate Fountain, Bad Apple, 13 October 2022 for I GET SO EMOTIONAL BABY

“Deeply perceptive and provocative work… It does exactly what art is supposed to do – it opens a window into our soul, and shines a light on moments we may often try to keep hidden.” - Emily Napolitano, Theatreview for TASSEL ME THIS

Emerson: Leap! on Tour at San Fran
Emerson and her band are hitting the road to celebrate the release of her debut EP, Leap!
The first headline tour marks a major milestone for one of Aotearoa's most exciting emerging pop artists. Showcasing her growth as both a songwriter and performer, Leap! reflects the diverse musical world Emerson has built over the past two years since winning the Smokefree Rockquest Solo-Duo Award in 2024.
Audiences can sing along to infectious pop hooks, connect with her honest storytelling, dance to fan favourites, and experience the electric live energy that has helped her build a dedicated following across New Zealand.
With support from ZM Radio and a catalogue that includes fan favourites such as Bored, Tip of My Tongue, Show U Off, and Want Him Bad!, Emerson's live show is packed with the songs that have fuelled her rapid rise, alongside brand-new music from Leap!.
Whether you've been following her journey from the beginning or are discovering her music for the first time, Leap! On Tour is a celebration of taking chances, backing yourself, and embracing the unknown. After all, the most exciting adventures often begin with a leap of faith.

Pioneers of the iconic Madchester sound, the Happy Mondays are heading back to New Zealand to celebrate the 35th anniversary of their seminal album, Pills 'n' Thrills and Bellyaches.
Fusing funk, rock, psychedelia, and house with the pulsating energy of the UK’s burgeoning rave scene, the Happy Mondays became the face of a cultural revolution. Their 1990 release, Pills 'n' Thrills and Bellyaches, catapulted them into the mainstream, spending over six months on the UK Albums Chart and earning its place as one of the defining records of the decade.

Their enduring influence on British music was formally recognised in 2016 when they received the prestigious Ivor Novello Inspiration Award, a testament to their legacy as one of the UK’s most beloved and groundbreaking bands.
‘Always a great buzz when we play Australia and New Zealand . Looking forward to bringing the Happy Mondays Pills ‘n’ Thrills party there in September’’ - Shaun Ryder
This isn’t just a tour, it’s a full-throttle revival of Madchester chaos, and the year's wildest party is coming.

events.long_description:
AI Masterclass: Going Further with AI
(NZ Citizens and residents pay $250 with ID.)
You’ve been using AI for a while – maybe daily. You know how to prompt. But you’re still doing one-shot chats when your work deserves a proper system. This masterclass changes that.
Before you arrive, you’ll fill in a short intake form – what you do, what you want AI for, and what you can’t do (paste client data into public ChatGPT, work outside regulated tools, etc.). Jon reads every submission before class and shapes the day around the room. We won’t be doing a generic feature tour; the day is built to be a hands-on and customised workshop.
We’ll spend the day wiring AI into your actual work: the Claude desktop app, connectors to the tools you already use, a project built around your real documents and tasks, and Claude Design. You’ll leave with a working AI system to improve your life and work.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
•     Set up the Claude desktop app with Chat, Co-work, and Code – ready for real work
•     Enable and use connectors (Gmail, Drive, calendar) – and know which ones to leave off
•     Build a Claude project around your own documents and tasks, with voice input and plan mode
•     Write operating rules for your workspace – constraints, verification triggers, what never goes in public chat
•     Discover and run Anthropic-provided skills on your real task
•     Stress-test your output with synthetic personas before you ship
•     Produce polished visual artifacts with Claude Design
•     Apply professional judgement: when to delegate, when to verify, when not to use AI at all
 Please bring: A laptop (Co-work and Code need a keyboard). The Claude desktop app installed and signed in. A paid Claude subscription (Pro or Team) – required for connectors, Co-work, and skills. Your intake form submitted at least 3 days before class. One real task you want to work on.
  A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".
