events.name: Burnout to Balance - Proven Techniques to Pause, Recover & Return!
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
In today’s high-pressure world, burnout is often worn as a badge of honour—until the physical and mental toll becomes impossible to ignore. True recovery requires more than just "taking a break"; it requires resetting the nervous system from the inside out.
Led by Simon, a former high-stakes litigation lawyer who successfully navigated his own severe burnout, this workshop bridges the gap between understanding stress and actively healing from it. This practical, evidence-based workshop is designed to take you on a journey from chronic depletion to sustainable balance. You will explore what burnout actually is, identify your personal triggers, and master powerful physiological techniques to pause the stress response, recover your vitality, and return to life and work with renewed resilience.
What We Will Cover
Part 1: Understanding the Burnout Cycle (The Setup)
Before we can fix the problem, we must understand it. We begin by unpacking the foundations of chronic stress to help you map your own journey.
What is Burnout? Defining the psychological and physical parameters of exhaustion.
The Root Causes: Identifying the systemic, professional, and personal drivers of chronic stress.
The Nervous System Hijack: How prolonged pressure traps the body in a constant "fight-or-flight" state, impacting sleep, digestion, and cognitive function.
Part 2: The Science of Physiological Recovery (The Solution)
While mindset matters, burnout lives in the body. We will introduce the fastest, most effective tool for resetting a hijacked nervous system: Functional Breathing Training.
The Three Dimensions of Health: How biochemical, biomechanical, and psychophysiological breathing patterns dictate your stress levels.
Measuring Your Stress Tolerance: Learn how to assess your current breathing efficiency and physiological stress baseline.
Immediate Relief vs. Long-Term Resilience: Practices that offer instant calm during acute anxiety, paired with lifelong training to rebuild your nervous system.
What You Will Walk Away With
By the end of this one-day workshop, you will:
Recognise the Warning Signs: Deeply understand your own burnout triggers and early warning indicators.
Interrupt the Stress Response: Master proven, discreet techniques to pause the "fight-or-flight" response in real-time.
Improve Everyday Well-being: Know how to optimise your breathing patterns to combat poor sleep, fatigue, and brain fog.
A Personalised Recovery Plan: Walk away with a practical toolkit to integrate self-regulation and physical recovery into a busy professional life.
What to Bring: Please bring a notepad and pen to track your personal pacing metrics, record your breathing patterns, and map out your recovery strategy.
Participant Self-Management & Safety
This workshop is designed for adult learners. It is a supportive, respectful space where you are encouraged to engage at your own comfort level and self-manage your energy throughout the day (including taking breaks to decompress as needed).
Please note: The advanced physiological recovery techniques practiced in this workshop are highly effective for nervous system regulation. No prior experience with breathwork or yoga is required.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
“Relationships are all there is. Everything in the universe only exists because it is in relationship to everything else. Nothing exists in isolation. We have to stop pretending we are individuals that can go it alone.” -Margaret J. Wheatley
You aren't alone. In a world of screens, finding genuine, in-person connection can feel surprisingly tough. But building a supportive network and circles doesn't require a total personality makeover—it starts with who you already are.
This hands-on, high-energy workshop is designed to help you map out your unique strengths, passions, and existing ties to build a community where you truly belong. We skip the generic networking advice and dive straight into practical, real-world tools to help you spark meaningful relationships.
What you’ll walk away with:
Your Personal Connection Map: A clear overview of your unique interests, strengths, and hidden community links.
The "Icebreaker" Blueprint: 1–2 simple frameworks to confidently shift casual small talk into deeper, more rewarding conversations.
The "Reach Out" Breakthrough: Break the ice right then and there by sending two messages or writing a letter during the session—getting the hardest part out of the way!
A Ready-to-Use Action Plan: A customised roadmap to connect with 1–3 new or existing friends, with your first milestone already crushed before you leave.
"Networking is not about just connecting people. It's about connecting people with people, people with ideas, and people with opportunities." — Michele Jennae
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Overview

A self-publishing workshop delivered by an internationally bestselling author.

Are you interested in learning how to become a full-time self-supporting author?

Want to see your name on best-seller lists around the world?

Have you always dreamed of seeing a book that you wrote on the shelves at your local bookshop or library, available for anyone to read?

Or maybe you dream of being published with one of the big traditional publishing houses but have discovered that the main way they're picking up books nowadays is by scooping up already successful independently published authors?

This three hour workshop will be delivered by George Penney, an internationally bestselling author of fiction and non-fiction, a twenty-year industry veteran who has been published both through Penguin Random House and independently, and the owner of Swashbuckler Press, an independent publishing company formerly based in London--now in Nelson, New Zealand.

It will provide you with a crash-course rundown on how to independently publish and distribute your novels, poems and short stories, using the same processes, editors, cover designers, and distribution techniques as the large publishing houses.

Participants will leave with a solid starter-foundation for establishing a successful publishing career.

For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

Awaken Your Intuition - the Third Eye Chakra
Tap into your inner knowing through Kundalini Yoga, breathwork, meditation and sound.

About this Event

This workshop is part of an 8-part chakra journey across 2026. Each session stands alone or can be experienced as part of the full series.
Join us for an afternoon of deep connection as we explore the Third Eye Chakra (Ajna) through the powerful practices of Kundalini Yoga and the healing vibrations of a Gong Bath.
The Third Eye Chakra is the centre of intuition, insight, clarity, and inner knowing. When balanced, it helps you trust your intuition, quiet mental chatter, and see life's path with greater clarity. Through movement, breathwork, meditation, and sound, we'll create space to connect with your inner wisdom and restore balance to this energy centre.

🧘‍♀️Kundalini Yoga | 1:30pm – 3:00pm
Experience a 90-minute Kundalini Yoga class designed to awaken the Third Eye Chakra through breathwork (Pranayama), dynamic movement and postures, meditation, and deep relaxation.

☕Herbal Tea Break | 3:00pm – 3:30pm
Take time to relax, enjoy a cup of herbal tea, oracle cards and connect with others in a welcoming and supportive environment.

🎶Gong Bath | 3:30pm – 4:30pm
Lie back, get comfortable, and allow the soothing sounds and vibrations of the gong to guide you into a deeply restorative state of relaxation. A gong bath can help calm the nervous system, release stress, and leave you feeling refreshed and centred.
✨Choose the experience that suits you—you are welcome to attend either the yoga or the gong bath sessions or enjoy the full afternoon.
💫Suitable for beginners and experienced practitioners alike - no experience with yoga or sound healing needed. Modifications are offered throughout the yoga class.
💫 Bring an open heart, a yoga mat, blanket, water bottle and anything you need to feel cozy + supported.
✨Whether you're joining the entire afternoon or just one session, you'll leave feeling calmer, clearer, and more deeply connected to yourself.
Spaces are limited, so bookings are recommended.
Investment:
$35 Yoga | $30 Gong Bath | $55 Both
Special discounted ticket options:
$100 two person special - bring a friend with you to attend the yoga and the gong session. Must select this ticket option for the discount to apply (i.e. both people must book together).
$150 three workshop special - for one person to attend the last three workshops in this series (both kundalini yoga and gong bath) - on 12 September (third eye), 18 October (crown), and 6 December (aura). Must select this ticket option for the discount to apply (i.e. all 3 workshops must be booked together).
If you want to pay by cash on the day or by bank transfer, please send an email to to book your place.


Agenda

Info: Move, breathe, and reset your energy with a nourishing Kundalini Yoga practice to clear the mind, reset your energy, and reconnect with your body. No prior experience necessary - open to all levels.

Gong Bath | $30
Info: Soothe your nervous system and bathe in the healing frequencies of the gong. This is a deeply restful, restorative session — no movement required, just lie back and receive.

Overview

Experience Marlborough’s Arts Trail and Gala Evening with Michael Hurst. Art, artists, and inspiration.

The Alzheimers Arts Trail returns for its fifth year on 19 & 20 September 2026, showcasing the depth and diversity of artistic talent across Marlborough.

Now a much-anticipated event on the local arts calendar, the Trail invites visitors to step inside studios and exhibition spaces, meet the artists behind the work, and experience creativity in a uniquely personal way.

2026 promises to be our biggest and most engaging Arts Trail yet, connecting artists with a wider audience while supporting the important work of Alzheimers Marlborough.

NOTE: Arts Trail brochures must be collected in person...details below.




Gala Evening

Saturday 12 September 2026

6.00pm - 8.30pm
Hosted by Oak & Ivy, 42 Alfred Street, Blenheim

Join us for a special Gala Opening Evening to launch the Arts Trail in style.

Enjoy a relaxed and vibrant evening featuring canapés and Hunters Wines, alongside an inspiring talk from guest speaker Michael Hurst.

With a career spanning more than 30 years, Michael Hurst is one of New Zealand’s most respected actors. Alongside Jennifer Ward-Lealand, he recently starred in the acclaimed production of In Other Words, a powerful and moving story exploring the impact of Alzheimer’s.

A natural storyteller and engaging speaker, Michael will share insights and stories from his remarkable career in the arts.

The evening will also feature both a live auction, raising funds to support the important work of Alzheimer’s Marlborough.

A wonderful evening of conversation, creativity and community.

Tickets:

$55 per person




Alzheimers Arts Trail

Saturday 19 & Sunday 20 September 2026
10:00am – 4:00pm daily
Locations: Across Marlborough (multiple studios and galleries)

A self drive event over two days, the Arts Trail opens the doors to artists across the region, offering a unique behind-the-scenes look at Marlborough’s creative talent.

What to expect:

Open studios and gallery spaces
Meet-the-artist experiences
A wide variety of art styles and mediums
Opportunities to purchase original artwork

Visitors will receive a full Arts Trail programme with trail map, allowing you to plan your own route and discover Marlborough’s vibrant creative community.

Tickets:

$25 Early Bird Ticket per person
$30 General Ticket per person (from 1 August)




Arts Trail brochures to be collected in person from:

Wine + Food Experience, 42 Alfred Street, Bleheim

Wednesday 16th, Thursday 17th, Friday 18th September, 4.00pm - 6.30pm

Saturday19th & Sunday 20th September, 10.00am - 12.00pm

Silent Art Auction




In the lead-up to the Arts Trail, browse and bid on an outstanding collection of donated artworks in the Silent Art Auction.

The exhibition will be on display at The Wine + Food Experience, 42 Alfred Street, Blenheim, from mid-August, with proceeds helping support the important work of Alzheimers Marlborough.

For more information vistit our website: Art Trail 2026 - Marlborough and follow us on Facebook or Instagram as we introduce our artists and reveal our generous sponsors and supporters.

Overview

An inspiring gala with curated art and experiences, raising funds for support services and family violence prevention in our community.

One Night. One Cause. Lasting Impact.
Join us for an inspiring evening of connection and purpose; all in support of building a safer, stronger community for wāhine and whānau.


The Women’s Support Motueka Gala is a special fundraising event dedicated to strengthening our prevention work alongside our essential support services. Every day, we walk alongside women and whānau navigating the impacts of family violence. At the same time, we are deeply committed to creating change before harm occurs; through education, community awareness, and early intervention.

Enjoy a beautiful evening featuring the auction of a range of experiences and curated art, with contributions from generous businesses and talented local artists that reflect the richness and spirit of our region.

All funds raised will support Women’s Support Motueka to continue providing free, confidential services; including advocacy, counselling, and support for healing, while also growing our prevention efforts such as education workshops, and our youth outreach campaign focused on building healthy relationships from an early age.

This is more than a night out. It is an opportunity to stand alongside our community, and to be part of creating lasting change.

Pioneers of the iconic Madchester sound, the 𝐇𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐲 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬 are heading back to Australia and New Zealand to celebrate the 35th anniversary of their seminal album, 𝑃𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 '𝑛' 𝑇ℎ𝑟𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝐵𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑦𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑒𝑠.

Fusing funk, rock, psychedelia, and house with the pulsating energy of the UK’s burgeoning rave scene, the 𝐇𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐲 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬 became the face of a cultural revolution. Their 1990 release, 𝑃𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 '𝑛' 𝑇ℎ𝑟𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑠 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝐵𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑦𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑒𝑠, catapulted them into the mainstream, spending over six months on the UK Albums Chart and earning its place as one of the defining records of the decade.

Fronted by the inimitable 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐮𝐧 𝐑𝐲𝐝𝐞𝐫, with 𝐁𝐞𝐳 ( freaky dancing and percussion), 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤 𝐃𝐚𝐲 (guitar), 𝐆𝐚𝐫𝐲 𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐧 (drums), 𝐌𝐢𝐤𝐞𝐲 𝐒𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞 (bass) 𝐃𝐚𝐧 𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐝 (musical director/guitar/keys), and 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐳𝐞𝐡 𝐁𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐲 (backing vocals), the band will perform highlights from the classic album; including anthems like 𝑆𝑡𝑒𝑝 𝑂𝑛, 𝐾𝑖𝑛𝑘𝑦 𝐴𝑓𝑟𝑜, and 𝐿𝑜𝑜𝑠𝑒 𝐹𝑖𝑡, alongside fan favourites such as 24 𝐻𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑃𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑦 𝑃𝑒𝑜𝑝𝑙𝑒, 𝐻𝑎𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑙𝑢𝑗𝑎ℎ, 𝐽𝑢𝑑𝑔𝑒 𝐹𝑢𝑑𝑔𝑒, and 𝑊.𝐹.𝐿.

Their enduring influence on British music was formally recognised in 2016 when they received the prestigious 𝐈𝐯𝐨𝐫 𝐍𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐨 𝐈𝐧𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐀𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐝, a testament to their legacy as one of the UK’s most beloved and groundbreaking bands.

‘Always a great buzz when we play Australia and New Zealand . Looking forward to bringing the Happy Mondays Pills ‘n’ Thrills party there in September’’ - 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐮𝐧 𝐑𝐲𝐝𝐞𝐫

This isn’t just a tour, it’s a full-throttle revival of Madchester chaos, and the year's wildest party is coming.

‘’Funky dancing, maraca shaking, and incredible vocal performances Happy Mondays showed why they were so big in the 90s and have been able to keep that special place in the hearts of the fans for so long.’’ – 𝐌𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐜 𝐍𝐞𝐰𝐬 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐡𝐥𝐲

‘’With Bez and Ryder’s between song banter raising the amusement stakes, the promised Hallelujah was given an airing and its iconic sounds had the crowd bouncing and swaying, it was clear that the Monday’s have lost none of their magic. They are still funky, downright vulgar but so endearing.’’ – 𝐔𝐊 𝐌𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐜 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐢𝐞𝐰𝐬

‘’The show was packed with anthems. Friday night's headline set from the Happy Mondays provided a wonderful dose of nostalgia from one of Manchester's most iconic outfits.’’ – 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐍𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐧 𝐄𝐜𝐡𝐨

events.name: Ōtari Glow Worm Tour
events.venue: Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush, 160 Wilton Road, Wilton, Wellington
events.long_description:
Take a guided night tour through Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush and discover some of the fascinating night-time residents on your way to see the titiwai/glowworms. Enjoy the tranquil beauty of the bush after dark and witness the magical glow of these unique creatures.

This outdoor night-time tour takes just over an hour.
The tour requires a moderate level of fitness; the route includes numerous steps and a steep incline to and from the glowworms.
No dogs, and not suitable for babies and young children.

Meet at the Ōtari Visitors Centre, 150 Wilton Road. Wrap up in warm clothes, wear sturdy walking shoes, and bring a torch or head lamp.

Glow Worm Tour Ticket Refund Policy:
• No Refunds: We do not offer refunds for Glow Worm Tour tickets.
• Ticket Transfers: If you can’t attend your booked tour, with 2 weeks notice we can put you on a future tour, subject to availability.
• Weather Conditions: Tours operate rain or shine. In the event of extreme weather or unsafe conditions, we will reschedule your tour or provide a refund.

For any changes or enquiries, please get in touch with us in advance at Treehouse@wcc.govt.nz or call 04 499 1400.

This tour is operated by the Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush Trust. Join the Trust from only $20 a year and the glow worm tour is free, plus you’ll be supporting the amazing work the Trust does. Join today at owbt.nz/membership-donations/

events.long_description:
Spring for Kaibosh - musical fundraiser
DJs, dancing and doing good.

Dress up, get down to Moon and boogie all night while helping Kaibosh feed those in our communities that need it most.

Don’t miss this fantastic fundraiser with stellar DJs spinning all night, lights and visuals from the legendary Cubeman and Metrokorg, and sweet sounds from Torque Sounds.

House, breaks, tech house, techno, rave, bass music and more, with good times guaranteed.

Raffle, plus spot prizes for the best dressed (costume theme: spring!).

All proceeds from ticket sales and raffle go straight to Kaibosh Food Rescue. If you can’t make it, you can donate or become a supporter via the Kaibosh website. https://kaibosh.org.nz/get-involved/donate/

Early bird special and reduced ticket price for the unwaged.
Get your tickets from Humanitix ( https://events.humanitix.com/spring-for-kaibosh)

Under 18s must be accompanied by their legal guardian.

DJs

Flatmate
Dance Therapy record label head Flatmate (aka your Flatmate) has a playful curiosity for music, a passion for storytelling and an infectious energy whether behind the decks, in the studio or on the dancefloor. He builds worlds rich in story and sonic diversity, capturing the warmth of the past while exploring the progressive endeavours of the present. (@flatmate__ and @dancetherapyrecords on Insta)

Nam Chucks b2B Amira
Nam and Amira possess a deep appreciation and respect for Soundsystem philosophy, dedicating their musical selections to the concepts of unity, inclusivity and respect for all sounds sacred and indigenous. Join these two empowered wāhine through sounds of their diaspora. (@nam_chucks on Insta)

Hexadecimal Emerging from the UK underground breakbeat scene in the early 2000s, Scott Reeder quickly established himself as an internationally respected DJ and producer. With 150+ releases to his name and two albums on Distinctive Records, his output has helped shape a generation of forward-thinking club music.
Now based in New Zealand, Hexadecimal remains highly active, delivering genre-blending, dancefloor-driven DJ sets that reflect both his deep roots and global perspective. (@hexadecimalmusic on Insta)

Ché D
Ngāmotu New Plymouth–based visual artist and musician/producer Ché Rogers, aka DJ Ché D, weaves stylish minimal house and techno tunes. Shaken, not stirred, he blends underground classics, originals, and live-improvised remixes with a serving of indie and goth condiments. (@che_rogers_art on Insta)

Lowli
Event co-organiser Laurie and his DJ sets are, in a word: FUN! He’s guaranteed to get carried away and bring anyone, and everyone, on the dancefloor with him. (@lowli_dj on Insta)

The Village Idiot
Longtime Kaibosh supporter, Lee Slater, has been hogging house-party stereos, and sound systems, for over 20 years. Expect flowing, bouncy tunes and a little bit of wonkiness.

DJ Danger
Ange has been dishing up tasty tunes around Pōneke for the past decade. Expect an eclectic, genre-bending collection of tunes in her vinyl-only set.

VJs & sound

Cubeman
VJ Cubeman is an established New Zealand visual artist and live media technician dedicated to turning sound into immersive light environments. Specialising in architectural projection mapping and live video manipulation, Cubeman captures and remixes real-world music moments into what he terms "the new".
If you’re not familiar with his ‘work’ prepare to have your minds blown! (@vjcubeman on Insta)

Metrokorg
A frequent partner-in-pixels, with Cubeman, Kane is a dedicated champion of the underground scene, actively supporting tech crews and behind-the-scenes production. His VJing, custom projection mapping and immersive mood lighting have helped craft hypnotic visual environments for major festivals and events including Bloom, CubaDupa, Sunny Side Up and numerous Kāpiti gigs. (@metrokorg on Insta)

We’re stoked that this epic event will be POWERED BY TORQUE – Pōneke’s brilliant, custom-built Tub’s Audio sound system. (@torque_sounds on Insta)

See you on the dancefloor…

Chekhov’s 130-year-old masterpiece gets a contemporary twist, set against a rural vineyard backdrop.

Sonny and his Uncle Vanya have spent years keeping the family estate running to support Sonny’s father, celebrated novelist Alex Serebryakov. When Alex returns with his much younger wife and announces plans to sell the vineyard, years of quiet sacrifice and buried resentment rise to the surface.

Overview

A workshop for creatives wanting to use social media for promotion without sacrificing their sanity and time.

Need to promote your work on social media but you’re getting lost in the algorithm or see it as a time waste?

Or maybe you’re not sure what to post to get attention for your creative business?

Maybe you don’t know where to start with all these new social media platforms springing up all over the place.

Or maybe you’re scared of negativity or saying the wrong thing.

Then this is the workshop for you.

With simple, actionable steps, you’ll be taken through how to be a creative on social media in a way that won’t feel like you’re over-exposed or selling your soul.

Attendees will leave this workshop with a working knowledge of how to have a presence on the big popular social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, X, Bluesky, Threads, Mastodon, Tiktok and Substack.)




For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

STRUNG OUT (USA) RETURN FOR FULL-BLOWN NZ TOUR —PERFORMING
SUBURBANTEENAGEWASTELANDBLUES IN FULL

Tickets Available now!
https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/.../33281/Strung-Out-USA.utr

Strung Out tore through NZ in 2023, and you lapped it up. You loved them, and they loved
you—so much so that they’re returning this September for a full-blown New Zealand tour, hitting
four locations across both the North and South Island.

And this time, they’re bringing something special.

To celebrate the 30th Anniversary of SUBURBANTEENAGEWASTELANDBLUES, Strung Out
will be playing the album in its entirety.

One of punk’s holy grails, it’s fast, ferocious, and
precise—a record that helped define the genre and influenced generations of bands that
followed.

Released in 1996, SUBURBANTEENAGEWASTELANDBLUES pushed the boundaries of the
genre—faster, sharper, and more intricate than anything that came before. Three decades on, it
still hits hard, and hearing it played live, front to back, is an experience no self-respecting punk
fan can miss.

Hailing from Simi Valley, California, Strung Out are long-standing punk rock royalty and one of
Fat Wreck Chords’ defining “big four.” With decades of touring under their belts, they have a
proven track record of igniting crowds and delivering high-octane, full-throttle punk shows.

Expect a night of relentless energy: razor-sharp riffs, pounding drums, and shout-along
choruses delivered with force.

This is controlled chaos at its best: sweat-soaked rooms, ringing
ears, and intensity that pulls you right in.

Last time Strung Out were here, shows sold out. This run will be no different.

Don’t sleep on it, or you’ll miss it.

Friday September 11th, 2026 — Last Place — Hamilton
Saturday September 12th, 2026 — Whammy Bar — Auckland
Sunday September 13th, 2026 — Valhalla — Wellington
Monday September 14th, 2026 — Loons — Christchurch

events.venue: Wellington Railway Station,Bunny Street, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The Daffodil Express
All aboard for one of Steam Incorporated’s most popular events of the year!

Join us on our annual Daffodil Express — a special heritage train journey to Carterton’s much‑loved Daffodil Festival in the heart of the Wairarapa.

Travel in vintage style behind our beautifully restored locomotives and carriages, with convenient boarding available at Wellington, Petone, Waterloo and Upper Hutt.

Sit back and enjoy the journey as we leave the city behind, race through the Hutt Valley suburbs, head through to the Wairarapa — including the famous 8.8km tunnel, one of the longest on New Zealand’s passenger network.

Once in Carterton, you’ll have time to explore everything the festival has to offer, including stunning daffodil fields at Middle Run Farm, bustling street markets and artisan stalls, live music and entertainment, food, crafts, and family-friendly fun.

After a relaxing few hours, simply hop back onboard for the return journey — no traffic, no parking hassles — just a great day out by rail.

🎟️ This excursion is extremely popular and sells out every year, so early booking is essential.

Make it a day to remember — gather your friends and family and experience this iconic Wairarapa tradition the best way possible: with Steam Incorporated.

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
"Ash rule. They are geniuses. Gods maybe."- NME
Ireland’s favourite power pop trio, Ash, finally return to Australia and New Zealand to Celebrate the 30th Anniversary of their iconic debut album, ‘1977’, by performing the album in full. Released in 1996, the album’s title references both the decade the band members were born in and the year Star Wars first hit cinemas.
‘1977’ has sold more than 2 million copies worldwide and was written, recorded and released when most of Ash were still only 19. A cinematic punk-pop soundtrack to binge drinking, chasing girls, youth and frustrated adolescent idealism, the album fused power pop, glam rock, post-grunge and Britpop into a loud, melodic and exuberant sound.
It struck a chord with the hearts, minds and hormones of a generation of like-minded teens, delivering a run of singles including “Girl From Mars”, “Kung Fu”, “Angel Interceptor”, “Goldfinger” and “Oh Yeah” — all of which reached the UK Top 20 and helped cement Ash’s reputation.
The 30th Anniversary Celebration of ‘1977’ will give Ash fans the chance to relive the album that featured “hit after honey-topped hit” and Britpop ruled the airwaves. Oh yeah!

San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

events.name: SHRED FEST - FEAT OBSCURA (GER), FVKVSHIMA & GUESTS, WELLINGTON
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Tickets here

SHRED FEST 2026 is coming! The renowned travelling metal festival will storm across New Zealand, delivering an unmatched celebration of technical excellence, intensity, and musical precision.

This year’s New Zealand edition features two of the most acclaimed names in modern extreme metal Obscura (GER) & Fvkvshima (NZ)

OBSCURA (GER) – Progressive death metal pioneers and masters of technical virtuosity. Following two successful Australian tours along with a return to New Zealand, OBSCURA is back to present their latest album A Sonication as part of their ongoing world tour.

Joining the international lineup are one of New Zealands most formidable local acts:

FVKVSHIMA - A progressive, driving, mechanical powerhouse surfacing from the shores of Wellington, NZ. Gargantuan, lurching drop-tuned phrases, layered with soaring apocalyptic textures. Resurrecting members from Shakahn, Backyard Burial, Planet of the Dead, and Diecast, FVKVSHIMA has collective decades of songwriting experience across a variety of genres, now condensed into its menacing live set.

Additional guests will appear in every city on this tour

Line Up
OBSCURA (GER)
FVKVSHIMA (NZ)
+ Special Guests

Dates
15/09 NZ Auckland – Whammy
16/09 NZ Wellington – Valhalla
17/09 NZ Christchurch – Churchills Tavern

SHRED FEST 2026 promises a diverse and uncompromising showcase of extreme metal — from technical precision to devastating heaviness. Expect the ultimate convergence of musicianship, passion, and power.

Tickets on sale via www.yourmatebookings.com & https://www.shredfest.net/

Obscura shared their thoughts on the upcoming tour:
"We're thrilled to bring Shred Fest to Australia in 2026 alongside the crushing talents of Fallujah, Anoxia, and Ashen. It’s been a long time coming, and we're ready to deliver a relentless set for our fans down under. No VIP packages — every band will be at the venue to meet you, talk music, and celebrate the most extreme sounds around. Come early, stay late, and support every act. We can’t wait to see you all there."

Official SHRED FEST channels;

Website: https://www.shredfest.net/
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61569365417641 / https://www.facebook.com/shredfestausnz / https://www.facebook.com/yourmatebookings
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/shredfest_moreisnotenough / https://www.instagram.com/shredfestausnz/
Tiktok: @shredfest_world
YouTube: youtube.com/@SHREDFEST_MOREISNOTENOUGH

All Interviews and Press Enquiries; please get in touch with Anthony ab@yourmatebookings.com

events.long_description:
Presented by: Bench Music and TEG Touring
Few figures have shaped the sound and spirit of house music like Timmy Regisford.
From New York's legendary WBLS radio station to executive A&R roles at Atlantic, MCA, Motown and DreamWorks Records, Regisford has spent more than four decades helping define dance music from both behind the scenes and behind the decks.
As founder and resident of the iconic Club Shelter, Timmy created one of dance music's most influential institutions - a sanctuary built on soulful house, disco, Afro rhythms, jazz, gospel and community that continues to inspire DJs and dancers around the world.
Known for marathon sets that unfold over many hours, Timmy's performances are journeys through rhythm, emotion and timeless music rather than peak-time moments. His influence stretches across generations, remaining just as essential to young selectors discovering the roots of house as it is to those who experienced New York's golden era firsthand.

O'Flynn | Wellington
WELLINGTON! O’Flynn makes his long-awaited New Zealand debut this September, arriving with a new album that captures him at a defining moment. 🌴

TICKET INFORMATION:
Pre-Sale Live: Wednesday 8th July, 10 am (NZT)
General On Sale: Thursday 9th July 10 am (NZT)

THESE TICKETS WILL GO FAST! GET IN EARLY, SIGN UP FOR PRE-SALE NOW.

Meow
Thursday 17th September | 8:00 pm - 12:00 am
Support from: Beccie B, Rydr

For over a decade, O’Flynn has quietly become one of the UK’s most respected producers and DJs, a singular voice in contemporary electronic music, grounded in dexterous production and an instinctive feel for the underground. His catalogue runs deep, shaped by curiosity, and marked by collaborations with artists such as Bonobo and Barry Can’t Swim.

Releasing music across Ninja Tune, Blip Discs, and his own imprint Hundred Flowers, O’Flynn’s work has earned support from tastemakers including Four Tet, Ben UFO, Gilles Peterson, and James Blake.

A pivotal moment came via Bonobo’s Fabric mix, which led to the collaborative track Otomo, a quietly monumental piece, and later saw O’Flynn join Bonobo on tour. Around the same time, he released Shimmer, a collaborative album with Frazer Ray via Ninja Tune’s Technicolour imprint, praised by DJ Mag as “a perfect cocktail of soaring emotions and bottom-heavy bass.”

Live, O’Flynn completed a five-week sold-out residency at London’s Phonox, followed by a sold-out headline show at KOKO, marking a clear step up in scale and demand.

In 2023, O’Flynn became a resident on Rinse FM, further cementing his role as both curator and craftsman. More recently, he delivered the inaugural release on Barry Can’t Swim’s Earth’s Only Paradise label, two tracks that stretched from disco-lit dancefloors to sharp-edged club pressure.

Now, O’Flynn returns with Kairos, his third full-length album, released July 17 via his own Panthus label. Named for the ancient Greek concept of the decisive moment, when conditions align, Kairos feels exactly that: a record where club energy meets patience, detail, and atmosphere. Music built for immersion.

This debut NZ tour marks the arrival of an artist fully in his stride, backed by an album rich in colour, tone, and intent.

The Bay Express to the Hastings Blossom Festival
Welcome spring in style and climb aboard The Bay Express for a magnificent full-day rail adventure. We are heading to Hawke's Bay for the spectacular Hastings Blossom Festival!

Sit back and relax as our majestic steam locomotive takes you through changing landscapes, winding its way toward the sunny Hawke's Bay. There is no better place to experience the sights and sounds of mainline steam than from our open-air viewing platform. It is the ultimate vantage point for taking stunning photos, hearing the thunderous echo of the engine, and catching the fresh spring breeze.

Throughout the entire journey, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. You can purchase a range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, hot espresso coffees, and sweet treats right from your seat as the scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight into the heart of the action. The train will be stopping right in the middle of Hastings, putting you directly in the center of the festival. Upon arrival, you'll step off the train and straight into the vibrant celebrations of the annual Hastings Blossom Festival. Enjoy a fantastic afternoon exploring the famous public parade, live entertainment, market stalls, and beautiful spring blooms. It’s a proud local tradition celebrating the region's rich orchard heritage, and you are perfectly positioned to enjoy it all at your leisure before our return journey home.

What's Included
Your ticket covers your return journey to Hastings in beautifully maintained premium carriages alongside unrestricted access to the open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography. You will also have full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling refreshments, espresso coffees, and snacks. Best of all, you get direct arrival right into the heart of Hastings for the Blossom Festival celebrations with plenty of time to enjoy the festival parade, markets, and entertainment.

Following the release of their recent single, “I Do Mine”, Debt Club announce their first Aotearoa nationwide tour. The tour will celebrate the release of their debut album “Foothold” which is out August 12th & available for vinyl pre-order now!

Debt Club are a Pōneke based indie / folk rock six piece who blend jangling indie rock, folk, alt-country and emo into a sound defined by rich arrangements, soaring saxophone melodies, and emotionally direct songwriting. Since forming in 2023, the band has quickly become a notable presence in Aotearoa’s underground music scene through their dynamic live performances and textured, heartfelt songs. Debt Club have shared stages with Marlin's Dreaming, Phoebe Rings and Australia’s Floodlights, while appearing at festivals including Rhythm and Vines, Twisted Frequency, CubaDupa and Newtown Festival. Following the release of their debut EP, “Taste For Stout,” the band recently unveiled “I Do Mine,” the first single from their forthcoming debut album “Foothold,” due out on August 12th.

Joining Debt Club for the Wellington date is First Reserve & Dillon Jo!

First Reserve is inevitable. Before adopting the moniker in 2023, Ryan Connaghan had been prolifically writing music that communicated their experiences in life, love, and loneliness. These themes are all approached on songs like “Last One” and “Me & My Friends” – the first offerings from First Reserve’s debut EP “There’s A God” set for release on November 14th, 2025. Thanks to their exhilarating live performances joined by a four-piece band, First Reserve has amassed a cult of devoted supporters both in their hometown of Te Whanganui-a-Tara and beyond. On stage, their sound is both intimate and larger-than-life, combining influences from alt-rock, indie-folk, and pop. First Reserve has supported visiting internationals Hot Mulligan (US) and Keli Holiday (AUS), and have toured with Kiwi favourites PARK RD, There’s A Tuesday, and Wet Denim.

Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s staple, Dillon Jo, is a queer, female-fronted four-piece band formed at Massey University in Wellington. Describing their sound as “Dreamy Droppy Rock Pop,”. ‘Dillon Jo’ is the project of Wellington Based artists Betty Smith and Georgie Levien, building paths between the elements of dream pop, shoegaze, folk, alt rock, and indie pop to create their genre defying sound. They have discovered vibrant chemistry over the past few months since making quite a stir in Wellington, playing numerous shows including opening for The Rions, Foley, Wet Denim, Hemi Hemingway and Coast Arcade only to name a few. Having heard of each other through the Reality music TV show Take The Mic 2022 which they were both contestants on, they formed Dillon Jo in early 2025. Releasing their first acoustic single ‘It was you (she’s been waiting for)’ in April 2025 and releasing two more singles later in the year, including ‘Shiver’ and ‘Jo’. The band also consists of Kahu Sanson-Burnett, (a multi-talented musician, producer, and previous member of Parallel Park) and Ruadh Munro, (Drums and previous member of Scarlett crush) Dillon Jo has transformed their live sets into an unbridled big-sound shoegaze experience

events.name: The Trinity Hill Vintage Escape
events.venue: Plimmerton Railway Station,Plimmerton, New Zealand, Porirua
events.long_description:
The Trinity Hill Vintage Escape
The Trinity Hill Vintage Escape 🍷

Welcome spring in style and step aboard The Trinity Hill Vintage Express for a magnificent, all-inclusive rail and epicurean adventure. We are heading to Hawke's Bay for an exclusive winery experience at one of New Zealand's most prestigious estates.

Sit back and indulge as our majestic steam locomotive sweeps you through changing landscapes, winding its way through the dramatic scenery of the Manawatū Gorge toward sunny Hawke's Bay. There is no better place to experience the romance and grandeur of mainline steam than from our open-air viewing platform. It is the ultimate vantage point for taking stunning photos, capturing the thunderous echo of the engine, and taking in the fresh spring breeze.

Throughout the entire journey, our onboard licensed café carriage will be at your service. You can purchase a range of premium alcoholic and non-alcoholic refreshments, fresh hot coffees, teas, and sweet treats to enjoy right from your seat as the scenery rolls elegantly by.

Our tracks lead straight to Hastings, where a private coach awaits to escort you directly to the legendary Trinity Hill Vineyard in the globally acclaimed Gimblett Gravels district.

This exclusive afternoon centers completely around celebrated viticulture:
- Behind the Cellar Door: Go on an insider's tour to discover their world-class winemaking craft and rich heritage.
- Curated Artisan Lunch: Unwind on the stunning estate grounds with a premium lunch box featuring your choice of a hand-crafted sandwich (such as the bold Beef and Kraut with pickles and cheese, an elegant Chicken and Tarragon, or a vibrant Salad and Hummus with salsa verde).
- Perfect Pairings: Accompanied by a savory scone, sweet slice, and fresh fruit, your estate lunch is paired perfectly with a complimentary glass of Trinity Hill's flagship Hawke's Bay Collection Wine.

Your ticket covers your return rail travel behind a genuine steam locomotive from Kapiti, Horowhenua, or Manawatū, complete with reserved premium carriage seating offering panoramic views. You will have full access to our open-air viewing platform for unbeatable sightseeing and photography, alongside entry to our fully licensed café carriage throughout the rail journey. Seamless coach transfers will also be waiting in Hastings to transition you smoothly from rails to vines.

Once at Trinity Hill, you will enjoy an exclusive winery tour exploring Trinity Hill’s history and winemaking craft. To complement the afternoon, you will receive a curated estate lunch box featuring a premium sandwich, savory scone, sweet slice, and fresh fruit, paired perfectly with a complimentary glass of Trinity Hill's premium Hawke's Bay Collection Wine (or a non-alcoholic alternative).

Approximate Itinerary
Morning – Northbound to Hastings
Plimmerton depart – 5:25am
Paraparaumu depart – 5:55am
Ōtaki depart – 6:30am
Levin depart – 7:00am
Palmerston North depart – 8:10am
Woodville depart – 8:55am
Hastings arrive – 11:55am

On arrival into Hastings, passengers transfer by coach to Trinity Hill Vineyard.

Afternoon/Evening – Return Journey
Hastings depart – 4:00pm
Woodville depart – 6:50pm
Palmerston North depart – 7:50pm
Levin depart – 8:45pm
Ōtaki depart – 9:15pm
Paraparaumu depart – 9:45pm
Plimmerton arrive – 10:15pm

Tickets are strictly limited! Space in these premium carriages is restricted to preserve the intimate nature of this estate experience. Secure your tickets today for an exceptional spring day out on the rails!

events.long_description:
Kaiwhakaataata Māra | Garden Performers
SPRING’S SPRITES

Celebrating this 35th year, Shakespeare Globe Centre New Zealand is delighted to bring some of Shakespeare’s most sprightly characters to life to help re-enliven the Wellington City Council’s Botanic Garden ki Paekākā, as it springs back into life after wintering over.

On Sunday 20 September, for an hour or so from 10am and again from 1pm, Pucks, fairies, friends and the odd Bottom will caress your ears with familiar quips and quotes from the Bard’s canon, as you hover to behold the rebirth of plants erupting into bloom.
For half an hour from 11.30am and 2.30pm, the characters combine at the Joy Fountain by the Glenmore Street entrance to present ‘exploded’ versions of their quotes into vignettes of his favourite plays. If you wish to participate, there will be a few roles with cue-scripts available to join the revels and explore the beauty of Shakespeare’s words and magic midst the fresh flowers springing forth.

But wait, there’s….a costume competition, with prizes, for the best Bottom and Puck, presented at the end of the performance. Fun for all!

Dare to Lead™ | Wellington | 23-25 September 2026
Dare to Lead is the ultimate starting point for brave leaders, courageous cultures, and organisational change.

About this Event


The ultimate starting point for brave leaders, courageous cultures and organisational change.


"Highly recommend."
"Inspiring."
"An amazing experience."
"One 'aha moment' after the other."

Founded on the research of Dr. Brené Brown, Dare to Lead™ is an empirically based courage-building programme, delivered by Boma New Zealand CEO and Certified Dare to Lead™ Facilitator Kaila Colbin.
Brené has spent two decades studying shame and more than seven years specifically looking at leadership. During her research, she interviewed leaders from all over the world — from Fortune 100 companies, non-profits, public sector entities, and more — and asked one question: what is the future of leadership?
Remarkably, their answers pointed to one thing: we need braver leaders.


We need more courage.

The most significant finding from Brené’s latest research, and the foundation of Dare to Lead™, is that courage is a collection of four skill sets that are teachable, measurable, and observable.


After completing the three-day Dare to Lead™ programme you'll understand how to:
Effectively navigate vulnerability and unlock change
Turn values from fluffy language into tangible, practical behaviours
Build a common culture of trust in your team
Cultivate the skills to rise from setbacks and be more resilient


This curriculum is essential for teams who want to:
Be better equipped to deal with difficult conversations
Reduce unhealthy and unproductive behaviour
Be more creative and innovative
Build resilience and improve alignment
Foster a culture of accountability and trust


This experience is for you if:
You're in a position of leadership within your organisation
You see the potential in people and processes, and are willing to take responsibility for achieving that potential
You’re passionate about accelerating performance in yourself and others
You have to navigate organisational change as part of your role



Need help with the cost?
If you are an Educator or at a Not-for-Profit, you can automatically access a special price of $1,995 + GST when you register.
We also have partial scholarships available to attend the programme. Apply here and we’ll be in touch.
Boma is a Regional Business Network Provider. Your organisation may be eligible for funding support to attend this programme. Find out more at regionalbusinesspartners.co.nz


Our Health and Safety Plan
Boma is committed to delivering safe events. We follow best practices suggested by the New Zealand health authorities and work closely with our suppliers to prioritise health and wellbeing.
Our comprehensive health and safety plans ensure you can book with certainty and attend with confidence.



Our refund policy
For details on event refunds and transfers, please see our refund policy.


Contact us
Please email with any questions.

events.name: KITA / LOVE LIVES HERE: 愛住在這裡
events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
Melding inspirations of folk, soul, pop and psychedelia with the guitar and spirited storytelling of musician-actor Nikita 雅涵 Tu-Bryant (Avatar 2, Far North); the thick  lushness of Moog synth and Fender Rhodes from Ed Zuccollo (aka Zuke); and the filthy  drive and barking drums of Rick Cranson (Little Bushman), KITA have long-since  solidified themselves as a must-see live band with a massive sound.
Front-woman Nikita 雅涵 Tu-Bryant is amidst her Artist in Residence at The Hannah Theatre in Wellington, translating her debut art-house film "LOVE LIVES HERE 愛住在這裡" for stage. The narrative originally inspired by the band's EP LOVE LIVES HERE which they toured nationwide in 2023. Tu-Bryant is debuting the film into a full immersive cinema-live-theatrical experience with a chorus of dancers and live band for her residency at the end of this year. In the meantime, she revives the live-in-concert version of this vulnerable ambitious work-in-progress. Excerpts from the film will be remixed live by Elfling. This show was showcased at Twisted Frequency, and now powerhouse trio KITA bring it back to the capital playing one of their favourite venues in Pōneke. 

Support act to be revealed beginning of September

San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

VAMPIRE DISKO: THE DEBUT 

Advance tickets at: https://buytickets.at/12xuproductions/2269600

For one evening only, Wellington descends into darkness as "vampyres" (don't worry, vampires aren't real...or are they?), goths, and nocturnal misfits gather on the dance floor for the city's first ever VAMPIRE DISKO

Wellington's newest night of Goth, Post-Punk, EBM, Dark Synth Pop, Post Punk, Industrial and Wave for creatures of the night who enjoy getting dressed as vampires, or at least being around people that do!

We invite you to arrive dressed for the eternal night inspired by cult classic vampire films such as Interview with the Vampire, Queen of the Damned, The Lost Boys, The Hunger, Nosferatu and sooo many more... The more dramatic your look, the better! Victorian, Modern, or Halloween Vampire- your efforts will not go unnoticed!

MUSIC IS DECIDEDLY DARK: Expect DJs playing a large amount of 80s classic goth like Bauhaus, Sisters of Mercy, Siouxsie and the Banshees, Christian Death, Clan of Xymox, Skinny Puppy, Nitzer Ebb, Front 242, classic dark 80s like Depeche Mode, Soft Cell, The Cure, Echo and the Bunnymen and New Order and many cutting edge brand new artists who lean toward the dark side. Think She Past Away, Boy Harsher, Riki, Kontravoid, Lebanon Hanover, Nox Novacula, H.Ä.L.T., The Frozen Autumn, Patriarchy....

And for those of who you want a taste of 90s-10s, we won't completely shy away, but you simply MUST request a song in the Facebook event if you really have your heart set on something.

Soundtracking the night: DJ Matai, Nightmare + Coffin Nail spinning until the early hours. We DO of course plan to have you in bed before SUNLIGHT HITS!

This is a LGBTQIA+ friendly event where self-expression is encouraged and the dance floor belongs to everyone.

events.name: Mental Health First Aid Aotearoa
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Mental Health First Aid Aotearoa
NZ Citizens and residents pay $219 with ID.  f you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $499 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register..
Mental Health First Aid is an evidence-based workshop which gives people the skills and confidence to have supportive conversations with their whānau, co-workers and community and help guide them to professional help if needed.
You will learn to recognise common mental health challenges, how to provide initial help to someone experiencing a mental health challenge using a practical, evidence-based action plan, and how to respond in a crisis situation. During the workshop you will have the opportunity to practice new skills in a safe environment.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
Mental health challenges covered in the course include:
Depression
Anxiety
Psychosis
Substance use problems
Mental Health Crisis Covered:
Suicidal thoughts and behaviours
Non- Suicidal self-injury
Panic attack
Traumatic events
Severe effects from Alcohol or other substance use
Aggressive behaviours
People who attend Mental Health First Aid training can complete a short online assessment to be accredited as a Mental Health First Aider. You must attend the full two days to be able to do the online assessment for accreditation. The accreditation is valid for three years.
If you choose not to be accredited, you will receive a certificate of participation if you attend the full course. You will also receive a workbook as part of your course fee.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Biker Breakfast
Bikers Breakfast is on again this year.
Closer to the date will advise details of a ride, but RAC wgtn will also have a stand there to share what we are about.
Open to some people to be available to help on the stand.

Other details of the Bikers Breakfast are:-
"We are organising our second annual Bikers Breakfast on Saturday 26 September from 8:30 am – 12:30 pm. This motorcycle safety event will be held in collaboration with Kapiti Coast District Council and Southwards Car Museum. Last year the Ulysses Club participated, and this year we would like to have a few more clubs in attendance, if possible.
Ride Forever course providers will be attending to speak with motorcyclists about the merits of learning to ride safely by signing up for ACC’s Ride Forever courses. The Motorcycle Collective will be setting up a safety gear Op Shop with a range of motorcycle apparel and equipment, and we will be giving away hot drinks and bacon butties.
A blind zone demonstration will show how easily a motorcycle can be invisible to large trucks – riders can sit in the cab of the truck and see if they can spot the bikes. There will be a helmet cleaning station and free rider safety packages that include important safety items like screen cleaners and re-usable hand warmers."

Sacred Rewilding Forest circle 🎶 W ❤️ Shared picnic

What to Expect: Sacred Women's Circle


🌸Welcome, Sister. If you are feeling a pull in your heart to join us, that calling is your initiation.
Trust where you are being led. The circle lives within each of us.
Sacred Women's Circles have been used for thousands of years to build supportive communities, encourage authentic self-expression, and remind us that we are never alone on our journeys.

This is a dedicated, women-only gathering to honor our womb energy and embrace our sacred sisterhood.
Together, we step into a safe container to lower our walls, let our facades drop, and form real, authentic relationships rooted in vulnerability and trust.

✨ Meet Your Host: Crystal Mihinui
Your space is held by Crystal Mihinui, a dedicated practitioner with over 40 years of profound experience in music, frequency, and energy work. Crystal weaves her extensive background into every circle to create a deeply safe, transformative container for your healing. Her unique medicine includes:
Reiki Master: Channeling universal life force energy to restore balance and harmony to your body, mind, and spirit.

Music Therapist & Classically Trained Pianist: Using a lifetime of technical mastery and a deep understanding of musical psychology to shift emotional blocks and soothe the nervous system.
Sound Healing Practitioner: Blending acoustic frequencies to guide you into profound states of meditation, relaxation, and inner awakening.

🌿 The Journey & Flow
Gathering at our beautiful, secret forest spot surrounded by native trees, birds, and mountains, our flow includes
Sacred Circle & Oracle Cards: Opening our space with Archangel cards, inviting in nature spirits, and honoring our ancestors.
Womb Healing: Activating our deep feminine intuition using womb mudras and sacred mantras.
Shamanic Sound Journey: A deeply restorative guided meditation powered by crystal singing bowls and energy healing from the realm of the Fae.
Sisterhood Sharing: Returning to the circle to softly share our experiences, stories, and wisdom.
Ritual Releasing what no longer serves us by offering our written words to the sacred forest.

Forest Bathing & Journaling: Immersion in the healing frequencies of nature.📍

Location & Meeting Points
We have two meeting point options, both provided upon booking.
You can choose to:
Meet at our cozy home-based studio to rideshare together
Or meet directly at our beautiful outdoor location in Rivendell.☔

Rain Plan: If the wild weather joins us, we will move to our beautiful indoor alternative (details provided upon booking).🎒

What to Bring
A shared vegetarian dish to enjoy together during our gathering
A journal and pen for your reflections
Comfortable clothing suitable for the forest.
Swimming gear (if you would like to take a dip! 🏖).🎟

Investment & Inclusivity Children's Tickets: Children are very welcome to join our sacred space and are half price.
Community Services Card: Concession tickets are gladly available; please bring your proof of entitlement on arrival

Cancellation Policy: As a small, heart-led family business, our time is precious. Tickets are non-refundable, but you are deeply welcome to gift your ticket to another sister if you cannot make it.

Producers Night Market
✨ Producers Night Market – Kāpiti & Horowhenua ✨

Following the fantastic feedback from our February Producers Market and growing demand for a night-time experience, we’re excited to be partnering once again with the Ōtaki and Te Horo Business Association to bring you the Producers Night Market!

This relaxed, family-friendly evening market will showcase the very best of our region, fresh local produce, plants, flowers, and healthcare products, with a strong focus on supporting local growers, makers, and small businesses across Kāpiti and Horowhenua.

🌿 What to expect
- Beautiful twilight setting under the trees with festive lighting
- Live local musicians
- Seating areas to relax and enjoy the atmosphere
- A curated selection of food trucks in the car park
- A vibrant community vibe celebrating local talent and produce

👉 Find out more / register: www.otakiwomensclub.org/producers-market

💡 Please note: Stallholders will need to provide their own lighting for their stall spaces. At this time of year there will still be good natural light early in the evening.

💰 Stall fees
$20 for a 3m x 3m site
$40 for a 3m x 6m site

📅 Dates
Thursday 1 October 2026 | 4:30pm – 8:30pm
Thursday 28 January 2027 | 4:30pm – 8:30pm
Thursday 1 April 2027 | 4:30pm – 8:30pm
(If postponement is required, the event will move to the following Thursday.)

📍 Proudly supported by the Ōtaki Women’s Community Club and the Ōtaki & Te Horo Business Association.


Producers can sell:
- Fresh fruit and vegetables, eggs, olives, seasonal produce.
- Crackers, breads, cakes, biscuits and pastries.
- Coffee, tea, small batch jams, chutneys and honey.
- Wine, cider, beer, spirits, Liqueurs.
- Juice or other non alcoholic beverages.
- Olive oil, sauces, chocolates, sweets.
- Ice Cream, cream, milk, cheese and dairy products.
- Herbal tonics and food-based wellness blends.
- Healthcare products locally made, natural body products.
- Flowers, trees, plants and seeds.

events.long_description:
Four Last Songs - Wellington
One of the world’s most acclaimed conductors, Sir Donald Runnicles, returns to the NZSO in a programme of pure luxury and ravishing beauty.

Programme:
R Strauss Rosenkavalier Suite
R Strauss Four Last Songs
Brahms Symphony No. 3

The sensuous, glittering raptures of the Rosenkavalier Suite evoke the decadence of 18th century Vienna in a dazzling array of complex waltzes.

Then delve deeper into Richard Strauss’ most personal, revealing and achingly beautiful music with his sublime Four Last Songs. These profound songs, performed by silver-voiced soprano Madeleine Pierard, sumptuously evoke a sunset portrait of a wife well loved and a life well lived.

We balance this decadence with the crystalline Symphony No. 3 from Johannes Brahms. In music that plays between light and shadow, the work takes on as its organising motto frei aber froh — free but happy.

Sir Donald Runnicles appears with generous support from Dame Bronwen Holdsworth DNZM.

events.name: Trip: Belmont Regional Park at Dry Creek Entrance
events.venue: Hebden Cres,Dry Creek Campsite, Haywards, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
Trip: Belmont Regional Park at Dry Creek Entrance
We will climb for 40 minutes up the 4WD Buchanans Road Tramping Track, passing Dendrobium cunninghamii, Earina autumnalis, Helichrysum lanceolatum and Metrosideros colensoi.

From there we’ll walk bait lines and informal unformed tracks for a 90-minute circuit of Syzygium maire (maire tawake, swamp maire). Botanising time will be additional to this. Bring good footwear and gaiters if you have them for waterlogged sites. There is one place with hip-stretching tall steps cut into soil. Areas can be slippery when wet. Hand ropes are beside steep mud steps. This is a 7.5km walk with moving time of around two and a half hours.

There is recent research on Syzygium maire in the Wellington region, published by the School of Biological Sciences at Victoria University. The authors highlight that we ‘need to identify refugia in accessible, albeit sometimes fragmented, habitat’ and recommend ‘leveraging human–nature interactions in areas to create, expand, and protect habitat for [this] rare species in a rapidly changing world’. Syzygium maire has a threat classification of Threatened-Nationally Vulnerable. The research illustrates the preferred habitat of Syzygium maire is waterlogged areas. Such areas are few and shrinking, both nationally and in Wellington region.

This trip will look at thriving Syzygium maire that have fruited and seeded in the rare wetlands below Boulder Hill. We’ll see Ramarama, Threatened – Nationally Critical, and Coprosma rubra, At Risk – Declining and over 100 other plant species observed on iNaturalist. These can be seen in a map view of the proposed quarry Overburden Disposal Area.

Ominously there’s a Fast-track proposal to turn this precious area into a quarry overburden disposal area. This has been reported on by Radio NZ. The Friends of Belmont Regional Park and Wellington Botanical Society have strongly opposed this. The Fast-track application is here.

Non-members are welcome to join, making it an excellent opportunity to explore this region’s native flora.

Meet: Dry Creek Carpark, Hebden Crescent, Kelson, Lower Hutt at 9.30am. This Carpark with toilets is a 10-minute walk from Manor Park Station on the Hutt Valley Line. Trains leave Wellington at 8.35am and arrive at Manor Park Station at 9.08am.

Leader: John Barnett, 021 063 1590,

This tour will also be the first place in the world where we do a tour celebrating the release of our brand new record Season of Surrender. We hope to see you all soon!” - August Burns Red
Crafting their signature brand of metalcore for over two decades, AUGUST BURNS RED have ferociously established themselves as one of the foremost acts in the genre. Hailing from Lancaster, Pennsylvania, the band's milestones and legacy spans everything from multiple top 10 placements on the Billboard Top 200 and tours with everyone from Bullet For My Valentine through to A Day To Remember and countless more. Also with two GRAMMY Award nominations in their wake, nominated for Best Metal Performance in 2016 for Identity and again in 2018 for Invisible Enemy, AUGUST BURNS RED have never rested on their laurels or stopped pushing the limits of their sound; a fact that has loudly carried into 2026 with the upcoming release of a their tenth studio album Season Of Surrender due out on June 5 via Fearless Records. 
On a live front, AUGUST BURNS RED's reputation is as formidable as their creative output, renowned for their visceral performances across the globe, most recently stupefying Australian crowds in 2023 supporting Polaris nationally on the Fatalism Tour. Praised by Scenestr for delivering "a raging masterclass in pure American metalcore with a 20-year, career-spanning set list that resonated spectacularly" of the Adelaide show supporting Polaris, X-Press Magazine also declared of the band's 2023 Perth performance on the same run that ABR demonstrated "why they have cemented themselves as one of the most respected names in the scene." 
One of Australia's most prolific rising heavy acts, BLOOM wield an open-veined take on melodic hardcore that has seen them tour the globe, release two full-length albums and cultivate an army of dedicated fans along the way. Emerging in 2017, BLOOM released their 2024 debut full-length, Maybe In Another Life, before swiftly turning their gaze to their 2025 sophomore album, The Light We Chase. Wowing with their multi-faceted and matured collection of songs on album #2, also expanding their creative reach further than ever before, BLOOM kicked off 2026 with their biggest headline performances to date, touring Australia nationally to celebrate The Light We Chase. Whether sharing stages with the likes of Silverstein and Thornhill or enamouring as headliners, you can definitely count on one thing when it comes to a BLOOM live show: it is seriously not to be missed.

The up and coming folk-rock sensation, Mountain Boy and band bring their legendary live show to Auckland for their biggest tour ever to celebrate the release of the new album The Nights. 
This will be their first time headlining at San Fran and their first performance there in more than 6 years - when they opened for The Paper Kites in 2019. It is sure to be a full circle moment. 
"The Nights is the second album from Mountain Boy, and a continuation of their debut The Days. Where the first record was shaped by solitude, The Nights was made in the company of close friends — a shift that’s felt throughout the music. events.id: Cornelia Parker-City Gallery Wellington-Wellington NZ
events.name: Cornelia Parker
events.venue: City Gallery Wellington
events.long_description:
After three years of closure, the newly renovated and strengthened City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi will host the art of Cornelia Parker. The British visual artist is best known for her innovative and contemporary sculpture and installation art. Her large-scale, immersive installations explore themes of destruction and reconstruction, transformation and metamorphosis. Objects are exploded, crushed, and suspended in a world upended and remade anew.
Curated by independent UK-based curator Andrea Schlieker and City Gallery Wellington’s Senior Curator Aaron Lister, City Gallery Wellington’s exhibition will encompass Parker’s long career as an artist. This includes an immersive sound-and-light installation, ‘Stolen Thunder’. The work gathers the sounds of approaching storms from around the globe and across time. The exhibition will also showcase her paintings, photos, films, and sculptures.
“I have always said this is the one exhibition I want to do before I die,” said Charlotte Davy, Ringatohu Toi Director, Art and City Gallery Wellington. “I have been following Cornelia Parker’s work for the last twenty years. Bringing her mischievous, dark, and literally explosive work to Wellington is incredible.” 
Parker’s work often fills entire rooms and invites the viewer to move through and around the art. Given its physical scale, the blank canvas of the reopened gallery offers the perfect opportunity to host the exhibition. The exhibition will kick off in October 2026 and run through March 2027. 
Charlotte notes the exhibition’s themes are also of particular relevance to Wellington. “I hope that the exhibition and our return to Te Ngākau Civic Square will reflect our city and also help remake it. We are looking forward to opening with a bang.”
Hero image: © Cornelia Parker. Courtesy of the artist and Frith Street Gallery, London

Their debut album Fresh Out Of Air debuted at #2 on the Official NZ Music Charts, while their first national headline tour sold out across the country, including a 450-capacity show at The Tuning Fork. Their single “Perfect Crime” has surpassed 2 million streams, and they’ve shared stages with The Mountain Goats, headlined Warehouse Party and Summer Select, and played the main stage at Soundsplash.
Now, with three new singles released, Where’s Jai embark on a 10-date Australia and New Zealand headline tour this September.

San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

events.name: Che Fu & The Kratez
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Che Fu is on a national tour celebrating 25 years since breakthrough album, 'Navigator'. He'll bring his blend of soul, reggae, hip hop, rock, and Pacific influences to the Michael Fowler Centre. He'll be joined on stage by longstanding band The Kratez as well as soul artist Aaradhna, vocalist Betty-Anne, and hip hop artist King Kapisi.
Che Fu appeared on the NZ music scene with funk rockers Supergroove while still in high school. After around five years, he went solo and released hit song 'Chains' in 1996. You might recognise his other chart-topping songs ‘Fade Away’ and ‘Misty Frequencies’ on the 'Navigator' album.
The Niuean/Māori musician became a pioneer of hip-hop and Pasifika music. He was recently inducted into the NZ Music Hall of Fame. He's earned a Pacific Music Awards Lifetime Achievement Award. He's also a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit.

events.name: Effective Business Analysis
events.venue: Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBD,Level 5, 111 The Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Effective Business Analysis
Defining change with clarity and agility. Discover how to apply the core skills and techniques of elicitation, analysis, and communication.

About this Event


Description
The business world is demanding faster change, the ability to adapt and solutions that are fit for purpose. As a business analyst, you're counted on for your skills as a conceptual and practical thinker, a relationship builder, and a translator. You're relied upon to identify and describe the change required to address business issues. Sometimes there are problems that require a fix, opportunities that need to be realised or situations where the business simply doesn't know but is prepared to "give it a go" and experiment to gain insights to what it should do next.
In this course, you'll be introduced to a series of context aware, business-focussed approaches that you can apply to:
Work with stakeholders to uncover the business issue that needs to be addressed
Define the change required within its context
Prioritise and scope the requirements based on business value and
Specify requirements clearly to those delivering the solution
Designed and delivered by our Equinox IT team of practicing business analysts, this course covers how to structure your analysis activities based on the context and the issue at hand to describe requirements that fully represent the change required.




Outline
Day 1
Overview and concepts
What is business analysis?
Requirements analysis framework

Discover – understanding context
Understanding a business domain
Adjusting to different types of initiative
Stakeholders – identification, classification and engaging
Techniques (root cause analysis, 5 whys, diverge, converge, etc.)
The discovery canvas

Focus topic: Elicitation –gathering information and understanding
Purpose and context
Selecting the right technique (interviews, workshops, research, observation, brainstorming, etc.)
Planning a session
Running a session
Post session activities
Main exercise - role play

Day 2
Define – understanding the change required
Introduction to capabilities
Information and data – concept/domain Modelling
Business process – tips on modelling
Business rules – their relationship with other business concepts
Scenarios – use cases
Change strategy map
Change aspect map
Defining user and other stories

Scope – understanding priority and value
Helping the business to assess value
Techniques
User story maps

Day 3
Focus topic: Workshop Facilitation–gaining consensus
Being self-aware
Facilitation
Preparation
Group dynamics
Handling various situations
Main exercise - role play

Deliver – packaging for delivery
Backlog refinement
Developing good acceptance criteria
Understanding various types of solution requirements and contributing elements

Focus topic: Communication – telling the story
A brief overview of the difference between specification and communication




Learning outcomes
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to;
Analyse and understand the kind of business issue that needs to be addressed
Engage stakeholders and analyse their business needs
Define a change strategy
Define the aspects of change required
Understand various business models e.g. business process, information, business rules
Define a user story and associated requirements
Use effective techniques to elicit requirements
Understand how to plan and facilitate a requirements workshop
Understand scoping based on business value
Analyse, document and review solutions and detailed requirements
Define acceptance criteria
Understand how to communicate with a variety of audiences




Accreditation and certification
This course aligns with the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge v3.0®.




Audience
The primary audience for this course is business analysts, systems analysts and enterprise analysts of all experience levels. The course will also be of value to any project team members involved in requirements definition activities.




Prerequisites
There are no prerequisites for this course, however, some experience in business analysis will help.

English in the Community courses help you to learn more English, get to know your community and meet new people. The groups aim to help you use what you already know, learn more from your tutor and the other students and feel more at home in your local community. 
To enrol in these courses, please contact the CEC office on 04 385 8919 or cec@whs.school.nz.
By the end of the course, you'll: 
• Be more confident in speaking English in everyday situations
• Be able to understand more English, especially “New Zealand English”
• Have increased your vocabulary
• Be able to talk more about living in New Zealand and your local community
The courses are free for NZ residents and citizens. The course fee for non-residents is $155.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Assertiveness - Stand Up for Yourself
(NZ Citizens and residents pay $79 with ID, all others pay $149).

Come prepared to participate in class, as well as be working on assigned activities between classes. We'll work both individually and as a group using this environment to help us grow as we learn.

events.long_description:
For those who have completed our French Intermediate 3 course or equivalent (approx 110 hours of French learning).  The course will focus on developing conversation skills.
For people who already know the basics vocabulary and grammar points and want to improve their conversational and fluency skills.  
Expected course outcomes:
1. revisit language structures, grammar and vocabulary previously studied
2. discuss new topics such as media, environment, work, education (students are encouraged to suggest topics of general interest)
3. explore new grammar points (the pluperfect, present and past conditional, "if" clause, the subjunctive)
4. continue working on pronunciation and development of conversational skills.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.id: Sewing - All Levels-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: Sewing - All Levels
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Sewing - All Levels
All levels welcome! Beginning sewers will learn basic skills and techniques and those with some experience will improve their skills and learn tips and tricks.
Beginners - If you're a beginner, you'll start by making a lined bag, which teaches all the basic skills involved. After that you'll move on to a project of your choice, in consultation with the tutor.  Please bring: 1 metre of firm cotton fabric for your bag outer and 1 metre of a lighter cotton fabric for the lining. You'll also need to bring scissors, a Bernina bobbin (this can be purchased from the CEC office on the day of the course for $7), pins, thread to match your outer fabric, an 18 cm zip and tape measure to the first session.
 If you're a returning student, or have already mastered the basic skills, you'll work on your own project so please bring along whatever you're currently working on (or something new) and your sewing kit. 
Please note PDF patterns are not suitable for this course unless you are very experienced in using them;  we strongly recommend patterns from the following companies:  Simplicity, Butterick, New Look or Quicksew.
By the end of the course, you'll have been introduced to basic skills in dressmaking, if beginners, or further skills for the more experienced.
You'll be able to:
• Use all sewing machine equipment and demonstrate basic sewing techniques (basic seams and finishes)
• Begin to read a commercial pattern and select appropriate materials for task
• Cut out and construct a garment using techniques learned
• (In addition), use a variety of advanced sewing techniques e.g. rolled hems, various zip insertions (invisible and standard), make buttonholes or line garments. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Japanese - Introductory 2
(NZ Citizens and residents pay $105 with ID, all others pay $205).
For those who have done Introductory 1 (16 hours) or have equivalent knowledge (e.g. who may have picked up some basic survival language through travel).
